<s>Veṇīsaṃhāram</s> (The Binding of the Braid) /
ACT 1
First Act /
VERSE 1.1
Though repelled, these bees have ravished the nectar; like the moon whose interior is stirred, its buds burst open—

children.text: vidhattāṃ siddhiṃ no nayanasubhagāmasya sadasaḥ ē̃ prakīrṇaḥ puṣpāṇāṃ haricaraṇayorañjalirayam // 1.1 //
children.translated_text: May this offering of flowers at the feet of <s>Hari</s>, scattered before this assembly that delights the eyes, grant us success. // 1.1 //
VERSE 1.2

children.text: kālindyāḥ pulineṣu kelikupitāmutsṛjya rāse rasaṃ $ gacchantīmanugacchato 'śrukaluṣāṃ kaṃsadviṣo rādhikām &
children.translated_text: Having left behind in the sport on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) the playfully angered <s>Rādhikā</s>, who abandoned the pleasure of the <s>rāsa</s> dance, and following her as she departed, her eyes clouded with tears, the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s>—
May the entreaty of him whose feet were placed in the footprints of hers, whose hair stood on end with emotion, and who was blessed by the glance of his appeased beloved, nourish you. // 1.2 //
And furthermore,
VERSE 1.3

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ saprema devyā kimidamiti bhayātsaṃbhramāccāsurībhiḥ $ śāntāntastattvasāraiḥ sakaruṇamṛṣibhirviṣṇunā sasmitena &
children.translated_text: Beheld with love by the Goddess, with bewilderment and fear by the <s>Asura</s> women asking 'What is this?', with compassion by the sages whose inner nature knows the essence of truth, with a smile by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: ākṛṣyāstraṃ sagarvairupaśamitavadhūsaṃbhramairdaityavīraiḥ ē̃ sānandaṃ devatābhirmayapuradahane dhūrjaṭiḥ pātu yuṣmān // 1.3 //
children.translated_text: With pride by the <s>Daitya</s> heroes who calmed the alarm of their wives by withdrawing their weapons, and with joy by the gods—may <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva), at the burning of <s>Mayapura</s> (Tripura), protect you. // 1.3 //
And furthermore,
[End of the <s>Nāndī</s> benediction]
VERSE 1.4
He who composed the nectar called the <s>Bhārata</s>, fit to be drunk through the cupped palms of the ears—
To that <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s> (Vyāsa), dark like a rain cloud, I pay homage. // 1.4 //

<s>Sūtradhāra</s> (Stage Director):
Enough of this digression!
VERSE 1.5
This poetic composition is offered here like another handful of flowers;
Like bees partaking of even scattered drops of honey, please appreciate whatever small merits it may have. // 1.5 //

[Looking around]
Now, O distinguished leaders of the assembly, we have something to announce.

children.text: tadidaṃ kavermṛgarājalakṣmaṇo bhaṭṭanārāyaṇasya kṛtiṃ veṇīsaṃhāraṃ nāma nāṭakaṃ prayoktumudyatā vayam / tadatra kavipariśramānurodhādvodāttakathāvastugauravādvā navanāṭakadarśanakutūhalādvā bhavadbhiravadhānaṃ dīyamānamabhyarthaye /
children.translated_text: And so, we are prepared to present the drama called <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, the work of <s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>, who bears the mark of a lion among poets. Therefore, I request your attention here, whether out of regard for the poet's labor, or out of respect for the gravity of the noble story's subject matter, or out of curiosity to witness a new drama.
[Behind the curtain]

children.text: bhāva tvaryatāṃ tvaryatām / ete khalvāryavidurājñayā puruṣāḥ sakalameva śailūṣajanaṃ vyāharanti / pravartyantāmaparihīyamānamātodyavinyāsādikā vidhayaḥ / praveśakālaḥ kila tatrabhavataḥ pārāśaryanāradatumburujāmadagnyaprabhṛtibhirmunivṛndārakairanugamyamānasya bharatakulahitakāmyayā svayaṃ pratipannadautyasya devakīsūnoścakrapāṇermahārājaduryodhanaśibiraṃ prati prasthātukāmasyeti /
children.translated_text: Sir, make haste, make haste! By the command of the noble <s>Vidura</s>, men are summoning the entire company of actors. Let the musical arrangements and other preparations proceed without interruption. For the time of entrance has come, it is said, for the son of <s>Devakī</s>, the wielder of the discus, who has undertaken the embassy himself for the welfare of the <s>Bharata</s> clan, accompanied by hosts of sages led by <s>Pārāśarya</s> (Vyāsa), <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Tumburu</s>, <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (Paraśurāma) and others, and who is about to set forth toward the camp of the great king <s>Duryodhana</s>.

children.text:
&sūtradhāraḥ&:
*ākarṇya sānandam**
aho nu khalu bho bhagavatā jagatprabhavasthitinirodhaprabhaviṣṇunā viṣṇunādyānugṛhītamidaṃ bharatakulaṃ sakalaṃ ca rājakamanayoḥ kurupāṇḍavarājaputrayorāhavakalpāntānalapraśamahetunā svayaṃ saṃdhikāriṇā kaṃsāriṇā dūtena / tatkimiti pāripārśvika nārambhayasi kuśīlavaiḥ saha saṃgītakam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sūtradhāra</s> (Stage Director):
[Listening with delight]
Ah, truly! The Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is the source of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe, has today bestowed his grace upon us, the most lowly of his servants!
[Entering]

<s>Pāripārśvika</s> (Assistant):
Very well. Let me begin. In what mode shall we sing?

children.text:
&sūtradhāraḥ&:
nanvamumeva tāvaccandrātapanakṣatrakrauñcahaṃsakulasaptacchadakumudapuṇḍarīkakāśakusumaparāgadhavalitagaganadiṅmaṇḍalaṃ svādujalajalāśayaṃ śaratsamayamāśritya pravartyatāṃ saṃgītakam / tathā hyasyāṃ śaradi

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.6
Of noble wing, sweet of voice, having adorned every direction, intoxicated and bold in their onset—
The sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> fall to the surface of the earth by the power of fate. // 1.6 //

<s>Sūtradhāra</s> (Stage Director):
Why, in this very mode—the autumn, whose sky is whitened by the pollen of moonlight, stars, <s>krauñca</s> birds, <s>haṃsa</s> geese, <s>saptacchada</s> blossoms, <s>kumuda</s> water-lilies, <s>puṇḍarīka</s> lotuses, and <s>kāśa</s> grass flowers.

<s>Pāripārśvika</s> (Assistant):
[With alarm]
Sir! May evil be averted! May ill omen be repelled!

children.text:
&sūtradhāraḥ&:
*savailakṣyasmitam**
māriṣa śaratsamayavarṇanāśaṃsayā haṃsā dhārtarāṣṭrā iti vyapadiśyante / tatkiṃ śāntaṃ pāpaṃ pratihatamamaṅgalam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sūtradhāra</s> (Stage Director):
[With an embarrassed smile]
Good sir, the <s>haṃsa</s> geese are called '<s>dhārtarāṣṭra</s>' in the context of describing the autumn season. So why this talk of averting evil?

children.text:
&pāripārśvikaḥ&:
na khalu na jāne / kiṃ tvamaṅgalāśaṃsayāsya vo vacanasya yatsatyaṃ kampitamiva me hṛdayam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Pāripārśvika</s> (Assistant):
Indeed, I know that well enough. But at the mere suggestion of ill omen in your words, truly my heart trembled.

children.text:
&sūtradhāraḥ&:
māriṣa nanu sarvamevedānīṃ pratihatamamaṅgalaṃ svayaṃ pratipannadautyena saṃdhikāriṇā kaṃsāriṇā / tathā hi

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.7

children.text: nirvāṇavairadahanāḥ praśamādarīṇāṃ $ nandantu pāṇḍutanayāḥ saha mādhavena &
children.translated_text: May the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, their fires of enmity extinguished, whose wealth is tranquility, rejoice together with <s>Mādhava</s> (Kṛṣṇa);

children.text: raktaprasādhitabhuvaḥ kṣatavigrahāśca ē̃ svasthā bhavantu kururājatanayāḥ sabhṛtyāḥ // 1.7 //
children.translated_text: And may the sons of the <s>Kuru</s> king, whose lands are adorned with blood, their conflicts ended, be at peace with their retainers. // 1.7 //

<s>Sūtradhāra</s> (Stage Director):
Good sir, surely everything inauspicious is now averted by the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> (Kṛṣṇa), who has himself undertaken the embassy of peace. For indeed—
[Behind the curtain, with contempt]
VERSE 1.8

children.text: lākṣāgṛhānalaviṣānnasabhāpraveśaiḥ $ prāṇeṣu vittanicayeṣu ca naḥ prahṛtya &
children.translated_text: Through the house of lac, through poison in food, through the assembly-hall entry—having struck at our very lives and wealth,

children.text: ākṛṣṭapāṇḍavavadhūparidhānakeśāḥ ē̃ svasthā bhavanti mayi jīvati dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ // 1.8 //
children.translated_text: And having dragged the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> bride by her garment and hair—do the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> remain at ease while I yet live? // 1.8 //
Ha! You wicked one! You vain reciter of auspicious prayers! You disgrace to the actor's profession!
Juncture of the plot / type: <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction)
[The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> and <s>Pāripārśvika</s> listen]

<s>Pāripārśvika</s> (Assistant):
Sir, whence comes this?

children.text:
&sūtradhāraḥ&:
*pṛṣṭhato vilokya**
aye eṣa khalu vāsudevagamanātkurusaṃdhānamamṛṣyamāṇaḥ pṛthulalāṭataṭaghaṭitavikaṭakīnāśatoraṇatriśūlāyamānabhīṣaṇabhrukuṭirāpibanniva naḥ sarvāndṛṣṭipātena sahadevānugamyamānaḥ kruddho bhīmasena ita evābhivartate / tanna yuktamasya purataḥ sthātum / tadita āvāmanyatra gacchāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sūtradhāra</s> (Stage Director):
[Looking behind]
Ah! This is indeed he who cannot tolerate the peace-making with the <s>Kurus</s> occasioned by the visit of <s>Vāsudeva</s> (Kṛṣṇa)—with his brow furrowed and fierce, displaying a grim scowl upon his broad forehead—
[Both exit]
End of the Prologue.
[Then enters <s>Bhīmasena</s>, angry, followed by <s>Sahadeva</s>]

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Ha! You wicked one! You vain reciter of auspicious prayers! You disgrace to the actor's profession! [Repeats: 'Through the house of lac...' etc.]

children.text:
&sahadevaḥ&:
*sānunayam**
ārya marṣaya marṣaya / anumatameva no bharataputrasyāsya vacanam / nirvāṇavairadahanā iti yathārthameva / sabhṛtyāḥ kuravaḥ kṣatajālaṃkṛtavasuṃdharāḥ kṣataśarīrāśca svargasthā bhavantviti bravīti /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sahadeva</s>:
[Conciliatorily]
Brother, forbear, forbear! The words of the son of <s>Bharata</s> (Yudhiṣṭhira) are approved by us too. 'May the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, their fires of enmity extinguished'—just as was said.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*sopālambham**
na khalu na khalvamaṅgalāni cintayitumarhanti bhavantaḥ kauravāṇām / saṃdheyāste bhrātaro yuṣmākam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[With reproach]
Surely, surely you ought not to contemplate inauspicious things for the <s>Kauravas</s>! Are they to be reconciled, those brothers who—
VERSE 1.9
The sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, who have waged enmity at every step—

children.text: rājā na cenniṣeddhā syātkaḥ kṣameta tavānujaḥ // 1.9 //
children.translated_text: Were the king not to restrain them, who among your younger brothers would endure it? // 1.9 //

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
[With anger]
Brother—

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
evamidam / ata evāhamadyaprabhṛti bhinno bhavadbhyaḥ / paśya /

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.10

children.text: pravṛddhaṃ yadvairaṃ mama khalu śiśoreva kurubhi- $ rna tatrāryo heturna bhavati kirīṭī na ca yuvām &
children.translated_text: This enmity that has grown since my very childhood with the <s>Kurus</s>—the noble one (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) is not its cause, nor <s>Kirīṭī</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), nor you two—

children.text: jarāsaṃdhasyoraḥsthalamiva virūḍhaṃ punarapi ē̃ krudhā saṃdhiṃ bhīmo vighaṭayati yūyaṃ ghaṭayata // 1.10 //
children.translated_text: Like the breast of <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s> rejoined, <s>Bhīma</s> in fury tears apart the peace that you all strive to forge. // 1.10 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Exactly so! And that is precisely why, from this day forth, I am separated from all of you. Behold!
Juncture of the plot / type: <s>parikara</s> (development)

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
[Conciliatorily]
Brother, when you are all so greatly inflamed with anger, our elder (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) is sometimes distressed.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
kiṃ nāma khidyate guruḥ / guruḥ khedamapi jānāti / paśya /

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.11

children.text: tathābhūtāṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpasadasi pāñcālatanayāṃ $ vane vyādhaiḥ sārdhaṃ suciramuṣitaṃ valkaladharaiḥ &
children.translated_text: Having seen the daughter of <s>Pāñcāla</s> in that state in the assembly of kings, having dwelt long in the forest with hunters wearing bark garments,

children.text: virāṭasyāvāse sthitamanucitārambhanibhṛtaṃ ē̃ guruḥ khedaṃ khinne mayi bhajati nādyāpi kuruṣu // 1.11 //
children.translated_text: Having resided in the house of <s>Virāṭa</s>, engaged in menial tasks—yet the elder feels distress not at the <s>Kurus</s>, even now, but only when I am aggrieved. // 1.11 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
What do you mean, the elder is distressed? Does the elder even know what distress is? Look!

children.text: tatsahadeva nivartasva / evaṃ cāticirapravṛddhāmarṣoddīptasya bhīmasya vacanādvijñāpaya rājānam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Sahadeva</s>, return. And from the words of <s>Bhīma</s>, whose wrath has blazed long unchecked, convey this message to the king.

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, what shall I say?
VERSE 1.12

children.text: yuṣmacchāsanalaṅghanāṃhasi mayā magnena nāma sthitaṃ $ prāptā nāma vigarhaṇā sthitimatāṃ madhye 'nujānāmapi &
children.translated_text: I have endured, sunk in the sin of transgressing your commands; I have borne the reproach among steadfast men, even among my own younger brothers—

children.text: krodhollāsitaśoṇitāruṇagadasyocchindataḥ kauravā- ē̃ nadyaikaṃ divasaṃ mamāsi na gururnāhaṃ vidheyastava // 1.12 //
children.translated_text: But when I, with mace reddened by the blood stirred by my fury, am annihilating the <s>Kauravas</s>—for that one day, you are not my elder, nor am I your obedient servant. // 1.12 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Convey this message:
[He strides about defiantly]

children.text:
&sahadevaḥ&:
*tamevānugacchannātmagatam**
aye kathamāryaḥ pāñcālyāścatuḥśālaṃ praviṣṭaḥ / bhavatu tāvadahamatraiva tiṣṭhāmi* /iti sthitaḥ**
children.translated_text:
<s>Sahadeva</s>:
[Following him, aside]
Ah, how has the brother entered the courtyard of <s>Pāñcālī</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>)! Well then, let me wait here.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*pratinivṛtyāvalokya ca**
sahadeva gaccha tvaṃ gurumanuvartasva / ahamapyāyudhāgāraṃ praviśyāyudhasahāyo bhavāmi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Turning back and looking]
<s>Sahadeva</s>, go, attend upon the elder. I too shall enter the armory and, with weapons as my companions, shall—

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, this is not the armory—this is the courtyard of <s>Pāñcālī</s>!

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*savitarkam**
kiṃ nāma nedamāyudhāgāraṃ pāñcālyāścatuḥśālamidam* /kiṃcidvihasya saharṣam**
āmantrayitavyā mayā pāñcālī* /sapraṇayaṃ sahadevaṃ haste gṛhītvā**
vatsa āgamyatām / yadāryaḥ kurubhiḥ saṃdhānamicchannasmānpīḍayati tadbhavānapi paśyatu /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Reflectively]
What? This is not the armory but the courtyard of <s>Pāñcālī</s>? [Laughing a little, with delight]
Then she must be greeted!
[Both mime entering]

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, here is a seat prepared. Please sit here and await the arrival of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>).

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*upaviśya**
vatsa kṛṣṇāgamanamityanenopodghātena smṛtam / atha bhagavānkṛṣṇaḥ kena paṇena saṃdhiṃ kartuṃ suyodhanaṃ prati prahitaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Sitting down]
Child, by this prelude of 'awaiting <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s arrival,' I am reminded—on what terms has the blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> gone to make peace?

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, for five villages.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*karṇau pidhāya**
ahaha hanta devasyājātaśatrorapyayamīdṛśastejopakarṣa iti yatsatyaṃ kampitamiva me hṛdayam* /parivṛtya sthitvā**
tadvatsa na tvayā kathitaṃ na mayā śrutam /

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.13
That mighty and most fierce <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior's) splendor of this king—
While gambling with dice, surely even that he has squandered away. // 1.13 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Covering his ears]
Alas, alas! That even the godly <s>Ajātaśatru</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) should suffer such a diminishment of glory—truly, my heart trembles at the thought!
[Behind the curtain]
(Prakrit) Be consoled, be consoled, my lady!
(Sanskrit rendering) Be consoled, be consoled, my lady!
VERSE 1.14
That lightning-like brilliance gathered today in the angered noble one—
This <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>), like the rainy season, will surely intensify it. // 1.14 //

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
[Looking toward the curtain, aside]
Ah! How is it that <s>Yājñasenī</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>), her eyes veiled by ever-swelling floods of tears, approaches the presence of the noble brother—

children.text: *tataḥ praviśati yathānirdiṣṭā draupadī ceṭī ca / draupadī sāsraṃ niśvasiti**
children.translated_text: [Then enters <s>Draupadī</s> as described, along with a maid-servant. <s>Draupadī</s> sighs tearfully.]

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_2}samassasadu samassasadu bhaṭṭiṇī / abaṇaissadi de maṇṇuṃ ṇiccāṇubaddhakuruvelo kumālo bhīmaseṇo /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) Be consoled, be consoled, my lady! Prince <s>Bhīmasena</s>, who is ever bound to enmity with the <s>Kurus</s>, will remove your anger.

children.text: SktCh_2: samāśvasitu samāśvasitu bhaṭṭinī / apaneṣyati te manyuṃ nityānubaddhakuruvairaḥ kumāro bhīmasenaḥ /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) Be consoled, be consoled, my lady! Prince <s>Bhīmasena</s>, who is ever bound to enmity with the <s>Kurus</s>, will remove your anger.

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_3}hañje buddhimadie hodi edaṃ jai mahārāassa paḍiulo huvissadi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) Dear clever one, that would be so only if he will act against the wishes of the great king (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>).

children.text: SktCh_3: hañje buddhimatike bhavatyetadyadi mahārājasya pratikūlo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) Dear clever one, that would be so only if he will act against the wishes of the great king.

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_4}*vilokya**
eso kumālo ciṭṭhadi / tā ṇaṃ ubasappadu bhaṭṭiṇī /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) [Looking] Here stands the prince. Let my lady approach him.
(Sanskrit rendering) Here stands the prince. Let my lady approach him.

<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) Dear one, let us do so.
(Sanskrit rendering) Dear one, let us do so.
[They walk about the stage]

Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) [Approaching] Victory, victory to the prince!
(Sanskrit rendering) Victory, victory to the prince!

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Not hearing, repeats again: 'That mighty and most fierce...' etc.]

Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) [Turning aside] My lady, the prince appears to be enraged.

children.text: SktCh_7: bhaṭṭini parikupita iva kumāraḥ lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) My lady, the prince appears to be enraged.

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_8}hañje jai evvaṃ tā avahīraṇā bi esā maṃ assāsaadi / tā ettha ubaviṭṭhā bhavia suṇomi dāva ṇāhassa vavasidaṃ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) Dear one, if that is so, even this disregard consoles me. So let me sit here and listen to what my lord has resolved.

children.text: SktCh_8: hañje yadyevaṃ tadavadhīraṇāpyeṣā māmāśvāsayati / tadatropaviṣṭā bhūtvā śṛṇomi tāvannāthasya vyavasitam /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) Dear one, if that is so, even this disregard consoles me. So let me sit here and listen to what my lord has resolved.
[Both do so]
VERSE 1.15

children.text: mathnāmi kauravaśataṃ samare na kopā- $ dduḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ na pibāmyurastaḥ &
children.translated_text: Shall I not churn the hundred <s>Kauravas</s> in battle? Shall I not drink the blood from the breast of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> in my fury?

children.text: saṃcūrṇayāmi gadayā na suyodhanorū ē̃ saṃdhiṃ karotu bhavatāṃ nṛpatiḥ paṇena // 1.15 //
children.translated_text: Shall I not crush the thighs of <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) with my mace? Let your king make peace on whatever terms he pleases! // 1.15 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Angrily, addressing <s>Sahadeva</s>]
What do you mean, peace for five villages?

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_9}*saharṣaṃ janāntikam**
ṇāha assudapuvvaṃ khu de īdisaṃ vaaṇaṃ / tā puṇo bi dāva bhaṇāhi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) [With delight, aside] My lord! Never before have I heard such words from you! Pray, say it again!

children.text: SktCh_9: nātha aśrutapūrvaṃ khalu ta īdṛśaṃ vacanam / tatpunarapi tāvadbhaṇa /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) My lord! Never before have I heard such words from you! Pray, say it again!

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Not hearing, repeats again: 'Shall I not churn...' etc.]

children.text:
&sahadevaḥ&:
ārya kiṃ mahārājasya saṃdeśo 'vyutpanna iva gṛhītaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, has the message of the great king been received as if by one unlearned?

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
What learning is there to be had in this?

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, this is what the elder has directed.

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Whose elder?

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
<s>Suyodhana</s>'s (<s>Duryodhana</s>'s).

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
What about it?
VERSE 1.16
<s>Indraprastha</s>, <s>Vṛkaprastha</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Vāraṇāvata</s>—
Give these four villages, and some one other as the fifth. // 1.16 //
<s>Sahadeva</s>:

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
And then what?

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Then, by this request naming village after village and the omission of the fifth, the disposition of hostility through the poisoned food, the house of lac, the gambling assembly, and other offenses has been revealed—

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*sāṭopam**
vatsa evaṃ kṛte kiṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[With vehemence]
Child, what is accomplished by doing this?

children.text:
&sahadevaḥ&:
ārya evaṃ kṛte loke tāvatsvagotrakṣayāśaṅki hṛdayamāviṣkṛtaṃ bhavati kururājasyāsaṃdheyatā ca darśitā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, by doing this, the heart that fears the destruction of its own lineage is at least revealed to the world, and the impossibility of peace with the <s>Kuru</s> king is demonstrated.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
sarvamapyetadanarthakam / kururājasya tāvadasaṃdheyatā tadaiva niveditā yadaivāsmābhirito vanaṃ gacchadbhiḥ sarvaireva kurukulasya nidhanaṃ pratijñātam / loke 'pi ca dhārtarāṣṭrakulakṣayaḥ kiṃ lajjākaro bhavatām / api ca re mūrkha

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.17
The destruction of the enemy's clan in anger would shame you in the eyes of the world,
But the dragging of our wife by her hair in the assembly does not shame you! // 1.17 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
All this is futile! The impossibility of peace with the <s>Kuru</s> king was already declared at the very moment when we, departing for the forest—

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_10}*janāntikam**
ṇāha ṇa lajjanti ede / tumaṃ bi dāva mā visumarehi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) [Aside] My lord, they feel no shame. But you at least, pray do not forget!

children.text: SktCh_10: nātha na lajjanta ete / tvamapi tāvanmā vismārṣīḥ /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) My lord, they feel no shame. But you at least, pray do not forget!

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Reminiscing]
Child, why does <s>Pāñcālī</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>) delay?

children.text:
&sahadevaḥ&:
ārya kā khalu velā tatrabhavatyāḥ prāptāyāḥ / kiṃ tu roṣāveśavaśādāgatāpyāryeṇa nopalakṣitā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, what time is it since the lady arrived? Indeed, she came but was not noticed by you, overcome as you were by the force of your rage.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*dṛṣṭvā sādarām**
devi samuddhatāmarṣairasmābhirāgatāpi bhavatī nopalakṣitā / ato na manyuṃ kartumarhasi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Seeing her, with respect]
O queen, in our surging anger we failed to notice your arrival. Therefore, do not take offense.

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_11}ṇāha udāsīṇesu tumhesu maṇṇū ṇa uṇa kubidesu /
children.translated_text:
<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) My lord, my anger is when you are indifferent, not when you are enraged.

children.text: SktCh_11: nātha udāsīneṣu yuṣmāsu manyurna punaḥ kupiteṣu /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) My lord, my anger is when you are indifferent, not when you are enraged.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
yadyevamapagataparībhavamātmānaṃ samarthayasva* /hastaṃ gṛhītvā pārśve samupaveśya mukhamavalokya**
kiṃ punaratrabhavatīmudvignāmivopalakṣayāmi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
If that is so, then consider yourself free from humiliation. [Taking her hand, seating her beside him, looking at her face] But what—

<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) My lord, what cause for distress when you are present?
(Sanskrit rendering) My lord, what cause for distress when you are present?
VERSE 1.18
While the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> yet live, and are not far away—
That the daughter of the <s>Pāñcāla</s> king should bear this condition! // 1.18 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Why do you not tell me? [Looking at her hair] Or rather, what need is there to be told—

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_13}hañje buddhimadie ṇivedehi dāva ṇāhassa / ko aṇṇo maha parihaveṇa khijjadi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) Dear clever one, tell my lord. Who else is pained by my humiliation?

children.text: SktCh_13: hañje buddhimatike nivedaya tāvannāthasya / ko 'nyo mama parībhavena khidyate /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) Dear clever one, report to my lord. Who else is pained by my humiliation?

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_14}jaṃ devī āṇavedi* /bhīmamupasṛtyāñjaliṃ baddhvā**
kumāla ido bi ahiaṃ ajja maṇṇukālaṇaṃ āsī devīe /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) As the queen commands. [Approaching <s>Bhīma</s> with folded hands] Prince, today there was an even greater cause for the queen's anger.
(Sanskrit rendering) As the queen commands. Prince, today there was an even greater cause for the queen's anger.
VERSE 1.19
In this forest fire of the <s>Kauravya</s> lineage, who is it that plays the moth?
By touching this <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>) with her unbound braid, as if she were a column of smoke! // 1.19 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
What? Something even greater than this? Then tell me, tell me!

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_15}suṇādu kumālo / ajja khu devī ambāsahidā subhaddappamuheṇa sabattivaggeṇa parivudā ajjāe gandhālīe pādavandaṇaṃ kāduṃ gadā āsī /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) Let the prince hear. Today the queen, accompanied by her mother-in-law and surrounded by her co-wives led by <s>Subhadrā</s>, went to pay respects at the feet of the elder lady <s>Gāndhārī</s>—

children.text: SktCh_15: śṛṇotu kamāraḥ / adya khalu devyambāsahitā subhadrāpramukheṇa sapatnīvargeṇa parivṛtāryāyā gāndhāryāḥ pādavandanaṃ kartuṃ gatāsīt /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) Let the prince hear. Today the queen, accompanied by her mother-in-law and surrounded by her co-wives led by <s>Subhadrā</s>, went to pay respects at the feet of the elder lady <s>Gāndhārī</s>—

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
That is proper. Elders should indeed be honored. Then what? Go on.

Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) Then, while returning, she was seen by <s>Bhānumatī</s>.
(Sanskrit rendering) Then, while returning, she was seen by <s>Bhānumatī</s>.

children.text:
&bhīmasanaḥ&:
*sakrodham**
āḥ śatrorbhāryayā dṛṣṭā / hanta sthānaṃ krodhasya devyāḥ / tatastataḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[With anger]
Ha! Seen by the wife of the enemy! Indeed, there is cause for the queen's fury! Then what? Go on.

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_17}tado tāe deviṃ pekkhia sahīvaaṇadiṇṇadiṭṭhīe sagavvaṃ īsi vihasia bhaṇidaṃ /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) Then she, looking at the queen and casting a glance directed by her companion, laughed slightly with pride and said—

children.text: SktCh_17: tatastayā devīṃ prekṣya sakhīvadanadattadṛṣṭyā sagarvamīṣadvihasya bhaṇitam /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) Then she, looking at the queen and casting a glance directed by her companion, laughed slightly with pride and said—

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
na kevalaṃ dṛṣṭoktā ca / aho kiṃ kurmaḥ / tatastataḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Not only seen but spoken to as well! Alas, what can we do? Then what? Go on.

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_18}ai jaṇṇaseṇi pañca gāmā patthīanti tti suṇīadi / kīsa dāṇiṃ bi de kesā ṇa saṃjamīanti /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) 'O <s>Yājñasenī</s>! It is heard that five villages are being sought. Why then are your tresses still not bound up?'

children.text: SktCh_18: ayi yājñaseni pañcagrāmāḥ prārthyanta iti śrūyate / kasmādidānīmapi te keśā na saṃyamyante /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) 'O <s>Yājñasenī</s>! It is heard that five villages are being sought. Why then are your tresses still not bound up even now?'

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
<s>Sahadeva</s>, did you hear that?
VERSE 1.20
For the minds of women become like those of their husbands through companionship;
Even a sweet creeper becomes poisonous when it clings to a venomous tree. // 1.20 //

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
What can one say? She is the wife of <s>Duryodhana</s>, after all. Consider—

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Clever one, then what did the queen say?

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_19}kumāla jai parijaṇahīṇā bhave tado devī bhaṇādi /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) Prince, the queen says this only if she is without attendants.

children.text: SktCh_19: kumāra yadi parijanahīnā bhavettadā devī bhaṇati /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) Prince, the queen would speak thus only if she were without attendants.

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
What then did you say?

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_20}mae evvaṃ bhaṇidaṃ / ai bhāṇumadi tumhāṇaṃ amukkesu kesesu kahaṃ amhāṇaṃ devīe kesā saṃjamīanti tti /
children.translated_text:
Maid-servant:
(Prakrit) I said this: 'O <s>Bhānumatī</s>, while your people's hair remains unloosed, how can our queen's tresses be bound up?'

children.text: SktCh_20: mayā evaṃ bhaṇitam / ayi bhānumati yuṣmākamamukteṣu keśeṣu kathamasmākaṃ devyāḥ keśāḥ saṃyamyanta iti /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) I said this: 'O <s>Bhānumatī</s>, while your people's hair remains unloosed, how can our queen's tresses be bound up?'

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*saparitoṣam**
sādhu buddhimatike sādhu / tadabhihitaṃ yadasmatparijanocitam* /svābharaṇāni buddhimatikāyai prayacchati**
atrabhavati pāñcālarājatanaye śrūyatām / acireṇaiva kālena

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.21
By the furious blows of his fierce mace whirled by his swinging arms, when <s>Suyodhana</s>'s (<s>Duryodhana</s>'s) pair of thighs are crushed to powder,

children.text: styānāvanaddhaghanaśoṇitaśoṇapāṇi- ē̃ ruttaṃsayiṣyati kacāṃstava devi bhīmaḥ // 1.21 //
children.translated_text: With hands reddened by thick, clotted blood, <s>Bhīma</s> shall braid your tresses, O queen! // 1.21 //

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[With satisfaction]
Well said, clever one, well said! That reply was worthy of a servant of ours. [Gives his own ornaments to the clever maid as a reward]
Juncture of the plot / type: <s>parinyāsa</s> (conclusion)

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_21}kiṃ ṇāha dukkaraṃ tue parikubideṇa /
 aṇugeṇhantu edaṃ vavasidaṃ de bhādaro /
children.translated_text:
<s>Draupadī</s>:
(Prakrit) My lord, what is impossible for you when you are enraged?
May your brothers approve this resolve of yours!

children.text: SktCh_21: kiṃ nātha duṣkaraṃ tvayā parikupitena / anugṛhṇantvetadvyavasitaṃ te bhrātaraḥ /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering) My lord, what is impossible for you when you are enraged? May your brothers approve this resolve of yours!
Juncture of the plot / type: <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement)

<s>Sahadeva</s>:
This has our approval.
[Behind the curtain, a great tumult is heard. All listen with astonishment.]
VERSE 1.22
Steady as the roar of <s>Mandara</s> mountain churning the waters of the ocean, whose cavities are flooded; fierce as the mutual clashing of thunder-clouds rumbling at the world's end;

A harbinger of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s (<s>Draupadī</s>'s) wrath, a tempest heralding the catastrophic destruction of the <s>Kuru</s> dynasty—whose is this war-drum that resounds in answer to our lion-roar? // 1.22 //
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[Entering in haste]

Chamberlain:
Prince! It is the blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)!
[All rise with folded hands]

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[With excitement]
Where is the blessed Lord?

Chamberlain:
He has been seized by <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>), who is enraged at his partisanship toward the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
[All mime agitation]

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
What? He has been seized?

Chamberlain:
No, no—an attempt was made to seize him!

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
What did the Lord do?

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
tataḥ sa mahātmā darśitaviśvarūpatejaḥsaṃpātamūrcchitamavadhūya kurukulamasmacchibirasaṃniveśamanuprāptaḥ / kamāramavilambitaṃ draṣṭumicchati /
children.translated_text:
Chamberlain:
Then that great soul, having shaken off the <s>Kuru</s> clan who were stunned by the blinding splendor of his revealed cosmic form, has arrived at our encampment. With him—

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
*sopahāsam**
kiṃ nāma durātmā suyodhano bhagavantaṃ saṃyantumicchati* /ākāśe dattadṛṣṭiḥ**
āḥ durātmankurukulapāṃsana evamatikrāntamaryāde tvayi nimittamātreṇa pāṇḍavakrodhena bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
[With derision]
Does the wicked <s>Suyodhana</s> truly wish to seize the blessed Lord? [Gazing up at the sky] Ha! Wretched <s>Kuru</s>—

children.text:
&sahadevaḥ&:
ārya kimasau durātmā suyodhano vāsudevamapi bhagavantaṃ svena rūpeṇa na jānāti /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sahadeva</s>:
Brother, does that wicked <s>Suyodhana</s> not even recognize the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> in his true form?

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
vatsa mūḍhaḥ khalvayaṃ durātmā / kathaṃ jānātu / paśya /

children.translated_text: VERSE 1.23

children.text: ātmārāmā vihitamatayo nirvikalpe samādhau $ jñānodrekādvighaṭitatamogranthayaḥ sattvaniṣṭhāḥ &
children.translated_text: Those who are self-delighting, whose minds are fixed in unwavering <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), who by the intensity of their knowledge have untied the knots of darkness, who are established in pure <s>sattva</s> (goodness)—

children.text: yaṃ vīkṣante kamapi tamasāṃ jyotiṣāṃ vā parastā- ē̃ ttaṃ mohāndhaḥ kathamayamamuṃ vettu devaṃ purāṇam // 1.23 //
children.translated_text: He whom [the wise] behold as something beyond darkness and light — how can this one, blinded by delusion, know that ancient god? (1.23)

<s>Bhīmasena</s>:
Child, this wretched fool is indeed deluded. How would he recognize him? Behold—
Noble <s>Jayaṃdhara</s>, what does the master now resolve?

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
svayameva gatvā mahārājasyādhyavasitaṃ jñāsyati kumāraḥ /
*iti niṣkrāntaḥ**
children.translated_text: [<s>Kañcukī</s> (chamberlain):] The prince will know the great king's resolution by going himself. [Exit.]
[Commotion behind the curtain.]
[Verse 1.24]

children.text: yatsatyavratabhaṅgabhīrumanasā yatnena mandīkṛtaṃ $ yadvismartumapīhitaṃ śamavatā śāntiṃ kulasyecchatā &
children.translated_text: That [fire of anger] which was with effort suppressed by a mind fearful of breaking the vow of truth, which one disposed to peace and desiring the family's tranquility wished even to forget —

children.text: taddyūtāraṇisaṃbhṛtaṃ nṛpavadhūkeśāmbarākarṣaṇaiḥ ē̃ krodhajyotiridaṃ mahatkuruvane yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ jṛmbhate // 1.24 //
children.translated_text: that fire of anger, kindled at the gambling table and by the dragging of the royal queen's hair and garments, now blazes forth mightily in the <s>Kuru</s> field — the wrath of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>! (1.24)

Ho! Ho! Let our <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> (army division) commanders — <s>Drupada</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Andhakas</s>, <s>Sahadeva</s>, and the rest — and the chief warriors of the <s>Kaurava</s> army, listen!
[<s>Bhīmasena</s>:] [Hearing this, with delight.] Let the noble one's fire of anger blaze forth, blaze forth with unobstructed force!

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_22}ṇāha kiṃ dāṇiṃ eso palaajalaharatthaṇidamaṃsalo khaṇe khaṇe samaradunduhī tāḍīadi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit] Lord, is this war-drum, resonant as the thunder of the clouds of dissolution, now being struck again and again?

children.text: SktCh_22: nātha kimidānīmeṣa pralayajaladharastanitamāṃsalaḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe samaradundubhistāḍyate /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Lord, is this war-drum, resonant as the thunder of the clouds of dissolution, now being struck again and again?
[<s>Bhīmasena</s>:] Queen, what else? The sacrifice is commencing!
[<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit] [With astonishment.] What sacrifice is this?
[Sanskrit rendering:] What sacrifice is this?
[Verse 1.25]

children.text: catvāro vayamṛtvijaḥ sa bhagavānkarmopadeṣṭā hariḥ $ saṃgrāmādhvaradīkṣito narapatiḥ patnī gṛhītavratā &
children.translated_text: We four are the officiating priests, that blessed <s>Hari</s> is the director of the rite, the king is consecrated for the sacrifice of war, and his wife has taken the vow;

children.text: kauravyāḥ paśavaḥ priyāparibhavakleśopaśāntiḥ phalaṃ ē̃ rājanyopanimantraṇāya rasati sphītaṃ yaśodundubhiḥ // 1.25 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Kauravas</s> are the sacrificial victims, the relief from the suffering of the beloved's humiliation is the fruit, and the drum of glory resounds mightily to invite the kings. (1.25)
[<s>Bhīmasena</s>:] The sacrifice of battle! For indeed —
[<s>Sahadeva</s>:] Noble one, let us now go, having been permitted by the elders, to act in a manner befitting our prowess.

children.text:
&bhīmasenaḥ&:
vatsa ete vayamudyatā evāryasyānujñānamanuṣṭhātum* /
utthāya**
devi gacchāmo vayamidānīṃ kurukulakṣayāya /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhīmasena</s>:] Son, we are indeed ready to carry out the noble one's command. [Rising.] Queen, we now go for the destruction of the <s>Kuru</s> clan!

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_24}*bāṣpaṃ dhārayantī**
ṇāha asurasamarāhimuhassa hariṇo via maṅgalaṃ tumhāṇaṃ hodu /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit] [Restraining tears.] Lord, may you have the same blessing as <s>Hari</s> when he faces the battle of the demons!

children.text: SktCh_24: nātha asurasamarābhimukhasya hareriva maṅgalaṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhavatu /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Lord, may you have the same blessing as <s>Hari</s> when he faces the battle of the demons!
[Both:] We accept [your] words of blessing!

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_25}aṇṇaṃ ca ṇāha puṇo bi tumhehiṃ samarādo āacchia ahaṃ samāsāsaidavvā /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit] And another thing, lord — when you return from the battle, you must console me again.

children.text: SktCh_25: anyacca nātha punarapi yuṣmābhiḥ samarādāgatyāhaṃ samāśvāsayitavyā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] And another thing, lord — when you return from the battle, you must console me again.
[Verse 1.26]
Again with face cast down from the shame of weariness from humiliation —
you shall not see <s>Vṛkodara</s> (Bhīmasena) without having annihilated all the <s>Kauravas</s>! (1.26)
[<s>Bhīmasena</s>:] O daughter of the <s>Pāñcāla</s> king, why even now with false consolation?

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_26}ṇāha mā khu mā khu jaṇṇaseṇīparihavuddībidakobāṇalā aṇavekkhidasarīrā saṃcarissaha / jado appamattasaṃcaraṇijjāiṃ riubalāiṃ suṇīanti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit] Lord, pray do not, pray do not go about heedless of your bodies, with the fire of anger kindled by <s>Yājñasenī</s>'s (Draupadī's) humiliation! For it is heard that the enemy forces require careful approach.

children.text: SktCh_26: nātha mā khalu mā khalu yājñasenīparibhavoddīpitakopānalā anapekṣitaśarīrāḥ saṃcariṣyatha / yato 'pramattasaṃcaraṇīyāni ripubalāni śrūyante /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Lord, pray do not go about heedless of your bodies, with the fire of anger kindled by <s>Yājñasenī</s>'s humiliation! For it is heard that the enemy forces require careful approach.
[Verse 1.27]
In the mire of blood, fat, flesh, and brains from elephants split open by mutual blows, where chariots are sunk and warriors stride with steps placed above [them],

where headless trunks dance to the terrible music of <s>Śiva</s>'s hosts at the grand feast of blood-drinking — in the waters of the single ocean of battle, the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> are skilled at moving about! (1.27)
[<s>Bhīmasena</s>:] O woman of noble warrior lineage!
[Exeunt all.]
Thus ends the first act. Act 2. The second act.
[Then enters the <s>Kañcukī</s> (chamberlain).]

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
ādiṣṭo 'smi mahārājaduryodhanena / vinayaṃdhara satvaraṃ gaccha tvam / anviṣyatāṃ devī bhānumatī / api nivṛttāmbāyāḥ pādavandanasamayānna veti / yatastāṃ vilokya nihatābhimanyavo rādheyajayadrathaprabhṛtayo 'smatsenāpatayaḥ samarabhūmiṃ gatvā sabhājayitavyā iti / tanmayā drutataraṃ gantavyam / aho prabhaviṣṇutā mahārājasya yanmama jarasābhibhūtasya maryādāmātramevāvarodhavyāpāraḥ / atha vā kimiti jarāmupālabheya yataḥ sarvāntaḥpurikāṇāmeva vyāvahāriko veṣaśceṣṭā ca / tathā hi

children.translated_text: [Verse 2.1]

children.text: noccaiḥ satyapi cakṣuṣīkṣitamalaṃ śrutvāpi nākarṇitaṃ $ śaktenāpyadhikāra ityadhikṛtā yaṣṭiḥ samālambitā &
children.translated_text: Though having eyes, I have not looked up fully; though hearing, I have not listened; though able, saying 'this is [not] my authority,' I have grasped the staff [of old age];

children.text: sarvatra skhaliteṣu dattamanasā yātaṃ mayā noddhataṃ ē̃ sevāsvīkṛtajīvitasya jarasā kiṃ nāma yanme kṛtam // 2.1 //
children.translated_text: with mind attentive to stumbling everywhere, I have walked without haste — what indeed has old age, which has claimed my life in service, not done to me? (2.1)

[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] I have been instructed by the great king <s>Duryodhana</s>: '<s>Vinayaṃdhara</s>, go quickly! Let Queen <s>Bhānumatī</s> be sought out — whether or not she has returned from the time of paying respects at her mother-in-law's feet. For, seeing her, the commanders of our army — <s>Rādheya</s> (Karṇa), <s>Jayadratha</s>, and the rest — whose [enemy] <s>Abhimanyu</s> has been slain, must go to the battlefield and be honored.' Therefore I must go most swiftly. Ah, the power of the great king, that for me, overcome by old age, the work of the women's quarters is merely a matter of propriety! Or rather, why should I blame old age, since the dress and behavior of all those in the inner apartments is customary? For indeed —

children.text:
*parikramya dṛṣṭvākāśe**
vihaṃgike api śvaśrūjanapādavandanaṃ kṛtvā pratinivṛttā bhānumatī* /karṇaṃ dattvā**
kiṃ kathayasi / eṣā bhānumatī devī patyuḥ samaravijayāśaṃsayā nirvartitagurudevapādavandanādyaprabhṛtyārabdhaniyamā bālodyāne tiṣṭhatīti / tadbhadre gaccha tvamātmavyāpārāya yāvadahamapyatrasthāṃ devīṃ mahārājāya nivedayāmi* /iti parikramya**
sādhu pativrate sādhu strībhāve 'pi vartamānā varaṃ bhavatī na punarmahārājaḥ yo 'yamudyateṣu balavatsvabalavatsu vā vāsudevasahāyeṣu pāṇḍuputreṣvariṣvadyāpyantaḥpuravihāramanubhavati* /vicintya**
idamaparamayathātathaṃ svāminaśceṣṭitam / kutaḥ

children.translated_text: [Verse 2.2]

children.text: ā śastragrahaṇādakuṇṭhaparaśostasyāpi jetā mune- $ stāpāyāsya na pāṇḍusūnubhirayaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śaraiḥ śāyitaḥ &
children.translated_text: Even the conqueror of that sage [<s>Paraśurāma</s>], whose axe was unyielding until the taking up of weapons — this <s>Bhīṣma</s> has been laid low on a bed of arrows by the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, causing grief to him [<s>Duryodhana</s>];
and he [<s>Duryodhana</s>] is pleased at the killing of <s>Abhimanyu</s>, a boy, alone, whose bow had been cut by enemies, while [the killer] was weary from victories over many proud archers! (2.2)

[Walking about and looking into the sky.] Bird-woman! Has <s>Bhānumatī</s> returned after paying respects to the feet of her mother-in-law? [Listening.] What do you say? 'This Queen <s>Bhānumatī</s>, in hope of her husband's victory in battle, having completed the salutation to the feet of her elders and the gods, has been observing a vow since dawn and stands in the pleasure garden.' Then, good woman, go attend to your duties while I report to the great king about the queen who is here. [Walking about.] Well done, faithful wife, well done! Though being a woman, you are superior — and not the great king, who even now, when the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, aided by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, are in arms — whether powerful or not so powerful — still enjoys the pleasures of the women's quarters. [Reflecting.] This too is another inappropriate action of the master. For —

children.text: sarvathā daivaṃ naḥ svasti kariṣyati / tadyāvadatrasthāṃ devīṃ mahārājāya nivedayāmi* /iti niṣkrāntaḥ**
children.translated_text: In any case, may fate bring us well-being! Now let me report to the great king about the queen who is here. [Exit.]
End of the interlude.

children.text: *tataḥ praviśatyāsanasthā devī bhānumatī sakhī ceṭī ca**
children.translated_text: [Then enter Queen <s>Bhānumatī</s>, seated, her friend, and a maidservant.]

children.text:
&sakhī&:
{Pkt_27}sahi bhāṇumadi kīsa dāṇiṃ tumaṃ sibiṇaadaṃsaṇamettassa kide ahimāṇiṇo mahārāadujjohaṇassa mahisī bhavia evvaṃ vialiadhīrabhāvā adimettaṃ saṃtappasi /
children.translated_text: [Friend:] [Prakrit] Friend <s>Bhānumatī</s>, why do you now, being the queen of the proud great king <s>Duryodhana</s>, lose your composure and grieve so excessively on account of a mere dream?

children.text: SktCh_27: sakhi bhānumati kasmādidānīṃ tvaṃ svapnadarśanamātrasya kṛte 'bhimānino mahārājaduryodhanasya mahiṣī bhūtvaivaṃ vigalitadhīrabhāvātimātraṃ saṃtapyase /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Friend <s>Bhānumatī</s>, why do you now, being the queen of the proud great king <s>Duryodhana</s>, lose your composure and grieve so excessively on account of a mere dream?

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_28}bhaṭṭiṇi sohaṇaṃ bhaṇādi suvaaṇā / sibiṇaanto jaṇo kiṃ ṇa khu palabadi /
children.translated_text: [Maidservant:] [Prakrit] My lady, the fair-faced one speaks well. Does not a person in sleep merely babble?

children.text: SktCh_28: bhaṭṭini śobhanaṃ vadati suvadanā / svapañjanaḥ kiṃ na khalu pralapati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] My lady, the fair-faced one speaks well. Does not a person in sleep merely babble?

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_29}hañje evvaṃ edaṃ / kiṃ du edaṃ sibiṇaaṃ adimettaṃ akusaladaṃsaṇaṃ me paḍibhādi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhānumatī</s>:] [Prakrit] Dear girl, that is so. But this dream appears to me as an excessively inauspicious vision.

children.text: SktCh_29: hañje evametat / kiṃ tvayaṃ svapno 'timātramakuśaladarśano me pratibhāti /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Dear girl, that is so. But this dream appears to me as an excessively inauspicious vision.

children.text:
&sakhī&:
{Pkt_30}piasahi jai evvaṃ tā kahehi sibiṇaaṃ jeṇa amhe bi paḍiṭṭhābaantīo dhammappasaṃsāe devadāsaṃkittaṇeṇa duvvādipaḍiggaheṇa a paḍihaḍissāmo /
children.translated_text: [Friend:] [Prakrit] Dear friend, if so, then tell the dream, so that we two, by praise of dharma, by invoking the gods, and by grasping dūrvā grass and such [auspicious things], may avert it.

children.text: SktCh_30: priyasakhi yadyevaṃ tatkathaya svapnaṃ yenāvāmapi pratiṣṭhāpayantyau dharmapraśaṃsayā devatāsaṃkīrtanena dūrvādiparigraheṇa ca parihariṣyāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Dear friend, if so, then tell the dream, so that we two, by praise of <s>dharma</s>, by invoking the gods, and by grasping <s>dūrvā</s> grass and such [auspicious things], may avert it.

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_31}sohaṇaṃ kkhu bhaṇādi suvaaṇā / akusaladaṃsaṇā sibiṇaā devadāṇaṃ pasaṃsāe kusalapariṇāmā honti tti suṇīadi /
children.translated_text: [Maidservant:] [Prakrit] The fair-faced one speaks well indeed. It is heard that dreams of inauspicious visions become auspicious in their outcome through praise of the gods.

children.text: SktCh_31: śobhanaṃ khalu bhaṇati suvadanā / akuśaladarśanāḥ svapnā devatānāṃ praśaṃsayā kuśalapariṇāmā bhavantīti śrūyate /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] The fair-faced one speaks well indeed. It is heard that dreams of inauspicious visions become auspicious in their outcome through praise of the gods.

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_32}jai evvaṃ tā kahaissaṃ / avahidā dāva hohi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhānumatī</s>:] [Prakrit] If so, then I shall tell. Be attentive now.
[Sanskrit rendering:] If so, then I shall tell. Be attentive now.
[Friend:] [Prakrit] I am attentive. Let my dear friend speak.
[Sanskrit rendering:] I am attentive. Let my dear friend speak.

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_34}halā bhaeṇa visumaridamhi / tā ciṭṭha jāva savvaṃ sumaria kahaissaṃ* /iti cintāṃ nāṭayati**
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhānumatī</s>:] [Prakrit] Dear, I have forgotten out of fear. So wait while I recall everything and tell you. [Mimes deep thought.]

children.text: SktCh_34: halā bhayena vismṛtāsmi / tattiṣṭha yāvatsarvaṃ smṛtvā kathayiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Dear, I have forgotten out of fear. So wait while I recall everything and tell you.
[Then enter <s>Duryodhana</s> and the chamberlain.]
[Verse 2.3]
Whether great or small, done secretly, done in person or through another,
an injury to one's enemies causes great delight. (2.3)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Well said is this by someone —
For today, hearing that <s>Abhimanyu</s> has been slain by <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Jayadratha</s>, and others, our hearts have as it were breathed again.

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
deva nedamatiduṣkaramācāryaśastraprabhāvāṇāṃ karṇajayadrathayorvā / kā nāmātra ślāghā /
children.translated_text: [<s>Kañcukī</s>:] Sire, this is no great feat for those who possess the power of the teacher's [<s>Droṇa</s>'s] weapons, or for <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Jayadratha</s>. What glory is there in this?

children.text:
&rājā&:
vinayaṃdhara kimāha bhavān / eko bahubhirbālo lūnaśarāsanaśca nihata ityatra kā ślāghā kurupuṃgavānāmiti / mūḍha paśya /

children.translated_text: [Verse 2.4]
When the aged son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> (<s>Bhīṣma</s>) was slain by placing <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> in front,
whatever glory belongs to the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, that same glory shall be ours! (2.4)

[King:] <s>Vinayaṃdhara</s>, what does the sir say? 'One [boy], by many, a child, with his bow cut — that he was killed: what glory is there in this for the foremost of the <s>Kurus</s>?' Fool, observe —

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
*savailakṣyam**
deva na mamāyaṃ saṃkalpaḥ / kiṃ tu bhavatpauruṣapratīghāto 'smābhirnāvalokitapūrva ityata evaṃ vijñāpayāmi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Kañcukī</s>:] [With embarrassment.] Sire, this is not my thought. But since we have never before witnessed an impediment to your valor, it is for that reason I speak thus.
[Verse 2.5]
Together with his retinue, together with his kinsmen, together with his allies, together with his sons, together with his brothers —

children.text: svabalena nihanti saṃyuge na cirātpāṇḍusutaḥ suyodhanam // 2.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) shall before long slay the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> in battle with his own might! (2.5)
[King:] That is how it is —
[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] [Closing his ears in fear.] May evil be averted! May this inauspicious [saying] be repelled!
[King:] <s>Vinayaṃdhara</s>, what did I say?

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
*sahabhṛtyagaṇaṃ sabāndhavaṃ sahamitraṃ sasutaṃ sahānujam / svabalena nihanti saṃyuge na cirātpāṇḍusutaṃ suyodhanaḥ // iti paṭhati**
etadviparītamabhihitaṃ devena /
children.translated_text: [<s>Kañcukī</s>:] [Recites:] 'Together with his retinue, together with his kinsmen, together with his allies, together with his sons, together with his brothers — <s>Suyodhana</s> shall before long slay the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> in battle with his own might!' The opposite of this was spoken by Your Majesty [i.e., you accidentally said <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s son will slay <s>Suyodhana</s>].

children.text:
&rājā&:
vinayaṃdhara adya khalu bhānumatī yathāpūrvaṃ māmanāmantrya vāsabhavanātprātareva niṣkrānteti vyākṣiptaṃ me manaḥ / tadādeśaya tamuddeśaṃ yatrasthā bhānumatī /
children.translated_text: [King:] <s>Vinayaṃdhara</s>, today indeed <s>Bhānumatī</s> departed from her residence early in the morning without taking leave of me as before, and my mind is disturbed. So point out the place where <s>Bhānumatī</s> is.
[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] This way, this way, Your Majesty.
[Both walk about.]
[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] [Looking ahead and smelling the fragrance from all around.]

children.text: deva paśya paśya / etattuhinakaṇaśiśirasamīraṇodvellitabandhanacyutaśephālikāviracitakusumaprakaramīṣadālohitamugdhavadhūkapolapāṭalalodhraprasūnavijitaśyāmalatāsaubhāgyamunmīlitabakulakundakusumasurabhiśītalaṃ prabhātakālaramaṇīyamagrataste bālodyānam / tadavalokayatu devaḥ / tathā hi

children.translated_text: [Verse 2.6]
With flowers that have fallen together with their nectar mixed with frost, awakened by night [i.e., blooming at night],
and lotuses whose dense fragrance is revealed from within buds split open by the rays of the sun — the bees are falling [upon them]. (2.6)

Sire, look, look! Before you lies the pleasure garden, delightful in the morning hour — where the fallen <s>śephālikā</s> flowers, their bonds loosened by the breeze cool with drops of dew, have formed heaps of blossoms; where it is slightly reddened like the cheeks of an innocent young bride, surpassing the beauty of dark creepers with <s>lodhra</s> flowers in bloom; where it is cool and fragrant with the opened <s>bakula</s> and <s>kunda</s> blossoms. Let Your Majesty behold it. For indeed —
Awakened, like kings being touched by the hands of <s>Bhānu</s> (the Sun) that have entered through the lattice-openings of the wide-spread petals yawning open,

children.text: strībhiḥ sārdhaṃ ghanaparimalastokalakṣyāṅgarāgā ē̃ muñcantyete vikacanalinīgarbhaśayyāṃ dvirephāḥ // 2.7 //
children.translated_text: together with their mates, their body-cosmetics barely visible from the dense fragrance, these bees now leave their beds in the cups of blooming lotuses. (2.7)
<s>Rājā</s>: (Looking around) <s>Vinayaṃdhara</s>, this is exceedingly beautiful at this dawn hour. Behold!

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
deva nanveṣā devī bhānumatī suvadanayā taralikayā ca paryupāsyamānā tiṣṭhati / tadupasarpatu devaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kañcukī</s> (Chamberlain): My lord, here is Queen <s>Bhānumatī</s>, attended by <s>Suvadanā</s> and <s>Taralikā</s>. Let my lord approach her.

children.text:
&rājā&:
*dṛṣṭvā**
ārya vinayaṃdhara gaccha tvaṃ sāṃgrāmikaṃ me rathamupakalpayitum / ahamapyeṣa devīṃ dṛṣṭvānupadamāgata eva /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: (Having looked) Noble <s>Vinayaṃdhara</s>, go and prepare my war-chariot. I too shall come presently, after seeing the Queen. (Exit Vinayaṃdhara)
<s>Kañcukī</s>: The lord's command is carried out. (Exit)
<s>Sakhī</s> (Friend): Dear friend, have you remembered it?
[Sanskrit rendering: Dear friend, have you remembered it?]

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_36}sahi sumaridaṃ / ajja kila pamadavaṇe āsīṇāe mama aggado keṇa bi adisaidadivvarūbiṇā ṇauleṇa ahisadaṃ vābādidaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Friend, I have remembered. Today, while I was seated in the pleasure-garden, before me some mongoose of surpassingly divine form killed a hundred serpents.

children.text: SktCh_36: sakhi smṛtam / adya kila pramadavana āsīnāyā mamāgrataḥ kenāpyatiśayitadivyarūpiṇā nakulenāhiśataṃ vyāpāditam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Friend, I have remembered. Today, while I was seated in the pleasure-garden, before me a mongoose of surpassingly divine form killed a hundred serpents.]

children.text:
&ubhe&:
{Pkt_37}*apavāryātmagatam**
santaṃ pābaṃ paḍihadaṃ amaṅgalaṃ* /prakāśam**
tado tado /
children.translated_text: Both: (Aside, to themselves) May the evil be averted! May the inauspicious be warded off! (Aloud) Then what happened?
[Sanskrit rendering: May the evil be averted! May the inauspicious be warded off! Then what happened?]

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_38}adisaṃdābobagahīahiaāe visumaridaṃ mae / tā puṇo bi sumaria kahaissaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: I had forgotten, as my heart was seized by excessive anguish. But now, remembering again, I shall tell it.

children.text: SktCh_38: atisaṃtāpopagṛhītahṛdayayā vismṛtaṃ mayā / tatpunarapi smṛtvā kathayiṣye /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: I had forgotten, as my heart was seized by excessive anguish. But now, remembering again, I shall tell it.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
aho devī bhānumatī suvadanātaralikābhyāṃ saha kimapi mantrayamāṇā tiṣṭhati / bhavatu / anena latājālenāntaritaḥ śṛṇomi tāvadāsāṃ viśrabdhālāpam* /iti tathā sthitaḥ**
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: Ah, Queen <s>Bhānumatī</s> is conferring something with <s>Suvadanā</s> and <s>Taralikā</s>. Very well. Concealed by this curtain of creepers, let me listen to their intimate conversation. (He stands thus)
<s>Sakhī</s>: Friend, enough of anguish! Let the dear friend speak.

children.text: SktCh_39: sakhi alaṃ saṃtāpena / kathayatu priyasakhī /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Friend, enough of anguish! Let the dear friend speak.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
kiṃ nu khalvasyāḥ saṃtāpakāraṇam / atha vānāmantrya māmiyamadya vāsabhavanānniṣkrānteti samarthita evāsyā mayā kopaḥ / ayi bhānumati aviṣayaḥ khalu duryodhano bhavatyāḥ kopasya /
kiṃ kaṇṭhe śithilīkṛto bhujalatāpāśaḥ pramādānmayā $ nidrācchedavivartaneṣvabhimukhaṃ nādyāsi saṃbhāvitā &
children.translated_text: Was the vine-like embrace of your arms loosened from my neck through some carelessness of mine? Were you not greeted face to face when I turned in my sleep-disturbed tossings?

children.text: anyastrījanasaṃkathālaghurahaṃ svapne tvayā lakṣito ē̃ doṣaṃ paśyasi kaṃ priye parijanopālambhayogye mayi // 2.8 //
children.translated_text: Did you perceive me in a dream speaking lightly with other women? What fault do you see, beloved, in me who deserves only the reproach of attendants? (2.8)

<s>Rājā</s>: What indeed is the cause of her anguish? Or perhaps — she left the bedchamber this morning without addressing me, so I had supposed she was angry. O <s>Bhānumatī</s>, <s>Duryodhana</s> is surely not a fitting object of your anger!
She, whose mind is fixed solely on me, with affection that is bound by jealous love,
has surely, out of the excessive fondness of a most beloved wife, imagined some trifling offence of mine on her own. (2.9)
(Reflecting) Or rather —
Even so, let me listen to what she will say.

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_40}halā haṃ tado tassa adisaidadivvarūbiṇo ṇaulassa daṃsaṇeṇa ussuā jādā /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Friend, then I became eager to see that mongoose of surpassingly divine form.

children.text: SktCh_40: halā ahaṃ tatastasyātiśayitadivyarūpiṇo nakulasya darśanenotsukā jātā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Friend, then I became eager to see that mongoose of surpassingly divine form.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
*savailakṣyam**
kiṃ nāmātiśayitadivyarūpiṇo nakulasya darśanenotsukā jātā / tatkimanayā pāpayā mādrīsutānuraktayā vayamevaṃ vipralabdhāḥ* /sotprekṣamiyamasmaditi paṭhitvā**
mūḍha duryodhana kulaṭāvipralabhyamānamātmānaṃ bahumanyamāno 'dhunā kiṃ vakṣyasi* /kiṃ kaṇṭha ityādi paṭhitvā diśo 'valokya**
aho etadarthamevāsyāḥ prātareva viviktasthānābhilāṣaḥ sakhījanasaṃkathāsu ca pakṣapātaḥ / duryodhanastu mohādavijñātabandhakīhṛdayasāraḥ kvāpi paribhrāntaḥ / āḥ pāpe matparigrahapāṃsule
tadbhīrutvaṃ tava mama puraḥ sāhasānīdṛśāni $ ślāghā sāsmadvapuṣi vinayavyutkrame 'pyeṣa rāgaḥ &
children.translated_text: That timidity of yours before me, such bold exploits, this pride and passion even in transgression of modesty toward my person,

children.text: taccaudāryaṃ mayi jaḍamatau cāpale ko 'pi panthāḥ ē̃ khyāte tasminvitamasi kule janma kaulīnametat // 2.10 //
children.translated_text: that magnanimity, some strange course in my dull-witted credulity — this is your noble birth in that well-known, tainted lineage! (2.10)

<s>Rājā</s>: (With embarrassment) What — she became eager to see a mongoose of surpassingly divine form? Then have I been deceived by this wicked woman who is enamored of <s>Mādrī</s>'s son? (Reading "she whose mind is fixed solely on me" again with suspicion) Fool <s>Duryodhana</s>, deluded by a harlot, how highly you thought of yourself — what will you say now? (Reading "Was the vine-like embrace..." again, looking in all directions) Ah, so this is why she desired a secluded spot early in the morning, and showed such partiality for the company of her friends! While <s>Duryodhana</s>, in his delusion, ignorant of this wanton's true heart, has been wandering about aimlessly. Ah, you wicked woman, disgrace to my household!
<s>Sakhī</s>: Then what happened?
[Sanskrit rendering: Then what happened?]

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_42}tado ujjhia taṃ āsaṇaṭṭhāṇaṃ ladāmaṇḍabaṃ paviṭṭhā / tado so bi maṃ aṇusaranto evva ladāmaṇḍabaṃ paviṭṭho /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Then, leaving that sitting place, I entered a bower of creepers. And he too, following me, entered the bower of creepers.

children.text: SktCh_42: tata ujjhitvā tadāsanasthānaṃ latāmaṇḍapaṃ praviṣṭā / tataḥ so 'pi māmanusaranneva latāmaṇḍapaṃ praviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Then, leaving that sitting place, I entered a bower of creepers. And he too, following me, entered the bower of creepers.]
In that very bower where, in the fullness of long-standing affection, my secret amorous pleasures were once revealed in private,

children.text: tatraiva duścaritamadya nivedayantī ē̃ hrīṇāsi pāpahṛdaye na sakhījane 'smin // 2.11 //
children.translated_text: now reporting her misconduct in that very place — are you not ashamed, O wicked-hearted one, before these friends? (2.11)
<s>Rājā</s>: Ah, what shamelessness befitting a harlot, from this wicked woman!
Both: Then what happened?
[Sanskrit rendering: Then what happened?]

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_44}tado teṇa sagavvaṃ pasāriakareṇa apahariaṃ me thaṇaṃsuaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Then, with an arrogantly outstretched hand, he snatched away my breast-cloth.

children.text: SktCh_44: tatastena sagarvaṃ prasāritakareṇāpahṛtaṃ me stanāṃśukam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Then, with an arrogantly outstretched hand, he snatched away my breast-cloth.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
*vicintya**
sagarvaṃ prasāritakareṇāpahṛtaṃ me stanāṃśukam* /sakrodham**
alamataḥ paraṃ śrutvā / bhavatu tāvattasya paravanitāskandanapragalbhasya mādrīsutahatakasya jīvitamapaharāmi* /kiṃcidgatvā vicintya**
atha veyameva tāvatpāpaśīlā prathamamanuśāsanīyā* /iti nivartate**
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: (Reflecting) "With an arrogantly outstretched hand, he snatched away my breast-cloth." (Angrily) Enough! I need hear no more. Very well, I shall take the life of that insolent wretch, <s>Mādrī</s>'s son, who dares to assault another's wife! (Walking a little, then reflecting) Or rather, let this sinful woman herself first be chastised! (He turns back)
Both: Then what happened?
[Sanskrit rendering: Then what happened?]
<s>Bhānumatī</s>: Then I was awakened by the sound of the auspicious morning drums of my noble lord, mingled with the singing of the courtesans.
[Sanskrit rendering: Then I was awakened by the sound of the auspicious morning drums of my noble lord, mingled with the singing of the courtesans.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
*savitarkam**
kiṃ nu pratibodhitāsmīti svapnadarśanamanayā varṇitaṃ bhavet* /vicintya**
bhavatu sakhīvacanādvyaktirbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: (With deliberation) What? "I was awakened" — could she be describing a dream? (Reflecting) Very well, the words of her friend will make it clear.
(Both [friends] look at each other with dejection.)

children.text:
&suvadanā&:
{Pkt_47}jaṃ kiṃ bi ettha accāhidaṃ taṃ bhāīrahīppamuhāṇaṃ ṇaīṇaṃ salileṇa avaharīadu / bhaavadāṇaṃ bamhaṇāṇaṃ bi āsīsāe āhudihudeṇa pajjalideṇa bhaavadā hudāsaṇeṇa a ṇassadu /
children.translated_text: <s>Suvadanā</s>: Whatever inauspicious thing has occurred here, let it be washed away by the waters of sacred rivers headed by the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges). Let it be destroyed also by the blessings of the holy <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and by the sacred fire blazing with oblations.

children.text: SktCh_47: yatkimapyatrātyāhitaṃ tadbhāgīrathīpramukhāṇāṃ nadīnāṃ salilenāpahriyatām / bhagavatāṃ brāhmaṇānāmapyāśiṣāhutihutena prajvalitena bhagavatā hutāśanena ca naśyatu /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Whatever inauspicious thing has occurred here, let it be washed away by the waters of sacred rivers headed by the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>. Let it be destroyed also by the blessings of the holy <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, by the sacred fire blazing with oblations, and by the blessed <s>Hutāśana</s> (fire-god).]

children.text:
&rājā&:
alaṃ vikalpena / svapnadarśanamevaitadanayā varṇitam / mayā punarmandadhiyānyathaiva saṃbhāvitam /
diṣṭyārdhaśrutivipralambhajanitakrodhādahaṃ no gato $ diṣṭyā no paruṣaṃ ruṣārdhakathane kiṃcinmayā vyāhṛtam &
children.translated_text: Fortunately, I did not go forth in anger born of a half-heard, misleading account; fortunately, no harsh word was uttered by me in the midst of my rage;

children.text: māṃ pratyāyayituṃ vimūḍhahṛdayaṃ diṣṭyā kathāntaṃ gatā ē̃ mithyādūṣitayānayā virahitaṃ diṣṭyā na jātaṃ jagat // 2.12 //
children.translated_text: fortunately, the tale reached its end to convince my bewildered heart; fortunately, the world has not been deprived of this one who was falsely accused by me. (2.12)
<s>Rājā</s>: Enough of doubt! It was indeed a dream that she was describing. And I, dull-witted, had interpreted it quite otherwise.
<s>Bhānumatī</s>: Friend, tell me — is there anything auspicious in this?
[Sanskrit rendering: Friend, tell me — is there anything auspicious in this?]

children.text:
&sakhī ceṭī ca&:
{Pkt_49}*anyo 'nyamavalokyāpavārya**
ettha ṇatthi thoaṃ bi suhasūaaṃ / jai ettha alīaṃ kahaissaṃ tā piasahīe abarāhiṇī bhavissaṃ / so evva siṇiddho jaṇo jo pucchido parusaṃ bi hidaṃ bhaṇādi* /prakāśam**
sahi savvaṃ evva edaṃ asuhaṇivedaṇaṃ / tā devadāṇaṃ paṇāmeṇa dujādijaṇapaḍiggaheṇa a antarīadu / ṇa hu dāṭhiṇo ṇaulassa vā daṃsaṇaṃ ahisadavahaṃ a sibiṇae pasaṃsanti viakkhaṇā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sakhī</s> and <s>Ceṭī</s> (maid): (Looking at each other, aside) There is not even a little that is auspicious here. If I speak falsely, I shall be a betrayer of my dear friend. That alone is a true friend who, when asked, speaks even harsh truths for one's benefit. (Aloud) Friend, all of this portends misfortune. Let it be warded off by obeisance to the gods and by gifts to the twice-born. For the wise do not praise in dreams the sight of a fanged creature, or of a mongoose, or the killing of a hundred serpents.

children.text: SktCh_49: atra nāsti stokamapi śubhasūcakam / yadyatrālīkaṃ kathayiṣye tatpriyasakhyā aparādhinī bhaviṣyāmi / sa eva snigdho jano yaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ paruṣamapi hitaṃ bhaṇati / sakhi sarvamevaitadaśubhanivedanam / taddevatānāṃ praṇāmena dvijātijanapratigraheṇa cāntaryatām / na khalu daṃṣṭriṇo nakulasya vā darśanamahiśatavadhaṃ ca svapne praśaṃsanti vicakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: There is not even a little that is auspicious here. If I speak falsely, I shall be a betrayer of my dear friend. That alone is a true friend who, when asked, speaks even harsh truths for one's benefit. Friend, all of this portends misfortune. Let it be warded off by obeisance to the gods and by gifts to the twice-born. For the wise do not praise in dreams the sight of a fanged creature, or of a mongoose, or the killing of a hundred serpents.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
avitathamāha suvadanā / nakulena pannagaśatavadhaḥ stanāṃśukāpaharaṇaṃ ca niyatamariṣṭodarkaṃ tarkayāmi /
paryāyeṇa hi dṛśyante svapnāḥ kāmaṃ śubhāśubhāḥ /
children.translated_text: For dreams, auspicious and inauspicious, are seen in succession;
but this number of a hundred seems to touch me along with my brothers. (2.13)
<s>Rājā</s>: <s>Suvadanā</s> speaks truly. I think that the killing of a hundred serpents by a mongoose and the snatching of the breast-cloth certainly portend calamity.

children.text:
*vāmākṣispandanaṃ sūcayitvā**
āḥ mamāpi nāma duryodhanasyānimittāni hṛdayakṣobhamāvedayanti* /sāvaṣṭambham**
atha vā bhīrujanahṛdayaprakampaneṣu kā gaṇanā duryodhanasyaivaṃvidheṣu / gītaścāyamartho 'ṅgirasā /

children.translated_text: The movements of planets, dreams, omens, and prayers —

children.text: phalanti kākatālīyaṃ tebhyaḥ prājñā na bibhyati // 2.14 //
children.translated_text: they bear fruit like the coincidence of the crow and the palm-nut; the wise do not fear them. (2.14)

(Indicating a twitch in the left eye) Ah, even for me, <s>Duryodhana</s>, evil omens disturb the heart. (With resolve) Or rather — what do such things matter to <s>Duryodhana</s>, which merely make timid hearts tremble? And this is the teaching of <s>Aṅgiras</s>:
Therefore, I shall dispel <s>Bhānumatī</s>'s groundless feminine suspicion.

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_50}halā suvaaṇe pekkha dāva udaagirisiharantaridavimukkarahavaro vialidasaṃjhārāappasaṇṇadurāloamaṇḍalo jādo bhaavaṃ diahaṇāho /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Friend <s>Suvadanā</s>, look! The blessed Lord of the Day has arisen, his chariot released from behind the peak of the eastern mountain, his orb clearly visible now that the redness of dawn has faded.

children.text: SktCh_50: halā suvadane paśya tāvadudayagiriśikharāntaritavimuktarathavaro vigalitasaṃdhyārāgaprasannadurālokamaṇḍalo jāto bhagavāndivasanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Friend <s>Suvadanā</s>, look! The blessed Lord of the Day has arisen, his chariot released from behind the peak of the eastern mountain, his orb clearly visible now that the redness of dawn has faded.]

children.text:
&sakhī&:
{Pkt_51}sahi rosāṇidakaṇaapattasariseṇa ladājālantarobahidakiraṇaṇivaheṇa piñjaridujjāṇabhūmibhāo duppekkhaṇijjo bhaavaṃ sahassarassī saṃvutto / tā samao de lohidacandaṇakusumagabbheṇa aggheṇa pajjubaṭṭhāduṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sakhī</s>: Friend, the blessed thousand-rayed one has become hard to look upon, with his beams streaming through the lattice of creepers like gold leaves fashioned by anger, turning the garden ground yellow. It is now time for you to worship him with an offering containing red sandalwood and flowers.

children.text: SktCh_51: sakhi roṣāṇitakanakapatrasadṛśena latājālāntaropahitakiraṇanivahena piñjaritodyānabhūmibhāgo duḥprekṣaṇīyo bhagavānsahasraraśmiḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / tatsamayaste lohitacandanakusumagarbheṇārgheṇa paryupasthātum /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Friend, the blessed thousand-rayed one has become hard to look upon, with his beams streaming through the lattice of creepers like gold leaves fashioned by anger, turning the garden ground yellow. It is now time for you to worship him with an offering containing red sandalwood and flowers.]

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_52}hañje taralie ubaṇehi me agghabhāaṇaṃ jāva bhaavado sahassarassiṇo sabariaṃ ṇivvattemi /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: <s>Taralikā</s>, bring me the offering vessel so that I may perform the worship of the blessed thousand-rayed one.

children.text: SktCh_52: hañje taralike upanaya me 'rghyabhājanaṃ yāvadbhagavataḥ sahasraraśmeḥ saparyāṃ nirvartayāmi /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: <s>Taralikā</s>, bring me the offering vessel so that I may perform the worship of the blessed thousand-rayed one.]
<s>Ceṭī</s> (Maid): As the Queen commands. (Exit)
[Sanskrit rendering: As the Queen commands.]
<s>Rājā</s>: This is the perfect opportunity to approach my beloved. (He approaches.)
(Enter [Ceṭī])

children.text:
&ceṭī&:
{Pkt_54}bhaṭṭiṇi edaṃ agghabhāaṇaṃ / tā ṇivvattīadu bhaavado sahassarassiṇo sabariā /
children.translated_text: <s>Ceṭī</s>: My lady, here is the offering vessel. Now let the worship of the blessed thousand-rayed one be performed.

children.text: SktCh_54: bhaṭṭini idamarghyabhājanam / tannivartyatāṃ bhagavataḥ sahasraraśmeḥ saparyā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: My lady, here is the offering vessel. Now let the worship of the blessed thousand-rayed one be performed.]

children.text:
&sakhī&:
{Pkt_55}*vilokyātmagatam**
kahaṃ mahārāo āado / hanta jādo se ṇiamabhaṅgo /
children.translated_text: <s>Sakhī</s>: (Looking, aside to herself) How — the king has come! Alas, her observance is now broken.

children.text: SktCh_55: kathaṃ mahārāja āgataḥ / hanta jāto 'syā niyamabhaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: How — the king has come! Alas, her observance is now broken.]
(The King approaches, signals the attendants away, takes the offering vessel himself, and presents it.)

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_56}*dinakarābhimukhī bhūtvā**
bhaavaṃ ambaramahāsarekkasahassapatta puvvadihāvahūmuhamaṇḍalakuṅkumavisesaa saalabhuaṇekkaraaṇappadība jaṃ ettha sibiṇaadaṃsaṇe kiṃ bi accāhidaṃ taṃ bhaavado paṇāmeṇa sabhāduassa ajjauttassa kusalapariṇāmi hodu* /arghyaṃ dattvā**
hañje taralie ubaṇehi me kusumāiṃ / abarāṇaṃ bi devadāṇaṃ sabariaṃ ṇivvattemi* /hastau prasārayati**
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: (Facing the Sun) O blessed one, sole thousand-petalled lotus of the great lake of the sky, special saffron-mark on the face of the bride of the eastern quarter, single jewel-lamp of all the worlds — whatever inauspicious thing appeared in my dream, may it, by obeisance to you, turn into well-being for my noble lord together with his brothers. <s>Taralikā</s>, bring me flowers, so that I may perform the worship of the other deities too. (She extends her hands, having offered the <s>arghya</s>.)

children.text: SktCh_56: bhagavannambaramahāsaraekasahasrapatra pūrvadiśāvadhūmukhamaṇḍalakuṅkumaviśeṣaka sakalabhuvanaikaratnapradīpa yadatra svapnadarśane kimapyatyāhitaṃ tadbhagavataḥ praṇāmena sabhrātṛkasyāryaputrasya kuśalapariṇāmi bhavatu / hañje taralike upanaya me kusumāni / aparāsāmapi devatānāṃ saparyāṃ nirvartayāmi /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: O blessed one, sole thousand-petalled lotus of the great lake of the sky, special saffron-mark on the face of the bride of the eastern quarter, single jewel-lamp of all the worlds — whatever inauspicious thing appeared in my dream, may it, by obeisance to you, turn into well-being for my noble lord together with his brothers. <s>Taralikā</s>, bring me flowers, so that I may perform the worship of the other deities too.]

children.text: *rājā puṣpāṇyupanayati sparśasukhamabhinīya ca kusumāni bhūmau pātayati**
children.translated_text: (The King offers the flowers. Having conveyed the pleasure of her touch, he drops the flowers on the ground.)

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_57}*saroṣam**
aho pamādo pariaṇassa* /parivṛtya dṛṣṭvā sasaṃbhramam**
kahaṃ ajjautto /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: (Angrily) What negligence of the attendants! (Turning and seeing, with alarm) How — my noble lord!
[Sanskrit rendering: What negligence of the attendants! How — my noble lord!]

children.text:
&rājā&:
devi anipuṇaḥ parijano 'yamevaṃvidhe sevāvakāśe / tatprabhavatyatrānuśāsane devī /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: My queen, these attendants are unskilled at such an occasion of service. In this matter, you have the authority to instruct them.
(<s>Bhānumatī</s> feigns embarrassment.)

children.text: vikira dhavaladīrghāpāṅgasaṃsarpi cakṣuḥ $ parijanapathavartinyatra kiṃ saṃbhrameṇa &
children.translated_text: Cast abroad your glance that glides in long white side-looks; why this alarm when attendants are nearby?

children.text: smitamadhuramudāraṃ devi māmālapoccaiḥ ē̃ prabhavati mama pāṇyorañjaliḥ sevituṃ tvām // 2.15 //
children.translated_text: Speak to me aloud, O queen, with a smile sweet and generous — my cupped palms are ready to serve you. (2.15)
<s>Rājā</s>: O beloved,

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_58}ajjautta abbhaṇuṇṇādāe tue atthi me kassiṃ bi ṇiame ahilāso /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Noble lord, with your permission, I wish to undertake a certain religious observance.

children.text: SktCh_58: āryaputra abhyanujñātāyāstvayāsti me kasminnapi niyame 'bhilāṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Noble lord, with your permission, I wish to undertake a certain religious observance.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
śrutavistāra evāsmi bhavatyāḥ svapnavṛttāntaṃ prati / tadalamevaṃ prakṛtisukumāramātmānaṃ khedayitum /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: I have already heard the full account of your dream. Enough — do not torment your naturally delicate self.

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_59}ajjautta adimettaṃ me saṅkā bāhei / tā aṇumaṇṇadu maṃ ajjautta /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Noble lord, excessive apprehension afflicts me. Therefore, let my noble lord give his consent.

children.text: SktCh_59: āryaputra atimātraṃ māṃ śaṅkā bādhate / tadanumanyatāṃ māmāryaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Noble lord, excessive apprehension afflicts me. Therefore, let my noble lord give his consent.]

children.text: kiṃ no vyāptadiśāṃ prakampitabhuvāmakṣauhiṇīnāṃ phalaṃ $ kiṃ droṇena kimaṅgarājaviśikhairevaṃ yadi klāmyasi &
children.translated_text: What is the use of the <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> (vast armies) that fill the directions and shake the earth? What of <s>Droṇa</s>? What of the arrows of the king of <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>)? — if you are to tremble so!

children.text: bhīru bhrātṛśatasya me bhujavanacchāyāṃ sukhopasthitā ē̃ tvaṃ duryodhanakesarīndragṛhiṇī śaṅkāspadaṃ kiṃ tava // 2.16 //
children.translated_text: Timid one, sheltered in the shade of the forest of arms of my hundred brothers, you, the consort of <s>Duryodhana</s> the lion-king — what ground have you for fear? (2.16)
<s>Rājā</s>: (Proudly) My queen, enough of this apprehension! Behold —

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_60}ajjautta ṇa hu kiṃ bi me saṅkākālaṇaṃ tumhesu saṇṇihidesu / kiṃ tu ajjauttassa evva maṇorahasaṃpattiṃ abhiṇandāmi /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Noble lord, truly I have no cause for apprehension while you are present. But I simply wish to celebrate the fulfillment of my noble lord's desires.

children.text: SktCh_60: āryaputra na khalu kimapi me śaṅkākāraṇaṃ yuṣmāsu saṃnihiteṣu / kiṃ tvāryaputrasyaiva manorathasaṃpattimabhinandāmi /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Noble lord, truly I have no cause for apprehension while you are present. But I simply wish to celebrate the fulfillment of my noble lord's desires.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
ayi sundari etāvanta eva manorathā yadahaṃ dayitayā saṃgataḥ svecchayā viharāmīti / paśya /
VERSE_2.17
premābaddhastimitanayanāpīyamānābjaśobhaṃ $ lajjāyogādaviśadakathaṃ mandamandasmitaṃ vā &
vaktrenduṃ te niyamamuṣitālaktakāgrādharaṃ vā / ē̃ pātuṃ vāñchā paramasulabhaṃ kiṃ nu duryodhanasya // 2.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: O beautiful one, my desires amount to no more than this — that I, united with my beloved, may sport at will. Behold! Your moon-face, gazed upon with eyes motionless in love's fixation, radiant with lotus-beauty, or your gentle, sweet smile dimmed by modesty, or your lips from which the lac-dye has been stripped by your vow — what is hard for <s>Duryodhana</s> to drink in, that is supremely easy to obtain? (2.17)
(A great commotion is heard offstage. All listen.)
<s>Bhānumatī</s>: (Embracing the King in fear) Protect me, protect me, noble lord!
[Sanskrit rendering: Protect me, protect me, noble lord!]

children.text: dikṣu vyūḍhāṅghripāṅgastṛṇajaṭilacalatpāṃśudaṇḍo 'ntarikṣe $ jhāṃkārī śarkarālaḥ pathiṣu viṭapināṃ skandhakāṣaiḥ sadhūmaḥ &
children.translated_text: In the quarters, thick with the dust raised by whirling grass and tree-roots, buzzing in the sky, rattling with gravel on the paths, smoking from the broken branches of trees,

children.text: prāsādānāṃ nikuñjeṣvabhinavajaladodgāragambhīradhīra- ē̃ ścaṇḍārambhaḥ samīro vahati paridiśaṃ bhīru kiṃ saṃbhrameṇa // 2.18 //
