children.translated_text: deep and steady as the outpouring of fresh rain-clouds in the groves near the palaces — a fierce gale blows across all directions. Timid one, why this alarm? (2.18)
<s>Rājā</s>: (Looking around) Beloved, enough of this alarm! Behold —

children.text:
&sakhī&:
{Pkt_62}mahārāo pavisadu edaṃ dārupavvaapāsādaṃ / uvveakārī khu aaṃ utthidaparusaraakalusīkidaṇaaṇo ummūlidataruvarasaddavittatthamandurāparibbhaṭṭhavallahatulaṃgamapajjāulīkidajaṇapaddhaī bhīsaṇo samīraṇāsāro /
children.translated_text: <s>Sakhī</s>: Let the king enter this wooden hilltop pavilion! For this fierce gust of wind is terrifying — it has muddied the eyes with harsh dust raised aloft, uprooted great trees whose crashing sounds have frightened the horses that have broken free from the stables, throwing the people's paths into confusion.

children.text: SktCh_62: mahārājaḥ praviśatvimaṃ dāruparvataprāsādam / udvegakārī khalvayamutthitaparuṣarajaḥkaluṣīkṛtanayana unmūlitataruvaraśabdavitrastamandurāparibhraṣṭavallabhaturaṃgamaparyākulīkṛtajanapaddhatirbhīṣaṇaḥ samīraṇāsāraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Let the king enter this wooden hilltop pavilion! For this fierce gust of wind is terrifying — it has muddied the eyes with harsh dust raised aloft, uprooted great trees whose crashing sounds have frightened the horses that have broken free from the stables, throwing the people's paths into confusion.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
*saharṣam**
upakāri khalvidaṃ vātyācakraṃ suyodhanasya / yasya prasādādayatnaparityaktaniyamayā devyā saṃpādito 'smanmanorathaḥ / kathamiti /
nyastā na bhrukuṭirna bāṣpasalilairācchādite locane $ nītaṃ nānanamanyataḥ saśapathaṃ nāhaṃ spṛśanvāritaḥ &
children.translated_text: No frown was set upon the brow, no eyes were veiled with tears, the face was not turned away, nor was I stopped with oaths when I touched her —

children.text: tanvyā magnapayodharaṃ bhayavaśādābaddhamāliṅgitaṃ ē̃ bhaṅktāsyā niyamasya bhīṣaṇamarunnāyaṃ vayasyo mama // 2.19 //
children.translated_text: the slender one, out of fear, gave a deep-bosomed, tight embrace; this fearsome wind, breaker of her vow, is my friend. (2.19)

<s>Rājā</s>: (Joyfully) This whirlwind is indeed helpful to <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>)! For by its grace, the Queen, having involuntarily abandoned her observance, has fulfilled my desire. How so?

children.text: tatsaṃpūrṇamanorathasya me kāmacāraḥ saṃprati vihāreṣu / tadito dāruparvataprāsādameva gacchāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: So, my desires being fully satisfied, I am now free to sport as I please. Let us then go to the wooden hilltop pavilion.
(All walk about carefully, miming the distress of the storm.)

children.text: kuru ghanoru padāni śanaiḥ śanairayi vimuñca gatiṃ parivepinīm /
children.translated_text: Step slowly, slowly with your broad thighs, O release this trembling gait!
If you fall, cling tightly to the vine of my arm — press firmly against my chest. (2.20)
<s>Rājā</s>:

children.text:
*praveśaṃ rūpayitvā**
priye alabdhāvakāśaḥ samīraṇaḥ saṃvṛtatvādgarbhagṛhasya / visrabdhamunmīlaya cakṣurunmṛṣṭareṇunikaram /
children.translated_text: (Miming entrance) Beloved, the wind has no access here, since the inner chamber is enclosed. Open your eyes freely, now that the dust has been wiped away.

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_63}*saharṣam**
diṭṭhiā iha dāva uppādasamīraṇo ṇa bādhedi /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: (Joyfully) Fortunately, the dreadful storm-wind does not afflict us here!
[Sanskrit rendering: Fortunately, the dreadful storm-wind does not afflict us here!]

children.text:
&sakhī&:
{Pkt_64}mahārāa ārohaṇasaṃbhamaṇissahaṃ piasahīe ūrujualaṃ / tā kīsa dāṇiṃ mahārāo āsaṇavediṃ ṇa bhūsedi /
children.translated_text: <s>Sakhī</s>: O king, the thighs of our dear friend are exhausted from the haste of climbing. Why then does the king not grace the seat-platform?

children.text: SktCh_64: mahārāja ārohaṇasaṃbhramaniḥsahaṃ priyasakhyā ūruyugalam / tatkasmādidānīṃ mahārāja āsanavedīṃ na bhūṣayati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: O king, the thighs of our dear friend are exhausted from the haste of climbing. Why then does the king not grace the seat-platform?]

children.text: reṇurbādhāṃ vidhatte tanurapi mahatīṃ netrayorāyatatvā- $ dutkampo 'lpo 'pi pīnastanabharitamuraḥ kṣiptahāraṃ dunoti &
children.translated_text: Even fine dust causes great distress to her long eyes; even a slight tremor, with her full breasts pressed against the chest, disrupts the necklace painfully;

children.text: ūrvormande 'pi yāte pṛthujaghanabharādvepathurvardhate 'syā ē̃ vātyā khedaṃ kṛśāṅgayāḥ suciramavayavairdattahastā karoti // 2.21 //
children.translated_text: even when the thighs move gently, the trembling increases from the weight of her broad hips — the storm, having seized each limb by the hand, inflicts prolonged suffering on this slender-bodied one. (2.21)
<s>Rājā</s>: (Looking at the Queen) My lady, no small harm has been done by the panic of the storm. For indeed —
(All sit down.)
The hem of your garment fluttering in the wind, that steals my gaze — your hip, my eye's beloved —

children.text: adhyāsituṃ tava ciraṃ jaghanasthalasya ē̃ paryāptameva karabhoru mamoruyugmam // 2.22 //
children.translated_text: for it to rest upon at length, O one of plantain-like thighs, my pair of thighs is quite sufficient. (2.22)
<s>Rājā</s>: Why then does the Queen sit upon this hard, uncovered stone surface?
(Enter [Chamberlain], bursting through the curtain in agitation.)
<s>Kañcukī</s> (Chamberlain): My lord — broken! Broken!
(All look on with anxiety.)
<s>Rājā</s>: What is it?
<s>Kañcukī</s>: Broken — by <s>Bhīma</s>!
<s>Rājā</s>: What! What are you babbling?
<s>Bhānumatī</s>: Sir, what calamity do you speak of?
[Sanskrit rendering: Sir, what calamity do you speak of?]
<s>Kañcukī</s>: (Fearfully) Indeed, broken by <s>Bhīma</s> — your —
<s>Rājā</s>: Shame on you, babbling old fool! What is this delusion of yours today?

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
deva na khalu kaścidvyāmohaḥ / satyameva bravīmi /

children.translated_text: Broken by <s>Bhīma</s> — the wind — is your chariot-banner,
which has fallen to the ground, its jingling bells crying out as if in lamentation. (2.23)
<s>Kañcukī</s>: My lord, there is no delusion at all. I speak the plain truth.

children.text:
&rājā&:
balavatsamīraṇavegātkampite bhuvane bhagnaḥ syandanaketuḥ / tatkimityuddhataṃ pralapasi bhagnaṃ bhagnamiti /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: The chariot-banner was broken by the powerful force of the wind shaking the earth! Then why do you babble in this excited manner, crying "Broken! Broken!"?

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
deva na kiṃcit / kiṃ tu śamanārthamasyānimittasya vijñāpayitavyo deva iti svāmibhaktirmāṃ mukharayati /
children.translated_text: <s>Kañcukī</s>: My lord, it is nothing. But to propitiate this evil omen, I thought my lord should be informed — it is my devotion to my master that makes me speak out.

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_66}ajjautta pariharīadu edaṃ aṇimittaṃ pasaṇṇabamhaṇaveāṇughoseṇa homeṇa a /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Noble lord, let this evil omen be averted by the chanting of satisfied <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> reciting the <s>Vedas</s>, and by a fire-offering.

children.text: SktCh_66: āryaputra parihāryatāmetadanimittaṃ prasannabrāhmaṇavedānughoṣeṇa homena ca /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Noble lord, let this evil omen be averted by the chanting of satisfied <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> reciting the <s>Vedas</s>, and by a fire-offering.]
<s>Rājā</s>: (Dismissively) Go then! Inform the royal priest <s>Sumitra</s>.
<s>Kañcukī</s>: As my lord commands. (Exit)
(Enter [Doorkeeper])

children.text:
&pratīhārī&:
{Pkt_67}*sodvegamupasṛtya**
jaadu jaadu mahārāo / mahārāa esā khu jāmāduṇo sindhurāassa mādā dussalā a paḍihārabhūmīe ciṭṭhadi /
children.translated_text: <s>Pratīhārī</s> (Doorkeeper): (Approaching with agitation) Victory, victory to the great king! My lord, the mother of your son-in-law, the king of <s>Sindhu</s>, and <s>Duḥśalā</s> are waiting at the door.

children.text: SktCh_67: jayatu jayatu mahārājaḥ / mahārāja eṣā khalu jāmātuḥ sindhurājasya mātā duḥśalā ca pratīhārabhūmau tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Victory, victory to the great king! My lord, the mother of your son-in-law, the king of <s>Sindhu</s>, and <s>Duḥśalā</s> are waiting at the door.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
*kiṃcidvicintyātmagatam**
kiṃ jayadrathamātā duḥśalā ceti / kaccidabhimanyuvadhāmarṣitaiḥ pāṇḍuputrairna kiṃcidatyāhitamāceṣṭitaṃ bhavet* /prakāśam**
gaccha / praveśaya śīghram /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: (Reflecting briefly, aside) What — <s>Jayadratha</s>'s mother and <s>Duḥśalā</s>? Could it be that the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, enraged by the slaying of <s>Abhimanyu</s>, have committed some terrible act? (Aloud) Go! Bring them in at once.
<s>Pratīhārī</s>: As the great king commands. (Exit)
[Sanskrit rendering: As the great king commands.]

children.text: *tataḥ praviśati saṃbhrāntā jayadrathamātā duḥśalā ca / ubhe sāsraṃ duryodhanasya pādayoḥ patataḥ**
children.translated_text: (Then enter, in agitation, <s>Jayadratha</s>'s mother and <s>Duḥśalā</s>. Both fall weeping at <s>Duryodhana</s>'s feet.)
<s>Mātā</s> (Mother): Save us, save us, O Lord of the <s>Kurus</s>!
[Sanskrit rendering: Save us, save us, O Lord of the <s>Kurus</s>!]
(<s>Duḥśalā</s> weeps.)

children.text:
&rājā&:
*sasaṃbhramamutthāpya**
amba samāśvasihi samāśvasihi / kimatyāhitam / api kuśalaṃ samarāṅgaṇeṣvapratirathasya jayadrathasya /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: (Raising them up anxiously) Mother, compose yourself, compose yourself! What calamity has occurred? Is all well with <s>Jayadratha</s>, who is unrivaled on the battlefield?
<s>Mātā</s>: Son, how can all be well?
[Sanskrit rendering: Son, how can all be well?]
<s>Rājā</s>: How so?

children.text:
&mātā&:
{Pkt_71}*sāśaṅkam**
ajja khu puttavahāmarisuddībideṇa gaṇḍīviṇā aṇatthamide diasaṇāhe tassa vaho paḍiṇṇādo /
children.translated_text: <s>Mātā</s>: (With apprehension) Today, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), inflamed with fury over the slaying of his son, has vowed at sunset to kill him.

children.text: SktCh_71: adya khalu putravadhāmarṣoddīpitena gāṇḍīvinānastamite divasanāthe tasya vadhaḥ pratijñātaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Today, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, inflamed with fury over the slaying of his son, has vowed at sunset to kill him.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
*sasmitam**
idaṃ tadaśrukāraṇamambāyā duḥśalāyāśca / putraśokādunmattasya kirīṭinaḥ pralāpairevamavasthā / aho mugdhatvamabalānām / amba kṛtaṃ viṣādena / vatse duḥśale alamaśrupātena / kutaścāyaṃ tasya dhanaṃjayasya prabhāvo duryodhanabāhuparigharakṣitasya mahārathajayadrathasya vipattimutpādayitum /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: (Smiling) So this is the cause of Mother's and <s>Duḥśalā</s>'s tears! These are but the ravings of <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), maddened by grief for his son — such is the state of affairs. How naive are these women! Mother, enough of despair. Dear <s>Duḥśalā</s>, enough of tears. For what power has that <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> to bring about the downfall of the great warrior <s>Jayadratha</s>, who is protected by the iron bar of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s arms?
<s>Mātā</s>: Son, the heroes march forth, heedless of their own bodies, their fury kindled by the slaughter of their sons and kinsmen.

children.text: SktCh_72: jāta putrabandhuvadhāmarṣoddīpitakopānalā anapekṣitaśarīrā vīrāḥ parikrāmanti /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Son, the heroes march forth, heedless of their own bodies, their fury kindled by the slaughter of their sons and kinsmen.]

children.text: hastākṛṣṭavilolakeśavasanā duḥśāsanenājñayā $ pāñcālī mama rājacakrapurato gaurgauriti vyāhṛtā &
children.translated_text: <s>Pāñcālī</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>) was dragged by her hair and garments by <s>Duḥśāsana</s> at my command, and called a common woman — 'Go! Go!' — before my royal court.

children.text: tasminneva sa kiṃ nu gāṇḍivadharo nāsītpṛthānandano ē̃ yūnaḥ kṣatriyavaṃśajasya kṛtinaḥ krodhāspadaṃ kiṃ na tat // 2.24 //
children.translated_text: Was not that son of <s>Pṛthā</s>, the bearer of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, present then? For a young man born of a warrior lineage and accomplished, would that not be cause for wrath? (2.24)
<s>Rājā</s>: (With a mocking smile) Just so! The wrath of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> is well known to all. Behold —
<s>Mātā</s>: He who has not yet fulfilled the burden of his vow has vowed to kill himself if he fails.
[Sanskrit rendering: He who has not yet fulfilled the burden of his vow has vowed to kill himself if he fails.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
yadyevamalamānandasthāne 'pi te viṣādena / nanu vaktavyamutsannaḥ sānujo yudhiṣṭhira iti / anyacca mātaḥ kā śaktirasti dhanaṃjayasyānyasya vā kuruśataparivāravardhitamahimnaḥ kṛpakarṇadroṇāśvatthāmādimahārathadviguṇīkṛtanirāvaraṇavikramasya nāmāpi grahītuṃ te tanayasya / ayi sutaparākramānabhijñe
dharmātmajaṃ prati yamau ca kathaiva nāsti $ madhye vṛkodarakirīṭabhṛtorbalena &
children.translated_text: Against <s>Dharmātmaja</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) and the twin sons of <s>Mādrī</s>, there is no contest at all; and amidst <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) and <s>Kirīṭabhṛt</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), through strength alone,

children.text: eko 'pi visphuritamaṇḍalacāpacakraṃ ē̃ kaḥ sindhurājamabhiṣeṇayituṃ samarthaḥ // 2.25 //
children.translated_text: who, even singly, could dare to assail the king of <s>Sindhu</s> with the whirling circle of his flashing bow? (2.25)

<s>Rājā</s>: If that is so, then you should cease your despair, for there is cause for joy, not sorrow! Should one not rather say, "<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> along with his brothers is finished"? And besides, Mother, what power has <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, or anyone else, to even utter the name of your son — whose glory is magnified by the retinue of a hundred <s>Kuru</s> princes, whose matchless valor is doubled by the great warriors <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Aśvatthāman</s> and others? O you who do not know your son's prowess —

children.text:
&bhānumatī&:
{Pkt_74}ajjautta jai bi evvaṃ taha bi gurukidapaḍiṇṇābharo dhaṇaṃjao ṇidāṇaṃ kkhu saṃkāe /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānumatī</s>: Noble lord, even if it be so, still <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, bearing the heavy burden of his solemn vow, is surely cause for apprehension.

children.text: SktCh_74: āryaputra yadyapyevaṃ tathāpi gurukṛtapratijñābharo dhanaṃjayaḥ nidānaṃ khalu śaṅkāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Noble lord, even if it be so, still <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, bearing the heavy burden of his solemn vow, is surely cause for apprehension.]
<s>Mātā</s>: Daughter, you have spoken well and suitably for the occasion.

children.text: SktCh_75: jāte sādhu kālocitaṃ tvayā mantritam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Daughter, you have spoken well and suitably for the occasion.]

children.text:
&rājā&:
āḥ mamāpi nāma duryodhanasya śaṅkāsthānaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ / paśya /

children.translated_text: With warriors innumerable, their limbs scarred by bowstring-marks, their bodies freed from armor, their parasols overlapping one another, creating the illusion of a white lotus-forest,

children.text: reṇugrastārkabhāsāṃ pracaladasilatādanturāṇāṃ balānā- ē̃ mākrāntā bhrātṛbhirme diśi diśi samare koṭayaḥ saṃpatanti // 2.26 //
children.translated_text: obscuring the light of the sun with dust, their swords glinting and formidable — the battle-divisions, led by my brothers, swarm in every direction, charging into the fray. (2.26)
<s>Rājā</s>: What! Are the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> truly cause for apprehension even for <s>Duryodhana</s>? Behold —

children.text: api ca bhānumati vijñātapāṇḍavaprabhāve kiṃ tvamapyevamāśaṅkase / paśya /
duḥśāsanasya hṛdayakṣatajāmbupāne $ duryodhanasya ca yathā gadayorubhaṅge &
children.translated_text: Just as the vow of the valorous <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> stands regarding the drinking of blood from <s>Duḥśāsana</s>'s chest-wound and the breaking of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s thighs with a mace,

children.text: tejasvināṃ samaramūrdhani pāṇḍavānāṃ ē̃ jñeyā jayadrathavadhe 'pi tathā pratijñā // 2.27 //
children.translated_text: so too should their vow regarding the slaying of <s>Jayadratha</s> be understood — on the battlefield of the mighty. (2.27)
And besides, <s>Bhānumatī</s>, you who know the prowess of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> — do you too harbor such fears? Behold —

children.text: kaḥ ko 'tra bhoḥ / jaitraṃ me rathamupakalpaya tāvat / yāvadahamapi tasya pragalbhapāṇḍavasya jayadrathaparirakṣaṇenaiva mithyāpratijñāvailakṣyasaṃpāditamaśastrapūtaṃ maraṇamupadiśāmi /
children.translated_text: Who goes there? Prepare my victory-chariot at once! I too shall teach that presumptuous <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, by protecting <s>Jayadratha</s> himself, a death unpurified by weapons — the shame of a false vow!
(Enter [Chamberlain])
With golden bells jingling at the strike, with <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) doubly streaming and billowing,

children.text: sajjo 'yaṃ niyamitavalgitākulāśvaḥ ē̃ śatrūṇāṃ kṣapitamanoratho rathaste // 2.28 //
children.translated_text: ready, with its restive horses reined in — this chariot of yours, destroyer of enemies' hopes, awaits. (2.28)
<s>Kañcukī</s>: My lord —

children.text:
&rājā&:
devi praviśa tvamabhyantarameva* /yāvadahamapi tasya pragalbhapāṇḍavasya ityādi paṭhanparikrāmati**
children.translated_text: <s>Rājā</s>: My queen, retire within. (He walks about, reciting "I too shall teach that presumptuous <s>Pāṇḍava</s>...")
(Exeunt all.)

Thus ends the Second Act.
ACT 3
The Third Act.
(Then enters a <s>Rākṣasī</s> (demoness) in a grotesque costume.)
<s>Rākṣasī</s>: (Laughing grotesquely, with satisfaction)
With thousands of pots filled with the fat of slain human flesh,

children.text: aṇiśaṃ a pibāmi śoṇiaṃ valiśaśadaṃ śamale huvīadu // 3.1 //
children.translated_text: and drinking blood ceaselessly — may the war last a hundred years! (3.1)

children.text:
{Pkt_77}*nṛtyantī saparitoṣam**
jai śindhulāavahadiahe via diahe diahe śamalakamma paḍibajjai ajjuṇe tado pajjattabhalidakoṭṭhāgāle maṃśaśoṇiehiṃ me gehe huvīadi* /parikramya diśo 'valokya**
aha kahiṃ ṇu khu luhilappie huvīadi / tā jāva imaśśiṃ śamale piabhattālaṃ luhilappiaṃ aṇṇeśāmi* /parikramya**
hodu śaddābaiśśaṃ dāva / ale luhilappiā luhilappiā ido ehi ido ehi /
children.translated_text: (Dancing with delight) If every day battle-deeds occur as on the day of the <s>Sindhu</s> king's slaying, then my house will be a well-stocked granary of flesh and blood! (Walking about, looking in all directions) Now where might <s>Rudhirapriya</s> (Blood-lover) be? Let me search for my dear husband <s>Rudhirapriya</s> on this battlefield. (Walking about) Well, let me call out then. Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>! <s>Rudhirapriya</s>! Come here, come here!

children.text: SktCh_76: hatamānuṣamāṃsabhārake kumbhasahasravasābhiḥ saṃcite / aniśaṃ ca pibāmi śoṇitaṃ varṣaśataṃ samaro bhavatu // 1 //
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: With thousands of pots filled with the fat of slain human flesh, and drinking blood ceaselessly — may the war last a hundred years! (1)]

children.text: SktCh_77: yadi sindhurājavadhadivasa iva divase divase samarakarma pratipadyate 'rjunastadā paryāptabhṛtakoṣṭhāgāraṃ māṃsaśoṇitairme gṛhaṃ bhaviṣyati / atha kva nu khalu rudhirapriyo bhaviṣyati / tadyāvadetasminsamare priyabhartāraṃ rudhirapriyamanveṣyāmi / bhavatu śabdāyiṣye tāvat / are rudhirapriya rudhirapriya ita ehīta ehi /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: If every day battle-deeds occur as on the day of the <s>Sindhu</s> king's slaying, then my house will be a well-stocked granary of flesh and blood. Now where might <s>Rudhirapriya</s> be? Let me search for my dear husband <s>Rudhirapriya</s> on this battlefield. Well, let me call out then. Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>! <s>Rudhirapriya</s>! Come here, come here!]
(Then enters a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) of similar appearance.)
<s>Rākṣasa</s>: (Miming fatigue)

children.text: paccaggahadāṇaṃ maṃśae jai uṇhe luhile a lambhai /
children.translated_text: If one could obtain fresh flesh of the newly slain, and warm blood,

children.text: tā eśe maha paliśśame khaṇamettaṃ evva lahu ṇaśśai // 3.2 //
children.translated_text: then this weariness of mine would vanish in just a moment. (3.2)

children.text: SktCh_78: pratyagrahatānāṃ māṃsaṃ yadyuṣṇaṃ rudhiraṃ ca labhyeta / tadeṣa mama pariśramaḥ kṣaṇamātrameva laghu naśyet // 2 //
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: If one could obtain fresh flesh of the newly slain, and warm blood, then this weariness of mine would vanish in just a moment. (2)]
(The <s>Rākṣasī</s> calls out again.)

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_79}*ākarṇya**
ale ke eśe maṃ saddābedi* /vilokya**
kahaṃ piā me vaśāgandhā* /upasṛtya**
vaśāgandhe kīśa maṃ śaddābeśi /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>: (Hearing) Ho, who is calling me? (Looking) Why, it is my beloved <s>Vasāgandhā</s> (Fat-scented one)! (Approaching) <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, why do you call me?
O beloved, drunk on the wine of blood, stumbling as you wander the battlefield,

children.text: śaddāaśi kīśa maṃ pie puliśaśahaśśaṃ hadaṃ śuṇīadi // 3.3 //
children.translated_text: why do you call me? A thousand warriors have been slain, I hear! (3.3)

children.text: SktCh_79: are kaiṣā māṃ śabdāyate / kathaṃ priyā me vasāgandhā / vasāgandhe kasmānmāṃ śabdāyase /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Ho, who is calling me? Why, it is my beloved <s>Vasāgandhā</s>! <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, why do you call me?]

children.text: SktCh_80: rudhirāsavapānamattike raṇahiṇḍanaskhaladgātrike / śabdāyase kasmānmāṃ priye puruṣasahasraṃ hataṃ śrūyate // 3 //
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: O beloved, drunk on the wine of blood, stumbling as you wander the battlefield, why do you call me? A thousand warriors have been slain, I hear! (3)]

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_81}ale luhilappiā edaṃ kkhu mae tuha kālaṇādo paccaggahadaśśa kaśśa bi lāeśiṇo pahūdavaśāśiṇehacikkaṇaṃ koṇhaṃ ṇavaluhilaṃ aggamaṃśaṃ a āṇīdaṃ / tā pibāhi ṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasī</s>: Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>! On your account I have brought fresh warm blood from some just-slain prince, rich and smooth with abundant fat, along with the choicest flesh. Now drink!

children.text: SktCh_81: are rudhirapriya idaṃ khalu mayā tava kāraṇātpratyagrahatasya kasyāpi rājarṣeḥ prabhūtavasāsnehacikkaṇaṃ koṣṇaṃ navarudhiramagramāṃsaṃ cānītam / tatpibaitat /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>! On your account I have brought fresh warm blood from some just-slain prince, rich and smooth with abundant fat, along with the choicest flesh. Now drink!]

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_82}*saparitoṣam**
śāhu vaśāgandhe śāhu / śohaṇaṃ tue kidaṃ / baliamhi pibāśide / tā ubaṇehi /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>: (With delight) Well done, <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, well done! Excellent is what you have done. I am exceedingly thirsty. Bring it here!

children.text: SktCh_82: sādhu vasāgandhe sādhu / śobhanaṃ tvayā kṛtam / balavadasmi pipāsitaḥ / tadupanaya /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Well done, <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, well done! Excellent is what you have done. I am exceedingly thirsty. Bring it here!]

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_83}ale luhilappiā ediśe hadaṇalagaatulaṃgamaśoṇiavaśāśamuddaduśśaṃcale śamalāṅgaṇe paḍibbhamante tumaṃ pibāśie śi tti accaliaṃ accaliaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasī</s>: Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, on such a battlefield, impassable with the blood and fat of slain men, elephants, and horses — that you are thirsty while wandering here is truly astonishing, most astonishing!

children.text: SktCh_83: are rudhirapriya īdṛśe hatanaragajaturaṃgamaśoṇitavasāsamudraduḥsaṃcare samarāṅgaṇe paribhramaṃstvaṃ pipāsito 'sītyāścaryamāścaryam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, on such a battlefield, impassable with the blood and fat of slain men, elephants, and horses — that you are thirsty while wandering here is truly astonishing, most astonishing!]

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_84}ai śutthide ṇaṃ puttaśoaśaṃtattahiaaṃ śāmiṇiṃ hiḍimbādeiṃ pekkhiduṃ gadamhi /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>: O well-settled one, I had gone to see our mistress, Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, whose heart is scorched by grief for her son.

children.text: SktCh_84: ayi susthite nanu putraśokasaṃtaptahṛdayāṃ svāminīṃ hiḍimbādevīṃ prekṣituṃ gato 'smi /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: O well-settled one, I had gone to see our mistress, Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, whose heart is scorched by grief for her son.]

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_85}luhilappiā ajja bi śāmiṇīe hiḍimbādeīe ghaḍukkaaśoe ṇa ubaśammadi /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasī</s>: <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, even today our mistress Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s>'s grief for <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> has not subsided.

children.text: SktCh_85: radhirapriya adyāpi svāminyā hiḍimbādevyā ghaṭotkacaśoko nopaśāmyati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, even today our mistress Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s>'s grief for <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s> has not subsided.]

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_86}vaśāgandhe kudo śe ubaśame / kevalaṃ ahimaṇṇuvahaśoaśamāṇadukkhāe śubhaddādevīe jaṇṇaśeṇīe a kadhaṃ kadhaṃ vi śamāśāśīadi /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>: <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, how can her grief subside? She is somehow consoled only by Queen <s>Subhadrā</s> and <s>Yājñasenī</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>), who share the same sorrow over <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s death.

children.text: SktCh_86: vasāgandhe kuto 'syā upaśamaḥ / kevalamabhimanyuvadhaśokasamānaduḥkhayā subhadrādevyā yājñasenyā ca kathaṃ kathamapi samāśvāsyate /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, how can her grief subside? She is somehow consoled only by Queen <s>Subhadrā</s> and <s>Yājñasenī</s>, who share the same sorrow over <s>Abhimanyu</s>'s death.]

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_87}luhilappiā geṇha edaṃ hatthiśilakabālaśaṃciaṃ aggamaṃśobadaṃśaṃ / pibāhi ṇavaśoṇiāsavaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasī</s>: <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, take this — choice flesh served in an elephant's skull-cup, heaped high. Drink the fresh blood-wine!
[Sanskrit rendering: <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, take this — choice flesh served in an elephant's skull-cup, heaped high. Drink the fresh blood-wine!]

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_88}*tathā kṛtvā**
vaśāgandhe aha kiappahūdaṃ tue śaṃciaṃ luhilaṃ aggamaṃśaṃ a /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>: (Having done so) <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, how much blood and choice flesh have you collected?

children.text: SktCh_88: vasāgandhe atha kiyatprabhūtaṃ tvayā saṃcitaṃ rudhiramagramāṃsaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, how much blood and choice flesh have you collected?]

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_89}ale luhilappiā puvvaśaṃciaṃ jāṇāśi jevva tumaṃ / ṇavaśaṃciaṃ śiṇu dāva / bhaadattaśoṇiakumbhe śindhulāavaśākumbhe duve dubadamacchāhibabhūliśśavaśomadattabalhīappamuhāṇaṃ ṇalindāṇaṃ aṇṇāṇaṃ bi pākidapuliśāṇaṃ luhilavaśāmaṃśaśśa ghaḍā abiṇaddhamuhā śahaśśaśaṃkkhā śanti me gehe /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasī</s>: Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, you know well the old stock. Now hear of the new collection: a pot of <s>Bhagadatta</s>'s blood, two pots of the <s>Sindhu</s> king's fat, and of <s>Drupada</s>, the lord of <s>Matsya</s>, <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, <s>Somadatta</s>, <s>Bālhīka</s> and other kings, and also of common soldiers — thousands of sealed jars of blood, fat, and flesh are stored in my house.

children.text: SktCh_89: are rudhirapriya pūrvasaṃcitaṃ jānāsyeva tvam / navasaṃcitaṃ śṛṇu tāvat / bhagadattaśoṇitakumbhaḥ sindhurājavasākumbhau dvau drupadamatsyādhipabhūriśravaḥsomadattabālhīkapramukhāṇāṃ narendrāṇāmanyeṣāmapi prākṛtapuruṣāṇāṃ rudhiravasāmāṃsasya ghaṭā apinaddhamukhāḥ sahasrasaṃkhyāḥ santi me gehe /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Ho, <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, you know well the old stock. Now hear of the new collection: a pot of <s>Bhagadatta</s>'s blood, two pots of the <s>Sindhu</s> king's fat, and of <s>Drupada</s>, the lord of <s>Matsya</s>, <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, <s>Somadatta</s>, <s>Bālhīka</s> and other kings, and also of common soldiers — thousands of sealed jars of blood, fat, and flesh are stored in my house.]

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_90}*saparitoṣamāliṅgya**
śāhu śugghaliṇīe śāhu / imiṇā de śugghaliṇitteṇa ajja uṇa śāmiṇīe hiḍimbādevīe śaṃvihāṇeṇa a paṇaṭṭhaṃ me jammadāliddaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>: (Embracing her with delight) Well done, O good housewife, well done! By your excellent housekeeping, and by the arrangements of our mistress Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, the poverty of my birth has been destroyed today!

children.text: SktCh_90: sādhu sugṛhiṇi sādhu / anena te sugṛhiṇītvenādya punaḥ svāminyā hiḍimbādevyāḥ saṃvidhānena ca pranaṣṭaṃ me janmadāridryam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: Well done, O good housewife, well done! By your excellent housekeeping, and by the arrangements of our mistress Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, the poverty of my birth has been destroyed today!]
<s>Rākṣasī</s>: <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, what arrangement has our mistress made?

children.text: SktCh_91: rudhirapriya kīdṛśaṃ svāminyā saṃvidhānaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: <s>Rudhirapriya</s>, what arrangement has our mistress made?]

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_92}vaśāgandhe ajja kkhu ahaṃ śāmiṇīe hiḍimbādevīe śavahumāṇaṃ śaddābia āṇatte jaha luhilappiā ajja pahudi tue ajjauttaśśa bhīmaśeṇaśśa piṭṭhadoṇupiṭṭhaṃ śamale āhiṇḍidavvaṃ tti / tā taśśa aṇumaggagāmiṇo hadamāṇuśaśoṇiaṇaīdaṃśaṇappaṇaṭṭhabubhukkhāpibāśaśśa iha evva me śaggaloo huvīadi / tumaṃ bi viśśaddhā bhavia luhilavaśāhiṃ kumbhaśahaśśaṃ śaṃcehi /
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasa</s>: <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, today our mistress Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s> has respectfully summoned me and commanded: "<s>Rudhirapriya</s>, from today onward you must follow close behind the noble lord <s>Bhīmasena</s> on the battlefield." Therefore, following in his wake, seeing the rivers of blood flowing from the humans he has slain, my hunger and thirst will vanish — this very place shall be my heaven! And you too, be at ease and collect a thousand pots of blood and fat.

children.text: SktCh_92: vasāgandhe adya khalvahaṃ svāminyā hiḍimbādevyā sabahumānaṃ śabdāyyājñapto yathā rudhirapriya adya prabhṛti tvayāryaputrasya bhīmasenasya pṛṣṭhato 'nupṛṣṭhaṃ samara āhiṇḍitavyamiti / tattasyānumārgagāmino hatamānuṣaśoṇitanadīdarśanapranaṣṭabubhukṣāpipāsasyehaiva me svargaloko bhaviṣyati / tvamapi visrabdhā bhūtvā rudhiravasābhiḥ kumbhasahasraṃ saṃcinu /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: <s>Vasāgandhā</s>, today our mistress Queen <s>Hiḍimbā</s> has respectfully summoned me and commanded: "<s>Rudhirapriya</s>, from today onward you must follow close behind the noble lord <s>Bhīmasena</s> on the battlefield." Therefore, following in his wake, seeing the rivers of blood flowing from the humans he has slain, my hunger and thirst will vanish — this very place shall be my heaven! And you too, be at ease and collect a thousand pots of blood and fat.]

The <s>Rākṣasī</s> (demoness):
(Prakrit) O blood-lover, for what reason are you following closely behind prince <s>Bhīmasena</s>?
Sanskrit chāyā: O blood-lover, for what reason are you following closely behind prince <s>Bhīmasena</s>?

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_94}vaśāgandhe teṇa hi śāmiṇā viodaleṇa duśśāśaṇaśśa luhilaṃ pāduṃ paḍiṇṇādaṃ / taṃ ca amhehiṃ lakkhaśehiṃ aṇuppaviśia pādavvaṃ tti /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon):
(Prakrit) O fat-scented one, our master <s>Vṛkodara</s> (Bhīma) has vowed to drink the blood of <s>Duḥśāsana</s>. And we <s>Rākṣasas</s> must follow along and drink it too.

children.text: SktCh_94: vasāgandhe tena hi svāminā vṛkodareṇa duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ pātuṃ pratijñātam / taccāsmābhī rākṣasairanupraviśya pātavyamiti /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: O fat-scented one, our master <s>Vṛkodara</s> has vowed to drink the blood of <s>Duḥśāsana</s>. And we <s>Rākṣasas</s> must follow along and drink it too.

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_95}*saharṣam**
śāhu śāmiṇi śāhu / śuśaṃvihāṇe me bhattā tue kade /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasī</s>:
*(with delight)*
Well done, my lord, well done! You have made good provision for my husband.

children.text: SktCh_95: sādhu svāmini sādhu / susaṃvidhāno me bhartā tvayā kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Well done, my lord, well done! You have made good provision for my husband.
*(A great tumult is heard offstage. Both listen attentively.)*

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_96}*ākarṇya sasaṃbhramam**
ale luhilappiā kiṃ ṇu kkhu eśe mahante kalaale śuṇīadi /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasī</s>:
*(hearing it, in alarm)*
Hey, blood-lover, what is this great tumult that is heard?

children.text: SktCh_96: are rudhirapriya kiṃ nu khalveṣa mahānkalakalaḥ śrūyate /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Hey, blood-lover, what indeed is this great tumult that is heard?

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_97}*dṛṣṭvā**
vaśāgandhe eśe kkhu dhiṭṭhajjuṇṇeṇa doṇe keśeśu ākiṭṭhia aśibatteṇa vābādīadi /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasa</s>:
*(looking)*
O fat-scented one, here <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> is dragging <s>Droṇa</s> by the hair and slaying him with the edge of his sword!

children.text: SktCh_97: vasāgandhe eṣa khalu dhṛṣṭadyumnena droṇaḥ keśeṣvākṛṣyāsipatreṇa vyāpādyate /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: O fat-scented one, here <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> is dragging <s>Droṇa</s> by the hair and slaying him with the edge of his sword!

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_98}*saharṣam**
luhilappiā ehi / gacchia doṇaśśa luhilaṃ pivamha /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasī</s>:
*(with delight)*
Blood-lover, come! Let us go and drink <s>Droṇa</s>'s blood!

children.text: SktCh_98: rudhirapriya ehi / gatvā droṇasya rudhiraṃ pibāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Blood-lover, come! Let us go and drink <s>Droṇa</s>'s blood!

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_99}*sabhayam**
vaśāgandhe bamhaṇaśoṇiaṃ kkhu edaṃ galaaṃ dahante dahante paviśadi / tā kiṃ ediṇā /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasa</s>:
*(fearfully)*
O fat-scented one, this is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s blood! It enters the throat burning and burning. So what use is it?

children.text: SktCh_99: vasāgandhe brāhmaṇaśoṇitaṃ khalvetadgalaṃ dahaddahatpraviśati / tatkimetena /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: O fat-scented one, this is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s blood! It enters the throat burning and burning. So what use is it?
*(Again a tumult offstage.)*

children.text:
&rākṣasī&:
{Pkt_100}luhilappiā puṇo bi eśe mahante kalaale śuṇīadi /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasī</s>:
(Prakrit) Blood-lover, again this great tumult is heard!
Sanskrit chāyā: Blood-lover, again this great tumult is heard!

children.text:
&rākṣasaḥ&:
{Pkt_101}vaśāgandhe eśe kkhu aśśatthāme ākiṭṭhidāśibatte ido evva āacchadi / kadā bi dubadasudalośeṇa amhe bi vābādaiśśadi / tā ehi / atikkamamha /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Rākṣasa</s>:
(Prakrit) O fat-scented one, here <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, with drawn sword, is coming this very way! Perhaps in his rage at <s>Drupada</s>'s son he may slay us too. So come! Let us get out of the way.

children.text: SktCh_101: vasāgandhe eṣa khalvaśvatthāmākṛṣṭāsipatra ita evāgacchati / kadāciddrupadasutaroṣeṇāvāmapi vyāpādayiṣyati / tadehi / atikramāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: O fat-scented one, here <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, with drawn sword, is coming this very way! Perhaps in his rage at <s>Drupada</s>'s son he may slay us too. So come, let us get out of the way.
*(Thus they both exit.)*
End of the interlude.
*(Then enters <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, with sword drawn, listening to the tumult.)*
(Verse 3.4)
This roar, terrifying to the ears, filling the caverns of the sky,

children.text: ravaḥ śravaṇabhairavaḥ sthagitarodasīkandaraḥ ē̃ kuto 'dya samarodadherayamabhūtapūrvaḥ puraḥ // 3.4 //
children.translated_text: echoing again and again like the fierce thunder of <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> clouds churned by the winds of the great dissolution — whence has this unprecedented war-cry arisen today? (3.4)
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:

children.text:
*vicintya**
dhruvaṃ gāṇḍīvinā sātyakinā vṛkodareṇa vā yauvanadarpādatikrāntamaryādena parikopitastātaḥ samullaṅghya śiṣyapriyatāmātmaprabhāvasadṛśamāceṣṭate / tathā hi

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.5)

children.text: yadduryodhanapakṣapātasadṛśaṃ yuktaṃ yadastragrahe $ rāmāllabdhasamastahetiguruṇo vīryasya yatsāṃpratam &
children.translated_text: That which befits his partisanship toward <s>Duryodhana</s>, that which is fitting for one who is master of all weapons,

children.text: loke sarvadhanuṣmatāmadhipateryaccānurūpaṃ ruṣaḥ ē̃ prārabdhaṃ ripughasmareṇa niyataṃ tatkarma tātena me // 3.5 //
children.translated_text: who received the totality of arms from <s>Rāma</s> (Paraśurāma), who is the lord of all archers in the world — and that which is worthy of his wrath — surely my father, the devourer of foes, has undertaken that very deed. (3.5)

*(reflecting)*
Surely my father, provoked beyond all bounds by the youthful arrogance of <s>Gāṇḍīvin</s> (Arjuna), or <s>Sātyaki</s>, or <s>Vṛkodara</s> (Bhīma), has cast aside his affection for pupils and is displaying prowess befitting his own power. For indeed —

children.text:
*pṛṣṭhato vilokya**
tadalamidānīṃ mama rathapratīkṣayānayā / saśastra evāsmi sajalajaladharaprabhābhāsureṇa supragrahavimalakaladhautatsaruṇāmunā khaḍgena / yāvatsamarabhuvamavatarāmi* /parikramya / vāmākṣispandanaṃ sūcayitvā**
āḥ kathaṃ mamāpi nāmāśvatthāmnaḥ samaramahotsavapramodanirbharasya tātavikramadarśanalālasasyānimittāni samaragamanavighnamutpādayanti / bhavatu gacchāmi* /sāvaṣṭambhaṃ parikramyāgrato vilokya**
kathamavadhīritakṣātradharmāṇāmujjhitasatpuruṣocitalajjāvaguṇṭhanānāṃ vismṛtasvāmisatkāralaghucetasāṃ dviradaturaṃgamacaraṇacāriṇāmagaṇitakulayaśaḥsadṛśaparākramavratānāṃ raṇabhūmeḥ samantādapakrāmatāmayaṃ mahānnādo balānām* /nirūpya**
hā dhikkaṣṭam / kathamete mahārathāḥ karṇādayo 'pi samarātparāṅmukhā bhavanti / kathaṃ nu tātādhiṣṭhitānāmapi balānāmiyamavasthā bhavet / bhavatu saṃstambhayāmi / bho bhoḥ kauravasenāsamudravelāparipālanamahāmahīdharā narapatayaḥ kṛtaṃ kṛtamamunā samaraparityāgasāhasena /

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.6)

children.text: yadi samaramapāsya nāsti mṛtyo- $ rbhayamiti yuktamito 'nyataḥ prayātum &
children.translated_text: If by abandoning the battle there is no fear of death, then it is fitting to depart elsewhere;

children.text: atha maraṇamavaśyameva jantoḥ ē̃ kimiti mudhā malinaṃ yaśaḥ kurudhve // 3.6 //
children.translated_text: but if death is inevitable for every creature, then why do you stain your fame in vain? (3.6)

*(looking behind)*
Enough now of waiting for my chariot. I am armed with this sword, gleaming with the lustre of a rain-laden cloud, with a well-grasped hilt of bright gold. Let me descend to the battlefield.
*(walks about; indicates a twitching of the left eye)*
Ah, how is it that even for me, <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, who am filled with the joy of the great festival of battle, eager to witness my father's valor — even for me, ill omens arise to obstruct my going to the battlefield? So be it, I shall go.
*(walks about with determination, looks ahead)*
What is this! This great cry of armies retreating on all sides from the battlefield — armies that have abandoned the duty of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, cast off the veil of modesty befitting noble men, forgotten the honor due to their lord, light-minded, trampling with the feet of elephants and horses, disregarding their vow of valor worthy of their lineage!
*(observing)*
Alas, what calamity! How is it that even these great warriors — <s>Karṇa</s> and the others — turn their backs on the battle? How could this be the state of armies commanded by my father? So be it, I shall rally them. Ho there! O kings, great mountains guarding the shore of the ocean of the <s>Kaurava</s> army! Enough, enough of this reckless desertion of the battlefield!
(Verse 3.7)
While my father, the teacher, the lord of all archers, stands as commander of the army, blazing like the submarine fire in the ocean of the enemy host consumed by the flames of his weapons,

children.text: karṇālaṃ saṃbhrameṇa vraja kṛpa samaraṃ muñca hārdikya śaṅkāṃ ē̃ tāte cāpadvitīye vahati raṇadhurāṃ ko bhayasyāvakāśaḥ // 3.7 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Karṇa</s>, enough of this panic! O <s>Kṛpa</s>, go to battle! O <s>Hārdikya</s> (Kṛtavarman), abandon your fear! When my father stands bearing the burden of war with his bow as his sole companion, what room is there for fear? (3.7)
Moreover —
*(offstage)*
Where is your father now?

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*śrutvā**
kiṃ brūtha / kuto 'dyāpi te tāta iti* /saroṣam**
āḥ kṣudrāḥ samarabhīravaḥ kathamevaṃ pralapatāṃ vaḥ sahasradhā na dīrṇamanayā jihvayā /

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.8)

children.text: dagdhuṃ viśvaṃ dahanakiraṇairnoditā dvādaśārkā $ vātā vātā diśi diśi na vā saptadhā sapta bhinnāḥ &
children.translated_text: Have the twelve <s>Ādityas</s> (suns) been urged to burn the universe with their fiery rays? Have the seven winds been split sevenfold in every direction?

children.text: channaṃ meghairna gaganatalaṃ puṣkarāvartakādyaiḥ ē̃ pāpaṃ pāpāḥ kathayata kathaṃ śauryarāśeḥ piturme // 3.8 //
children.translated_text: Has the vault of heaven been covered by the <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> and other clouds? Wretches! Sinners! Tell me, how can this be the end of my father, that treasury of valor? (3.8)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(having heard)*
What do you say? 'Where is your father now?'
*(angrily)*
Ah, wretches! Cowards in battle! How is it that your tongue has not been split into a thousand pieces for uttering such words?
*(enters a panic-stricken man, bearing marks of blows)*

The <s>Sūta</s> (charioteer):
Let the prince save me! Save me!
*(falls at his feet)*

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*vilokya**
aye kathaṃ tātasya sārathiraśvasenaḥ / ārya nanu trailokyatrāṇakṣamasya sārathirasi / kiṃ mattaḥ paritrāṇamicchasi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(looking)*
Ah, it is my father's charioteer, <s>Aśvasena</s>! Noble sir, you are the charioteer of one capable of protecting the three worlds! Do you seek protection from me?

The <s>Sūta</s>:
*(rising, with grief)*
Where is your father now?

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(with agitation)*
What — is father no more?

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Indeed so.

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
O father!
*(falls into a swoon)*

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Prince, compose yourself! Compose yourself!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*labdhasaṃjñaḥ sāsram**
hā tāta hā sutavatsala hā lokatrayaikadhanurdhara hā jāmadagĀÇènyāstrasarvasvapratigrahapraṇayin kvāsi / prayaccha me prativacanam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(regaining consciousness, with tears)*
O father! O loving father! O sole archer of the three worlds! O you who cherished the complete gift of weapons from <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (Paraśurāma)! Where are you? Give me an answer!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
kamāra alamatyantaśokāvegena / vīrapuruṣocitāṃ vipattimupagate pitari tvamapi tadanurūpeṇaiva vīryeṇa śokasāgaramuttīrya sukhī bhava /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Sūta</s>:
Prince, enough of this excessive surge of grief! When your father has met an end worthy of a heroic man, you too should cross the ocean of sorrow with valor befitting that, and find peace.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*aśrūṇi vimucya**
ārya kathaya kathaya kathaṃ tādṛgbhujavīryasāgarastāto 'pi nāmāstamupagataḥ /
VERSE_3.9
kiṃ bhīmādgurudakṣiṇāṃ gurugadādbhīmapriyaḥ prāptavān
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(shedding tears)*
Noble sir, tell me, tell me — how has my father, that ocean of mighty valor, come to his setting?
(Verse 3.9)
Did he receive the preceptor's fee of a mighty club-blow from <s>Bhīma</s>, dear to <s>Bhīma</s> as it was?

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Heaven forbid! Heaven forbid!

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
(Verse 3.9 continued)
Was he brought down by <s>Jiṣṇu</s> (Arjuna), who shows kindness to his disciples yet abandons propriety?

The <s>Sūta</s>:
How could that come to pass?

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
VERSE_3.9
govindena sudarśanasya niyataṃ dhārāpathaṃ prāpitaḥ
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
(Verse 3.9 continued)
Was he dispatched to the path of the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus's edge by <s>Govinda</s> (Kṛṣṇa)?

The <s>Sūta</s>:
That too did not happen.
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:

(Verse 3.9 concluded)
Then I suspect some misfortune from a quarter other than these three befell my preceptor. (3.9)

(Verse 3.9 concluded)
Then I suspect some misfortune from a quarter other than these three befell my preceptor. (3.9)
(Verse 3.10)

children.text: ete 'pi tasya kupitasya mahāstrapāṇeḥ $ kiṃ dhūrjaṭeriva tulāmupayānti saṃkhye &
children.translated_text: Even these enemies — could they equal him in battle when he was wrathful, wielding his great weapons, like <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva) himself?

children.text: śokoparuddhahṛdayena yadā tu śastraṃ ē̃ tyaktaṃ tadāsya vihitaṃ ripuṇātighoram // 3.10 //
children.translated_text: But when, with a heart choked by grief, he laid down his weapons, then the enemy committed against him a most terrible deed. (3.10)

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Prince —

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
And what was the cause of his grief and of his laying down his weapons?

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Surely the prince himself was the cause.

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
How can I myself be the cause?

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Listen.
*(shedding tears)*
(Verse 3.11)

children.text: aśvatthāmā hata iti pṛthāsūnunā spaṣṭamuktvā $ svairaṃ śeṣe gaja iti kila vyāhṛtaṃ satyavācā &
children.translated_text: When the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) clearly spoke the words '<s>Aśvatthāman</s> is slain,' and then, being truthful of speech, uttered the remainder 'an elephant' softly,

children.text: tacchrutvāsau dayitatanayaḥ pratyayāttasya rājñaḥ ē̃ śastrāṇyājau nayanasalilaṃ cāpi tulyaṃ mumoca // 3.11 //
children.translated_text: hearing that, he, the fond father, trusting the word of that king, released both his weapons on the battlefield and his tears alike. (3.11)

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
hā tāta hā sutavatsala hā vṛthāmadarthaparityaktajīvita hā śauryarāśe hā śiṣyapriya hā yudhiṣṭhirapakṣapātin* /iti roditi**
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
O father! O loving father! O you who gave up your life needlessly on my account! O treasury of valor! O you who loved your pupils! O partisan of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>!
*(weeps)*

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Prince, enough of this excessive lamentation and wretchedness!
(Verse 3.12)

children.text: śrutvā vadhaṃ mama mṛṣā sutavatsalena $ tāta tvayā saha śarairasavo vimuktāḥ &
children.translated_text: O father, you who were fond of your son — hearing the false report of my death, you gave up your life along with your weapons;

children.text: jīvāmyahaṃ punarayaṃ bhavatā viyuktaḥ ē̃ krūre 'pi tanmayi mudhā tava pakṣapātaḥ // 3.12 //
children.translated_text: yet I live on, bereft of you — O cruel one, your partiality toward me was in vain! (3.12)
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(falls into a swoon)*

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Let the prince compose himself! Compose himself!
*(Then enters <s>Kṛpa</s>.)*

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
*(sighing with distress)*
(Verse 3.13)
Shame on the younger brother of the <s>Kuru</s> lord! Shame on <s>Ajātaśatru</s> (Yudhiṣṭhira)! Shame on the kings who bore their weapons in vain! Shame on us!

children.text: keśagrahaḥ khalu tadā drupadātmajāyā ē̃ droṇasya cādya likhitairiva vīkṣito yaiḥ // 3.13 //
children.translated_text: For the seizing of <s>Draupadī</s>'s hair that day, and now this done to <s>Droṇa</s> — we merely watched both as if they were painted pictures. (3.13)

children.text: tatkathaṃ nu khalu vatsaṃ drakṣyāmyaśvatthāmānam / atha vā himavatsāragurucetasi jñātalokasthitau tasminna khalu śokāvegamahamāśaṅke / kiṃ tu pituḥ paribhavasadṛśamupaśrutya na jāne kiṃ vyavasyatīti / atha vā

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.14)
The terrible consequence of the first seizing of hair (<s>Draupadī</s>'s) is still unfolding on this earth;
with this second seizing of hair (<s>Droṇa</s>'s), surely all creatures will be annihilated. (3.14)

Now how shall I face the dear boy <s>Aśvatthāman</s>? But then again, in one whose heart is as heavy as the <s>Himavat</s> and the ocean, who understands the ways of the world — in him surely I need not fear an overwhelming surge of grief. Yet, hearing of the outrage against his father, I do not know what he will resolve. But then —

children.text:
*vilokya**
tadayaṃ vatsastiṣṭhati / yāvadupasarpāmi* /upasṛtya sasaṃbhramam**
vatsa samāśvasihi samāśvasihi /
children.translated_text:
*(looking)*
There the dear boy stands. Let me approach him.
*(approaching, with urgency)*
Dear child, compose yourself! Compose yourself!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*saṃjñāṃ labdhvā sāsram**
hā tāta hā sakalabhuvanaikaguro* /ākāśe**
yudhiṣṭhira yudhiṣṭhira

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.15)

children.text: ā janmano na vitathaṃ bhavatā kiloktaṃ $ na dvekṣi yajjanamatastvamajātaśatruḥ &
children.translated_text: From birth, it is said, you have never spoken an untruth; because you bear no enmity toward anyone, you are called <s>Ajātaśatru</s> ('one who has no enemy born');

children.text: tāte gurau dvijavare mama bhāgyadoṣā- ē̃ tsarvaṃ tadekapada eva kathaṃ nirastam // 3.15 //
children.translated_text: yet all that, regarding my father, the preceptor, that best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — through my ill fortune — you cast away in a single step! (3.15)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(regaining consciousness, with tears)*
O father! O sole preceptor of the entire world!
*(addressing the sky)*
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>! <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
kumāra eṣa te mātulaḥ śāradvataḥ pārśve tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Sūta</s>:
Prince, here your maternal uncle <s>Śāradvata</s> (<s>Kṛpa</s>) stands at your side.
(Verse 3.16)

children.text: gato yenādya tvaṃ saha raṇabhuvaṃ sainyapatinā $ ya ekaḥ śūrāṇāṃ gurukaṇḍūnikaṣaṇaḥ &
children.translated_text: He with whom you went to the battlefield today as commander of the army, he who was the sole whetstone for the prowess of heroes,

children.text: parīhāsāścitrāḥ satatamabhavanyena bhavataḥ ē̃ svasuḥ ślāghyo bhartā kva nu khalu sa te mātula gataḥ // 3.16 //
children.translated_text: he with whom you always had such delightful jests, that praiseworthy husband of your sister — O uncle, where has he gone? (3.16)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(looking to the side, with tears)*
Uncle! Uncle!

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
You have endured what must be endured. Enough now of this excessive surge of grief.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
mātula parityaktameva mayā paridevanam / eṣo 'haṃ sutavatsalaṃ tātamevānugacchāmi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
Uncle, I have already abandoned my lamentations. Here I am — I shall follow my loving father.

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, this is unbecoming of one such as you.

The <s>Sūta</s>:
Prince, enough of this recklessness!
(Verse 3.17)
My father departed from this world to the next out of fear of separation from me;

children.text: karomi virahaṃ tasya vatsalasya kathaṃ pituḥ // 3.17 //
children.translated_text: how can I endure separation from that loving father? (3.17)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
Noble <s>Śāradvata</s> —

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
vatsa yāvadayaṃ saṃsārastāvatprasiddhaiveyaṃ lokayātrā yatputraiḥ pitaro lokadvaye 'pyanuvartanīyā iti / paśya /

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.18)
Through the offering of <s>nivāpa</s> (oblations of water), <s>añjali</s> (joined-palm offerings), ritual flags, and <s>śrāddha</s> (memorial rites),
you are capable of serving him — whether alive or otherwise. (3.18)

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, as long as this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) endures, this way of the world is well established: that sons must serve their fathers in both worlds. Behold —

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
āyuṣman yathaiva mātulaste śāradvataḥ kathayati tattathā /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Sūta</s>:
Long-lived one, what your maternal uncle <s>Śāradvata</s> tells you is indeed so.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
ārya satyameveāñl̃m / kiṃ tvatidurvahatvācchokabhārasya na śaknomi tātavirahitaḥ kṣaṇamapi prāṇāndhārayitum / tadgacchāmi tamevoddeśaṃ yatra tathāvidhamapi pitaraṃ drakṣyāmi* /uttiṣṭhankhaḍgamālokya vicintya**
kṛtamadyāpi śastragrahaṇaviḍambanayā / bhagavañśastra

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.19)

children.text: gṛhītaṃ yenāsīḥ paribhavabhayānnocitamapi $ prabhāvādyasyābhūnna khalu tava kaścinna viṣayaḥ &
children.translated_text: You were taken up by him who, even when it was not fitting, out of fear of dishonor — by whose power nothing at all was beyond your reach;

children.text: parityaktaṃ tena tvamasi sutaśokānna tu bhayā- ē̃ dvimokṣye śastra tvāmahamapi yataḥ svasti bhavate // 3.19 //
children.translated_text: you were abandoned by him out of grief for his son, not out of fear — O weapon, I too release you, since your master is gone. Farewell to you! (3.19)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
Noble sir, this is truly so. But the burden of grief is so unbearable that without my father I cannot sustain my life-breath even for a moment. Therefore I shall go to that very place where I may see my father, even in such a state.
*(rising and looking at his sword, reflecting)*
Enough now of this mockery of bearing weapons! O blessed weapon —
*(Thus he casts it away.)*
*(offstage)*

children.text: bho bho rājānaḥ kathamiha bhavantaḥ sarve gurorbhāradvājasya paribhavamamunā nṛśaṃsena prayuktamupekṣante /
children.translated_text: Ho there! O kings! How is it that all of you tolerate this outrage committed by that cruel one against preceptor <s>Bhāradvāja</s> (<s>Droṇa</s>)?

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*ākarṇya śanaiḥ śastraṃ spṛśan**
kiṃ gurorbhāradvājasya paribhavaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(hearing, slowly touching the weapon)*
What? An outrage against preceptor <s>Bhāradvāja</s>?
*(again offstage)*
(Verse 3.20)
Of the <s>Ācārya</s>, the preceptor of the three worlds, <s>Droṇa</s>, who had laid down his weapons in grief in battle, whose face was wet with tears,

children.text: maulau pāṇiṃ palitadhavale nyasya kṛtvā nṛśaṃsaṃ ē̃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ svaśibiramayaṃ yāti sarve sahadhvam // 3.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, having cruelly placed his hand upon the white-haired head, now proceeds to his own camp with it — rally together, all of you! (3.20)

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*sakrodhaṃ sakampaṃ ca kṛpasūtau dṛṣṭvā**
kiṃ nāmedam /

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.21)
Before the very eyes of the kings who bore their bows, upon my father who had adopted a vow resembling the great fast unto death (<s>prāyopaveśa</s>),

children.text: tātasya me palitamaulinirastakāśe ē̃ vyāpāritaṃ śirasi śastramaśastrapāṇeḥ // 3.21 //
children.translated_text: upon his white-haired head from which the locks had been pulled apart — a weapon was used against him who was weaponless! (3.21)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
*(with anger and trembling, looking at <s>Kṛpa</s> and the charioteer)*
What is the meaning of this?

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, this is indeed what people are saying.

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
Was my father's head truly handled by that vile one?

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
*sabhayam**
kumāra āsīdayaṃ tasya tejorāśerdevasya navaḥ paribhavāvatāraḥ /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Sūta</s>:
*(fearfully)*
Prince, this was indeed the new culmination of outrage inflicted upon that lord, that mass of radiance.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
hā tāta hā putrapriya mama mandabhāgadheyasya kṛte śastraparityāgāttathāvidhena kṣudreṇātmā paribhāvitaḥ / atha vā

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.22)

children.text: parityakte dehe raṇaśirasi śokāndhamanasā $ śiraḥ śvā kāko vā drupadatanayo vā parimṛśet &
children.translated_text: When the body has been abandoned on the field of battle by one whose mind was blinded by grief, whether a dog, a crow, or the son of <s>Drupada</s> handles the head —

children.text: sphuraddivyāstraughadraviṇamadamattasya ca ripo- ē̃ rmamaivāyaṃ pādaḥ śirasi nihitastasya na karaḥ // 3.22 //
children.translated_text: it is my own foot that rests upon the head of the enemy, intoxicated by the wealth of blazing divine weapons — his hand did not rest there! (3.22)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
O father! O you who loved your son! On account of me, ill-fated as I am, having laid down your weapons, you were dishonored by such a wretch! But then again —
(Verse 3.23)

children.text: tātaṃ śastragrahaṇavimukhaṃ niścayenopalabhya $ tyaktvā śaṅkāṃ khalu vidadhataḥ pāṇimasyottamāṅge &
children.translated_text: Having clearly observed that my father had turned away from taking up weapons, you cast aside all fear and placed your hand upon his head;

children.text: aśvatthāmā karadhṛtadhanuḥ pāṇḍupāñcālasenā- ē̃ tūlotkṣepapralayapavanaḥ kiṃ na yātaḥ smṛtiṃ te // 3.23 //
children.translated_text: did it not occur to you that <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, bow in hand, a wind of destruction to the cotton-like <s>Pāṇḍava</s> and <s>Pāñcāla</s> armies, was still alive? (3.23)
Ah, vile one! Basest of the <s>Pāñcālas</s>!

children.text: yudhiṣṭhira yudhiṣṭhira ajātaśatro amithyāvādindharmaputra sānujasya te kimanenāpakṛtam / atha vā kimanenālīkaprakṛtijihmacetasā / arjuna sātyake bāhuśālinvṛkodara mādhava yuktaṃ nāma bhavatāṃ surāsuramanujalokaikadhanurdharasya dvijanmanaḥ pariṇatavayasaḥ sarvācāryasya viśeṣato mama pituramunā drupadakulakalaṅkena manujapaśunā spṛśyamānamuttamāṅgamupekṣitam / atha vā sarva evaite pātakinaḥ / kimetaiḥ

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.24)
Those who committed, approved, or witnessed this sin against a preceptor — those beasts in human form, those transgressors who bore weapons,

children.text: narakaripuṇā sārdhaṃ teṣāṃ sabhīmakirīṭinā- ē̃ mayamahamasṛṅmedomāṃsaiḥ karomi diśāṃ balim // 3.24 //
children.translated_text: along with the enemy of <s>Naraka</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), together with <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) — I shall make an offering to the directions with their blood, fat, and flesh! (3.24)

<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>! <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>! <s>Ajātaśatru</s>! You who never speak falsely! <s>Dharmaputra</s>! What harm had he done to you and your brothers? Or rather, what does it matter with one whose nature is deceitful and crooked-hearted? <s>Arjuna</s>! <s>Sātyaki</s>! <s>Bāhuśālin</s>! <s>Vṛkodara</s>! <s>Mādhava</s>! Was it fitting for you — that while this twice-born one, sole archer of gods, demons, and men, aged, the preceptor of all, and especially my father, was having his head touched by this stain of the <s>Drupada</s> lineage, this beast in human form — you merely stood by? But then, they are all sinners! What use dwelling on them?

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
vatsa kiṃ na saṃbhāvyate bhāradvājatulye bāhuśālini divyāstragrāmakovide bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, is this not to be expected of one who is the equal of <s>Bhāradvāja</s> in might of arm, skilled in the array of divine weapons?
(Verse 3.25)

children.text: piturmūrdhni spṛṣṭe jvaladanalabhāsvatparaśunā $ kṛtaṃ yadrāmeṇa śrutimupagataṃ tanna bhavatām &
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) with his axe blazing like fire touched the head of his father — that deed of his has come down to you through tradition;

children.text: kimadyāśvatthāmā tadarirudhirāsāravighasaṃ ē̃ na karma krodhāndhaḥ prabhavati vidhātuṃ raṇamukhe // 3.25 //
children.translated_text: can <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, blinded by fury on the battlefield, not accomplish a deed whose remains are washed in torrents of enemy blood? (3.25)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
Ho there! You <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Somakas</s>, <s>Māgadhas</s>, and other dregs of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> order!

children.text: sūta gaccha tvaṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ sāṃgrāmikaiḥ sarvāyudhairupetaṃ mahāhavalakṣaṇaṃ nāmāsmatsyandanamupanaya /
children.translated_text: Charioteer, go! Bring hither my chariot named <s>Mahāhava</s> ('Great Battle'), equipped with all implements of war and all weapons, bearing the marks of a great battle!

The <s>Sūta</s>:
As the prince commands.
*(exits)*

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
vatsa avaśyapratikartavye 'smindāruṇe paribhavāgnau sarveṣāmasmākaṃ ko 'nyastvāmantareṇa śaktaḥ pratikartum / kiṃ tu
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, in avenging this terrible fire of outrage which must be avenged by all of us — who other than you is capable of retribution? But —

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
What more is there?

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
I wish to see you anointed as commander of the army before you descend to the battlefield.

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
Uncle, that depends on another's authority and is of little consequence.

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
vatsa na khalu paratantraṃ nākiṃcitkaraṃ ca / paśya /

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.26)
How could the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> army be without <s>Bhīṣma</s> and without <s>Droṇa</s>,
if you, whose deeds equal theirs, were not yoked to the yoke of command? (3.26)

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, it neither depends on another's authority nor is it of little consequence. Behold —

children.text: kṛtaparikarasya bhavādṛśasya trailokyamapi na kṣamaṃ paripanthībhavituṃ kiṃ punaryudhiṣṭhirabalam / tadevaṃ manye parikalpitābhiṣekopakaraṇaḥ kauravarājo na cirāttvāmevābhyapekṣamāṇastiṣṭhatīti /
children.translated_text: For one such as you, fully resolved, even the three worlds would not be a worthy adversary, let alone the forces of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. Therefore I believe that the <s>Kaurava</s> king, with the materials for the consecration already prepared, awaits none other than you.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
yadyevaṃ tvarate me paribhavānaladahyamānamidaṃ cetastatpratīkārajalāvagāhanāya / tadahaṃ gatvā tātavadhaviṣaṇṇamānasaṃ kurupatiṃ saināpatyasvayaṃgrahaṇapraṇayasamāśvāsanayā mandasaṃtāpaṃ karomi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
If so, my heart, burning in the fire of outrage, hastens toward the waters of retribution. Then I shall go and console the <s>Kuru</s> lord, whose spirit is dejected by the slaying of my father, with the loving assurance that I accept the command of the army, and so ease his grief.

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, just so. Then let us proceed to that very place.
*(They walk about.)*
*(Then enter <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s>.)*
(Verse 3.27)
A man of spirit crosses the ocean of grief at the loss of kinsmen slain by the enemy, with his two arms bearing weapons as his two rafts;

children.text: ācāryaḥ sutanidhanaṃ niśamya saṃkhye ē̃ kiṃ śastragrahasamaye viśastra āsīt // 3.27 //
children.translated_text: when the <s>Ācārya</s> heard of his son's death in battle, why was he weaponless at the time of taking up arms? (3.27)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
O king of <s>Aṅga</s> —

children.text: atha vā sūktamidamabhiyuktaiḥ prakṛtirdustyajeti / yataḥ śokāndhamanasā tena vimucya kṣātradharmakārkaśyaṃ dvijātidharmasulabho mārdavaparigrahaḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: But then again, those who are learned say rightly: 'One's nature is difficult to abandon.' For, with his mind blinded by grief, he cast aside the harshness of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>dharma</s> and embraced the gentleness natural to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s <s>dharma</s>.

<s>Karṇa</s>:
O king, lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>, that is not quite so.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Then how is it?

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
evaṃ kilāsyābhiprāyo yathāśvatthāmā mayā pṛthivīrājye 'bhiṣektavya iti / tasyābhāvādvṛddhasya me brāhmaṇasya vṛthā śastragrahaṇamiti tathā kṛtavān /
children.translated_text:
<s>Karṇa</s>:
His intention was this: '<s>Aśvatthāman</s> should be consecrated by me in the sovereignty of the earth.' In his absence, the aged <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> thought, 'My bearing of weapons is in vain' — and so he acted accordingly.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*(nodding his head)*
So it is.

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
etadarthaṃ ca kauravapāṇḍavapakṣapātapravṛttamahāsaṃgrāmasya rājakasya parasparakṣayamapekṣamāṇena tena pradhānapuruṣavadhopekṣā kṛtā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Karṇa</s>:
And for this purpose, watching the mutual destruction in this great war between the <s>Kaurava</s> and <s>Pāṇḍava</s> factions, he tolerated the death of the chief warriors.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
This is fitting.

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
anyacca rājan drupadenāpyasya bālyātprabhṛtyabhiprāyavedinā na svarāṣṭre vāso dattaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Karṇa</s>:
Moreover, O king, <s>Drupada</s> too, knowing his intentions from childhood, did not grant him residence in his own kingdom.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Well said, O king of <s>Aṅga</s>, well said! Shrewdly spoken.

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
na cāyaṃ mamaikasyābhiprāyaḥ / anye 'bhiyuktā api naivedamanyathā manyante /
children.translated_text:
<s>Karṇa</s>:
Nor is this the opinion of mine alone. Other learned men too hold no different view.
(Verse 3.28)
Having given his assurance of safety, would that supreme warrior have merely looked on while the king of <s>Sindhu</s> (<s>Jayadratha</s>) was being slain by <s>Kirīṭin</s> (Arjuna)?
If this were not so, how else could it be explained? (3.28)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Just so. What doubt can there be?

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
*vilokya**
vatsa eṣa duryodhanaḥ sūtaputreṇa sahāsyāṃ nyagrodhacchāyāyāmupaviṣṭastiṣṭhati / tadupasarpāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛpa</s>:
*(looking)*
Dear child, there is <s>Duryodhana</s> seated with the son of the charioteer (<s>Karṇa</s>) under this banyan tree's shade. Let us approach.
*(They do so.)*

Both:
Victory to the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>!

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*dṛṣṭvā**
aye kathaṃ kṛpo 'śvatthāmā ca* /āsanādavatīrya kṛpaṃ prati**
guro abhivādaye* /aśvatthāmānamuddiśya**
ācāryaputra

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.29)
Come, you whose father was slain for our sake, embrace me — these limbs of mine are wearied beyond measure;

children.text: sparśastavaiṣa bhujayoḥ sadṛśaḥ pituste ē̃ śoke 'pi yo vikṛtimeti tanūruheṣu // 3.29 //
children.translated_text: the touch of your arms is like that of your father's — it makes even my body hair stand on end in the midst of grief! (3.29)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*(seeing them)*
Ah, <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Aśvatthāman</s>!
*(rising from his seat, to <s>Kṛpa</s>)*
Preceptor, I salute you.
*(addressing <s>Aśvatthāman</s>)*
Son of the <s>Ācārya</s> —
*(Embraces him and seats him at his side. <s>Aśvatthāman</s> sheds tears.)*

<s>Karṇa</s>:
Son of <s>Droṇa</s>, enough of casting yourself excessively into the fire of grief!
(Verse 3.30)

children.text: tātastava praṇayavānsa pituḥ sakhā me $ śastre yathā tava guruḥ sa tathā mamāpi &
children.translated_text: Your father was devoted to you, he was the dear friend of my father; as he was your preceptor in weapons, so was he mine;

children.text: kiṃ tasya dehanidhane kathayāmi duḥkhaṃ ē̃ jānīhi tadguruśucā manasā tvameva // 3.30 //
children.translated_text: what shall I say of the grief at his passing — know that sorrow for the preceptor in your own heart is the same as mine. (3.30)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Son of the <s>Ācārya</s>, what distinction is there between us two in this great ocean of calamity? Behold —

<s>Kṛpa</s>:
Dear child, what the <s>Kuru</s> lord says is exactly so.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
rājannevaṃ pakṣapātini tvayi yuktameva śokabhāraṃ laghūkartum / kiṃ tu

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.31)
While I live, my father suffered the seizing of his hair;
how will other fathers desire sons hereafter? (3.31)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
O king, with one so partial as you, it is indeed fitting to lighten the burden of grief. But —

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
drauṇāyana kimatra kriyate yadā tenaiva sarvaparibhavatrāṇahetunā śastramutsṛjatā tādṛśīmavasthāmātmā nītaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Karṇa</s>:
Son of <s>Droṇa</s>, what can be done about it, when he himself — the very shield against all dishonor — by laying down his weapons, brought himself to such a state?

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
aṅgarāja kimāha bhavānkimatra kriyata iti / śrūyatāṃ yatkriyate /

children.translated_text: (Verse 3.32)

children.text: yo yaḥ śastraṃ bibharti svabhujagurumadaḥ pāṇḍavīnāṃ camūnāṃ $ yo yaḥ pāñcālagotre śiśuradhikavayā garbhaśayyāṃ gato vā &
children.translated_text: Whoever bears weapons, proud of his own mighty arms, among the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> armies — whoever in the <s>Pāñcāla</s> clan, whether child, elder, or still in the womb,

children.text: yo yastatkarmasākṣī carati mayi raṇe yaśca yaśca pratīpaḥ ē̃ krodhāndhastasya tasya svayamapi jagatāmantakasyāntako 'ham // 3.32 //
children.translated_text: whoever was a witness to that deed, whoever moves against me in battle, and whoever else is hostile — blinded by rage, I shall be the destroyer of <s>Antaka</s> (Death) himself for each and every one of them! (3.32)

<s>Aśvatthāman</s>:
O king of <s>Aṅga</s>, what do you say — 'what can be done'? Hear what shall be done!
(Verse 3.33)

children.text: deśaḥ so 'yamarātiśoṇitajalairyasminhradāḥ pūritāḥ $ kṣatrādeva tathāvidhaḥ paribhavastātasya keśagrahaḥ &
children.translated_text: This is the very land where lakes were filled with the blood of enemies; the outrage against my father, the seizing of his hair, came from the <s>Kṣatriya</s> order itself;

children.text: tānyevāhitaśastraghasmaragurūṇyastrāṇi bhāsvanti me ē̃ yadrāmeṇa kṛtaṃ tadeva kurute drauṇāyanaḥ krodhanaḥ // 3.33 //
children.translated_text: these same blazing weapons of mine, whose mastery devours hostile warriors, are still in my possession — what <s>Rāma</s> (Paraśurāma) once did, the wrathful son of <s>Droṇa</s> shall do again! (3.33)
Furthermore, O <s>Karṇa</s>, disciple of <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (Paraśurāma) —

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
ācāryaputra tasya tathāvidhasyānanyasādhāraṇasya te vīrabhāvasya kimanyatsadṛśam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Son of the <s>Ācārya</s>, for one of your heroic nature, unparalleled as it is — what else could be a fitting match?

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
rājansumahānkhalu droṇaputreṇa voḍhumadhyavasitaḥ samarabhāraḥ / tadahamevaṃ manye / bhavatā kṛtaparikaro 'yamucchettuṃ lokatrayamapi samarthaḥ kiṃ punaryudhiṣṭhirabalam / ato 'bhiṣicyatāṃ saināpatye /
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛpa</s>:
O king, the burden of battle that the son of <s>Droṇa</s> has resolved to bear is truly immense. Therefore I hold this view: once fully resolved, he is capable of destroying even the three worlds, let alone the forces of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. Therefore let him be consecrated as commander of the army.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
suṣṭhu yujyamānamabhihitaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ / kiṃ tu prākpratipanno 'yamartho 'ṅgarājasya /
children.translated_text:
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
What you both say is eminently fitting. However, this matter was previously promised to the king of <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>).

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
rājannasadṛśaparibhavaśokasāgare nimajjantamenamaṅgarājasyārthe naivopekṣituṃ yuktam / asyāpi tadevārikulamanuśāsanīyam / ataḥ kimasya pīḍā na bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛpa</s>: O King, it is not right to neglect this man [<s>Duḥśāsana</s>], who is sinking in a sea of grief from an insult unbecoming [to his station], for the sake of the king of <s>Aṅga</s> [<s>Karṇa</s>]. The same enemy clan must be chastised on his behalf as well. Therefore, will his suffering not come to an end?
VERSE 3.34

children.text: prayatnaparibodhitaḥ stutibhiradya śeṣe niśā- $ makeśavamapāṇḍavaṃ bhuvanamadya niḥsomakam &
children.translated_text: Awakened with effort by praises, today — while the night remains — [I shall make] the world without <s>Keśava</s>, without the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, without <s>Soma</s>!

children.text: iyaṃ parisamāpyate raṇakathādya doḥśālinā ē̃ vyapaitu nṛpakānanātigururadya bhāro bhuvaḥ // 3.34 //
children.translated_text: Today this tale of battle shall be concluded by one mighty of arm; today let the heavy burden of the earth — the king's forest [of enemies] — be removed! (3.34)
<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: O King, Lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>, why even now this deliberation over what is proper and improper?

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
*vihasya**
vaktuṃ sukaramidaṃ duṣkaramadhyavasātum / bahavaḥ kauravabale 'sya karmaṇaḥ śaktāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s>: [Laughing] This is easy to say, but difficult to undertake. Many in the <s>Kaurava</s> army are capable of this deed.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
aṅgarāja evamidam / bahavaḥ kauravabale 'tra śaktāḥ / kiṃ tu duḥkhopahataḥ śokāveśavaśādbravīmi na punarvīrajanādhikṣepeṇa /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: O King of <s>Aṅga</s>, this is so — many in the <s>Kaurava</s> army are capable of this. But I speak thus out of the force of grief, being struck by sorrow — not by way of disparaging heroic men.

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
mūḍha duḥkhitasyāśrupātaḥ kupitasya cāyudhadvitīyasya saṃgrāmāvataraṇamucitaṃ naivaṃvidhāḥ pralāpāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s>: Fool! For one who is grieving, tears are appropriate; for one who is angered, entering battle with weapon in hand is fitting — not wild ravings of this sort!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*sakrodham**
are re rādhāgarbhabhārabhūta sūtāpasada mamāpi nāmāśvatthāmno duḥkhitasyāśrubhiḥ pratikriyāmupadiśi na śastreṇa / paśya /

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.35

children.text: nirvīryaṃ guruśāpabhāṣitavaśātkiṃ me tavevāyudhaṃ $ saṃpratyeva bhayādvihāya samaraṃ prāpto 'smi kiṃ tvaṃ yathā &
children.translated_text: Is my weapon rendered powerless by the curse of my preceptor's words? Have I just now fled the battlefield in fear, as you have done?

children.text: jāto 'haṃ stutivaṃśakīrtanavidāṃ kiṃ sārathīnāṃ kule ē̃ kṣudrārātikṛtāpriyaṃ pratikaromyasreṇa nāstreṇa yat // 3.35 //
children.translated_text: Was I born in a family of charioteers, skilled only in reciting panegyrics? Is it that I counter the insults of petty enemies with tears, not with weapons? (3.35)

<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: [Angrily] You there! You burden of <s>Rādhā's</s> womb! You lowborn offspring of a charioteer! You presume to advise even me, <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>, that for one who grieves, the remedy is tears, not weapons? Behold!
VERSE 3.36

children.text: nirvīryaṃ vā savīryaṃ vā mayā notsṛṣṭamāyudham /
children.translated_text: Whether my weapon is powerless or powerful, I have never abandoned it —
as your father, the mighty-armed one, did when frightened by the <s>Pāñcāla</s> [<s>Drupada</s>]! (3.36)
<s>Karṇa</s>: [Angrily] You there, you braggart! You bungler who grasps weapons in vain! Boy!
VERSE 3.37

children.text: sūto vā sūtaputro vā yo vā ko vā bhavāmyaham /
children.translated_text: Whether I am a charioteer or a charioteer's son, or whoever I may be —

children.text: daivāyattaṃ kule janma madāyattaṃ tu pauruṣam // 3.37 //
children.translated_text: birth in a family depends on fate, but valor depends on me! (3.37)
And moreover:

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*sakrodham**
are re rathakārakulakalaṅka rādhāgarbhabhārabhūta are āyudhānabhijña tātamapyadhikṣipasi / atha vā

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.38

children.text: sa bhīruḥ śūro vā prathitabhujasārastribhuvane $ kṛtaṃ yattenājau pratidinamiyaṃ vetti vasudhā &
children.translated_text: Whether he is a coward or a hero, celebrated in the three worlds for the strength of his arms — what he accomplished in battle daily, this earth itself knows.

children.text: parityaktaṃ śastraṃ kathamiti sa satyavratadharaḥ ē̃ pṛthāsūnuḥ sākṣī tvamasi raṇabhīro kva nu tadā // 3.38 //
children.translated_text: How did he abandon his weapon? He was one who observed the vow of truth! <s>Pṛthā's</s> son is a witness — where were you then, O coward of the battlefield? (3.38)
<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: [Angrily] You there, you blot on the chariot-maker's clan! You burden of <s>Rādhā's</s> womb! You, ignorant of weapons, you dare disparage even my father? Or rather —

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
*vihasya**
evaṃ bhīruraham / punarvikramaikarasaṃ tava pitaramanusmṛtya mahānme saṃśayo jātaḥ / api ca re mūḍha

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.39
If he abandoned his weapon, and those without weapons cannot repel armed enemies,

children.text: yadanena maulidalane 'pyudāsitaṃ ē̃ suciraṃ striyeva nṛpacakrasaṃnidhau // 3.39 //
children.translated_text: then why did he remain long indifferent to the seizing of the queen's hair, like a woman, in the assembly of kings? (3.39)
<s>Karṇa</s>: [Laughing] So I am a coward! But recalling your father, who delights solely in valor — a great doubt has arisen in me. And moreover, you fool —

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*sakrodhaṃ sakampaṃ ca**
durātmanrājavallabha pragalbha sūtāpasada asaṃbaddhapralāpin

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.40

children.text: kathamapi na niṣiddho duḥkhinā bhīruṇā vā $ drupadatanayapāṇistena pitrā mamādya &
children.translated_text: Somehow my father — whether from grief or cowardice — did not prevent <s>Drupada's</s> daughter's hand [from being seized].

children.text: tava bhujabaladarpādhmāyamānasya vāmaḥ ē̃ śirasi caraṇa eṣa nyasyate vārayainam // 3.40 //
children.translated_text: Now, as you swell with pride in the strength of your arms, this left foot of mine shall be placed upon your head — prevent it if you can! (3.40)
<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: [With anger and trembling] You wicked royal favorite! You insolent one! You lowborn charioteer! You senseless babbler!
[He rises to do so.]
<s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s>: Son of the preceptor, be patient! [They restrain him.]
[<s>Aśvatthāmā</s> mimes striking with his foot.]
VERSE 3.41
You may be inviolable by birth, but this foot you have raised —

children.text: anena lūnaṃ khaḍgena patitaṃ vetsyasi kṣitau // 3.41 //
children.translated_text: when it falls, severed by this sword, you shall know it on the ground! (3.41)
<s>Karṇa</s>: [Rising angrily and drawing his sword] You wretch! You braggart! You base <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! You self-praiser!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
are mūḍha kiṃ nāma jātyā kāmamavadhyo 'ham / iyaṃ sā jātistyaktā* /iti yajñopavītaṃ chinatti / punaśca sakrodham**
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: You fool! Why do you say I am inviolable by birth? That birth-status is hereby renounced! [He cuts his sacred thread.] And again, with fury:
VERSE 3.42
Today I shall make that crowned one [<s>Arjuna</s>] a breaker of false vows through [killing] me!

children.text: śastraṃ gṛhāṇa vā tyaktvā maulau vā racayāñjalim // 3.42 //
children.translated_text: Either take up your weapon, or clasp your hands upon your head [in surrender]! (3.42)
[Both draw their swords and prepare to strike each other. <s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s> restrain them.]
<s>Duryodhana</s>: Friend, son of the preceptor — enough of this weapon-grasping!
<s>Kṛpa</s>: Child, son of the charioteer — enough of this weapon-grasping!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
mātula mātula kiṃ nivārayasi / ayamapi tātanindāpragalbhaḥ sūtāpasado dhṛṣṭadyumnapakṣapātyeva /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: Uncle! Uncle! Why do you restrain me? This one too — bold in reviling my father — this lowborn charioteer is surely on the side of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>!
VERSE 3.43
When feeble men are overlooked with contempt by the truly brave,
they become terrified by those blinded with rage, and resort to this kind of boasting. (3.43)
<s>Karṇa</s>: O King, surely I am not the one who should be restrained!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
rājanmuñca muñcainam / āsādayatu madbhujāntaraniṣpeṣasulabhamasūnāmavasādanam / anyacca rājan / snehena kāryeṇa vā yattvamenaṃ tātādhikṣepakāriṇaṃ durātmānaṃ mattaḥ parirakṣitumicchasi tadubhayamapi vṛthaiva / paśya /

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.44

children.text: pāpapriyastava kathaṃ guṇinaḥ sahāyaḥ $ sūtānvayaḥ śaśadharānvayasaṃbhavasya &
