children.translated_text: How can one fond of sin be the ally of the virtuous? How can one of charioteer lineage [befriend] one born in the lineage of the Moon?

children.text: hantā kirīṭinamahaṃ nṛpa muñca kuryāṃ ē̃ krodhādakarṇamapṛthātmajamadya lokam // 3.44 //
children.translated_text: I shall slay <s>Kirīṭī</s> [<s>Arjuna</s>]! O King, release him — in my rage, today I shall make the world without <s>Karṇa</s> and without <s>Pṛthā's</s> son! (3.44)

<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: O King, release him! Release him! Let him experience the destruction of his vital breaths, easily obtained by being crushed between my arms! And furthermore, O King — whether out of affection or for some purpose you wish to protect this wretch who reviles my father from me — both are in vain! Behold!
[He wishes to strike.]

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
*khaḍgamudyamya**
are vācāṭa brāhmaṇādhama ayaṃ na bhavasi / rājanmuñca muñca / na khalvahaṃ vārayitavyaḥ* /hantumicchati**
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s>: [Raising his sword] You braggart! You lowest of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>! You are no [true <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>]! O King, release him, release him! Surely I am not to be restrained! [He wishes to kill him.]
[<s>Duryodhana</s> and <s>Kṛpa</s> restrain them.]
<s>Duryodhana</s>: <s>Karṇa</s>! Son of the preceptor! What is this delusion that has seized you both today?

children.text:
&kṛpaḥ&:
vatsa anyadeva prastutamanyatrāvega iti ko 'yaṃ vyāmohaḥ / svabalavyasanaṃ cedamasminkāle rājakulasyāsya yuṣmatta eva bhavatīti vāmaḥ panthāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛpa</s>: Child, one matter was under discussion, and the agitation has gone elsewhere — what is this delusion? If at this time the self-destruction of our own forces comes about through you two, that would be an evil path for this royal house.

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
mātula na labhyate 'sya kaṭupralāpino rathakārakulakalaṅkasya darpaḥ śātayitum /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: Uncle, the arrogance of this harsh-speaking blot on the chariot-maker's clan cannot be humbled!
<s>Kṛpa</s>: Child, this is not the time for conflict among the chief warriors of our own forces.
VERSE 3.45

children.text: ayaṃ pāpo yāvanna nidhanamupeyādariśaraiḥ $ parityaktaṃ tāvatpriyamapi mayāstraṃ raṇamukhe &
children.translated_text: Until this wicked one meets his death by enemy arrows, my beloved weapon — though dear to me — is renounced on the battlefield!

children.text: balānāṃ nāthe 'sminparikupitabhīmārjunabhaye ē̃ samutpanne rājā priyasakhabalaṃ vettu samare // 3.45 //
children.translated_text: When this lord of armies falls, with the fearsome <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> enraged, let the king then know in battle the [true] strength of his dear friend's forces! (3.45)
<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: Uncle, if that is so —
[He throws down his sword.]
<s>Karṇa</s>: [Laughing] This indeed is hereditary in men of your kind — this so-called renunciation of weapons!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
nanu re aparityaktamapi bhavādṛśairāyudhaṃ ciraparityaktameva niṣphalatvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: Well then, a weapon unrenounced by men of your kind is as good as long since renounced, being fruitless!
VERSE 3.46
As long as I stand with weapon in hand, what need is there for other weapons?

children.text: yadvā na siddhamastreṇa mama tatkena setsyati // 3.46 //
children.translated_text: Whatever cannot be accomplished by my weapon — by what [weapon] shall it be accomplished? (3.46)
<s>Karṇa</s>: You fool!
[Behind the scenes:]

children.text: āḥ durātmandraupadīkeśāmbarākarṣaṇamahāpātakindhārtarāṣṭrāpasada cirasya khalu kālasya matsaṃmukhamāgato 'si / kṣudrapaśo kvedānīṃ gamyate / api ca bho bho rādheyaduryodhanasaubalaprabhṛtayaḥ pāṇḍavavidveṣaṇaścāpapāṇayo mānadhanāḥ śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ /

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.47

children.text: spṛṣṭā yena śiroruhe nṛpaśunā pāñcālarājātmajā $ yenāsyāḥ paridhānamapyapahṛtaṃ rājñāṃ gurūṇāṃ puraḥ &
children.translated_text: He who, that royal beast, touched the hair of <s>Pāñcālarājātmajā</s> [<s>Draupadī</s>], who stripped even her garments before kings and elders —

children.text: yasyoraḥsthalaśoṇitāsavamahaṃ pātuṃ pratijñātavā- ē̃ nso 'yaṃ madbhujapañjare nipatitaḥ saṃrakṣyatāṃ kauravaḥ // 3.47 //
children.translated_text: he whose chest-blood I have vowed to drink — he has now fallen into the cage of my arms! Let the <s>Kauravas</s> save him if they can! (3.47)

You wretch! You great sinner who dragged <s>Draupadī</s> by her hair and garment! You vile offspring of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>! After so long, you have come before me at last! Where do you think you are going now, you wretched beast? And listen, O <s>Rādheya</s>, <s>Duryodhana</s>, <s>Saubala</s>, and the rest — you enemies of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, bow-wielding ones who stake your pride [upon enmity] — listen!
[All listen.]

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*sotprāsam**
aṅgarāja senāpate jāmadagnyaśiṣya droṇopahāsinbhujabalaparirakṣitasakalaloka* /dhṛtāyudha iti paṭhitvā**
idaṃ tadāsannatarameva saṃvṛttam / rakṣainaṃ sāṃprataṃ bhīmādduḥśāsanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: [With derision] O King of <s>Aṅga</s>! O Commander-in-chief! O disciple of <s>Jāmadagnya</s>! O scorner of <s>Droṇa</s>! O protector of all the world by the strength of your arms! [Reading out 'dhṛtāyudha' (weapon-wielder)] — This has come all too near now! Save <s>Duḥśāsana</s> from <s>Bhīma</s> — now!

children.text:
&karṇaḥ&:
āḥ kā śaktirvṛkodarasya mayi jīvati duḥśāsanasya chāyāmapyākramitum / yuvarāja na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyam / ayamahamāgato 'smi* /iti niṣkrāntaḥ**
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s>: What power has <s>Vṛkodara</s> [<s>Bhīma</s>], while I live, to even approach the shadow of <s>Duḥśāsana</s>? Prince, fear not! Fear not! Here I come! [Exit.]

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
rājankauravanātha abhīṣmadroṇaṃ saṃprati kauravabalamāloḍayantau bhīmārjunau rādheyenaivaṃvidhenānyena vā na śakyete nivārayitum / ataḥ svayameva bhrātuḥ pratīkāraparo bhava /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: O King! Lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>! Now that the <s>Kaurava</s> army is without <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> who are devastating it cannot be stopped by <s>Rādheya</s> or any other such man. Therefore, be yourself devoted to avenging your brother!

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
āḥ śaktirasti durātmanaḥ pavanatanayasyānyasya vā mayi jīvati śastrapāṇau vatsasya chāyāmapyākramitum / vatsa na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyam / kaḥ ko 'tra bhoḥ / rathamupanaya* /iti niṣkrāntaḥ**
children.translated_text: <s>Duryodhana</s>: Has the wretched son of the wind-god, or any other, the power — while I stand with weapon in hand — to even approach the shadow of my dear [brother]? Child, fear not! Fear not! Who is there? Bring my chariot! [Exit.]
[Tumult behind the scenes.]

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*agrato vilokya**
mātula hā dhikkaṣṭam / eṣa khalu bhrātuḥ pratijñābhaṅgabhīruḥ kirīṭī samaṃ duryodhanarādheyau śaravarṣairdurvārairabhidravati / sarvathā pītaṃ duḥśāsanaśoṇitaṃ bhīmena / na khalu viṣahe duryodhanānujasyaināṃ vipattimavalokayitum / anṛtamanumataṃ nāma / mātula śastraṃ śastram /

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.48
Even falsehood is better than truth! Curse heaven — let hell be mine!
To save <s>Duḥśāsana</s> from <s>Bhīma</s>, [I take up] the weapon that was renounced yet never truly renounced! (3.48)

<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: [Looking ahead] Uncle! Alas, how terrible! <s>Kirīṭī</s> [<s>Arjuna</s>], fearful of his brother's [<s>Bhīma's</s>] vow being broken, is assailing both <s>Duryodhana</s> and <s>Rādheya</s> together with irresistible showers of arrows! Surely <s>Bhīma</s> has drunk <s>Duḥśāsana's</s> blood! I cannot bear to witness this calamity befalling <s>Duryodhana's</s> brother! What has been sanctioned is indeed false! Uncle — my weapon! My weapon!
[He wishes to seize the sword.]
[Behind the scenes:]
O noble son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>! You must not transgress your truthful word, which has never been violated before!
<s>Kṛpa</s>: Child, an incorporeal voice protects you from falsehood!

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
kathamiyamamānuṣī vāgnānumanute saṃgrāmāvataraṇaṃ mama / bhoḥ kaṣṭam / āḥ pakṣapātino devā api pāṇḍavānām / sarvathā pītaṃ duḥśāsanaśoṇitaṃ bhīmena / bhoḥ kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭam /

children.translated_text: VERSE 3.49
While <s>Duḥśāsana's</s> blood was being drunk, I remained indifferent!
What other dear service can I now render to <s>Duryodhana</s> in battle? (3.49)

<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>: What? This supernatural voice does not permit me to enter battle? Alas, how terrible! Even the gods are partial to the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>! Surely <s>Bhīma</s> has drunk <s>Duḥśāsana's</s> blood! Alas, terrible, terrible!

children.text: mātula rādheyakrodhavaśādanāryamasmābhirācaritam / atastvamapi tāvadasya rājñaḥ pārśvavartī bhava /
children.translated_text: Uncle, in the grip of anger toward <s>Rādheya</s>, we have acted ignobly. Therefore, you too now stand at the side of this king.
<s>Kṛpa</s>: I shall go to provide a remedy there. You too should return to the encampment.
[They walk about and exit.]

children.text:
iti tṛtīyo 'ṅkaḥ /

ACT_4
caturtho 'ṅkaḥ /
*tataḥ praviśati prahāramūrcchitaṃ rathasthaṃ duryodhanamapaharansūtaḥ / sūtaḥ sasaṃbhramaṃ parikrāmati**
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the Third Act.

ACT 4
The Fourth Act.
[Then enters a charioteer, carrying away <s>Duryodhana</s>, who lies on the chariot, swooning from his wounds. The charioteer moves about hastily.]
[Behind the scenes:]

children.text: bho bho bāhubalāvalepapravartitamahāsamaradohadāḥ kauravapakṣapātapaṇīkṛtaprāṇadraviṇasaṃcayā narapatayaḥ saṃstabhyantāṃ saṃstabhyantāṃ nihataduḥśāsanapītāvaśeṣaśoṇitasnapitabībhatsaveṣavṛkodaradarśanabhayapariskhalatpraharaṇāni raṇātdravanti balāni /
children.translated_text: Ho! Ho! You kings, whose pride in the strength of your arms has led to the great passion for battle, who have staked your lives and wealth in partisanship for the <s>Kaurava</s> cause — stand firm! Stand firm! The armies are fleeing from the battlefield, their weapons slipping from their hands in terror at the sight of <s>Vṛkodara</s> [<s>Bhīma</s>] in his hideous guise, bathed in the remaining blood of the slain <s>Duḥśāsana</s>!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
*vilokya**
kathameṣa dhavalacapalacāmaracumbitakanakakamaṇḍalunā śikharāvabaddhavaijayantīsūcitena hatagajavājinarakalevarasahasrasaṃmardaviṣamodghātakṛtakalakalakiṅkiṇījālamālinā rathena śaravarṣastambhitaparabalaparākramaprasaraḥ pradrutamātmabalamāśvāsayankṛpaḥ kirīṭinābhiyuktamaṅgarājamanusarati / hanta jātamasmadbalānāmavalambanam /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
*Looking*
How is it that <s>Kṛpa</s>, having checked the advance of the enemy forces with a shower of arrows, swiftly reassuring his own army, follows <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>) who is being attacked by <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), in a chariot adorned with white and flashing <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) kissing the golden water-pot, with a victory-banner tied to the peak marking it out, garlanded with nets of tinkling bells set ringing by the noxious stench from the crushing together of thousands of corpses of slain elephants, horses, and men! Ah, a support has arisen for our forces!
*After tumultuous noise offstage*

children.text: bho bhoḥ asmaddarśanabhayaskhalitakārmukakṛpāṇatomaraśaktayaḥ kauravacamūbhaṭāḥ pāṇḍavapakṣapātinaśca yodhāḥ na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyam / ayamahaṃ nihataduḥśāsanapīvaroraḥsthalakṣatajāsavapānamadoddhato rabhasagāmī stokāvaśiṣṭapratijñāmahotsavaḥ kauravarājasya dyūtanirjito dāsaḥ pārthamadhyamo bhīmasenaḥ sarvānbhavataḥ sākṣīkaromi / śrūyatām /

children.translated_text: [Verse 4.1]

children.text: rājño mānadhanasya kārmukabhṛto duryodhanasyāgrataḥ $ pratyakṣaṃ kurubāndhavasya miṣataḥ karṇasya śalyasya ca &
children.translated_text: Before king <s>Duryodhana</s>, a treasury of pride, a bearer of the bow, in the direct presence of the kinsman of the <s>Kurus</s>, while <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Śalya</s> looked on,

children.text: pītaṃ tasya mayādya pāṇḍavavadhūkeśāmbarākarṣiṇaḥ ē̃ koṣṇaṃ jīvata eva tīkṣṇakarajakṣuṇṇādasṛgvakṣasaḥ // 4.1 //
children.translated_text: I have today drunk the warm blood from the chest — crushed by sharp nails — of that one who dragged the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> wife by her hair and garments, while he was still alive. (4.1)

Ho, ho! O warriors of the <s>Kaurava</s> army, whose bows, swords, javelins, and spears have slipped from your hands in fear at the sight of us, and O soldiers siding with the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> — fear not, fear not! I am he — intoxicated from drinking the blood flowing from the broad chest of the slain <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, moving with violent speed, my great festival of vows nearly complete — the slave of the <s>Kaurava</s> king, won at dice, the middle <s>Pārtha</s> (son of <s>Pṛthā</s>), <s>Bhīmasena</s> — I make all of you my witnesses! Listen!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
*śrutvā sabhayam**
aye āsanna eva durātmā kauravarājaputramahāvanotpātamāruto mārutiḥ / anupalabdhasaṃjñaśca tāvadatra mahārājaḥ / bhavatu / sudūramapaharāmi syandanam / kadācidduḥśāsana ivāsminnapyayamanāryo 'nāryamācariṣyati* /tvaritataraṃ parikramyāvalokya ca**
aye ayamasau sarasīsarojavilolanasurabhiśītalamātariśvasaṃvāhitasāndrakisalayo nyagrodhapādapaḥ / ucitā viśrāmabhūriyaṃ samaravyāpārakhinnasya vīrajanasya / atra sthitaścāyācitatālavṛntena haricandanacchaṭāśītalenāprayatnasurabhiṇā daśāpariṇāmayogyena sarasīsamīraṇenāmunā gataklamo bhaviṣyati mahārājaḥ / lūnaketuścāyaṃ ratho 'nivārita eva pravekṣyati cchāyām* /iti praveśaṃ rūpayitvā**
kaḥ ko 'tra bhoḥ* /samantādavalokya**
kathaṃ na kaścidatra parijanaḥ / nūnaṃ tathāvidhasya vṛkodarasya darśanādevaṃvidhasya ca svāminastrāsena śibirasaṃniveśameva praviṣṭaḥ / kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ kaṣṭam /

children.translated_text: [Verse 4.2]

children.text: dattvā droṇena pārthādabhayamapi na saṃrakṣitaḥ sindhurājaḥ $ krūraṃ duḥśāsane 'sminhariṇa iva kṛtaṃ bhīmasenena karma &
children.translated_text: Though <s>Droṇa</s> granted <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) a pledge of safety, the king of <s>Sindhu</s> (<s>Jayadratha</s>) was not protected; a cruel deed has been done by <s>Bhīmasena</s> upon this <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, as upon a deer;

children.text: duḥsādhyāmapyarīṇāṃ laghumiva samare pūrayitvā pratijñāṃ ē̃ nāhaṃ manye sakāmaṃ kurukulavimukhaṃ daivametāvatāpi // 4.2 //
children.translated_text: Having fulfilled in battle even the most difficult of vows against enemies as though it were easy — even with all this, I do not think fate, turned against the <s>Kuru</s> clan, is satisfied. (4.2)

[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
*Hearing this, with fear*
Alas, the wicked <s>Māruti</s> (<s>Bhīmasena</s>, son of the Wind), a storm-wind uprooting the great forest of the <s>Kaurava</s> prince, is close at hand! And the great king here has lost consciousness. So be it — I shall drive the chariot far away. Perhaps this ignoble one will commit an ignoble act upon this [king] too, as he did upon <s>Duḥśāsana</s>.
*Having driven around hastily and looked about*
Ah, here is this <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree, with dense clusters of shoots fanned by the cool, fragrant breeze wafting from the lotuses of the lake, playing over the water's surface. This is a fitting resting place for a warrior exhausted by the toils of battle. And the great king, stationed here, will be relieved of his fatigue by this lake-breeze — unsought, cool as a splash of <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood), naturally fragrant, incapable of deterioration, like an unasked-for fan of palm-leaf. And this chariot, with its banner cut down, will enter the shade unobstructed.
*Having mimed the entrance*
Who is here, ho!
*Looking around on all sides*
What — there is no attendant here! Surely, in terror of the sight of that terrible <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) and of the condition of their master, they have entered the camp enclosure. Alas! Alas!

children.text:
*rājānamavalokya**
kathamadyāpi na cetanāṃ labhate mahārājaḥ / bhoḥ kaṣṭam* /niḥśvasya**
children.translated_text:
*Looking at the king*
How is it that even now the great king does not regain consciousness? Alas!
*Sighing*
[Verse 4.3]
In this clan, like a forest where the young trees are broken by a cow-elephant in rut,

children.text: hatasakalakumārake kule 'smiṃ- ē̃ stvamapi vidheravalokitaḥ kaṭākṣaiḥ // 4.3 //
children.translated_text: with only one prominent <s>śāla</s> tree remaining, all the young princes slain — even you have been glanced at by the sidelong looks of Fate! (4.3)
[Verse 4.4]
Of <s>Bhīmasena</s>, who stands unscathed, mace in hand, who has not yet faced mortal danger —
even this remaining vow of his is being fulfilled by you, [O Fate]! (4.4)
Alas, O wretched Fate, you who have turned against the <s>Bharata</s> clan!

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*śanairupalabdhasaṃjñaḥ**
āḥ śaktirasti durātmano vṛkodarahatakasya mayi jīvati duryodhane pratijñāṃ pūrayitum / vatsa duḥśāsana na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyam / ayamahamāgato 'smi / nanu sūta prāpaya rathaṃ tamevoddeśaṃ yatra vatso me duḥśāsanaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
*Slowly regaining consciousness*
Ha! Does the wicked wretch <s>Vṛkodara</s> have the power to fulfil his vow while I, <s>Duryodhana</s>, am alive? Dear child <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, fear not, fear not! I have come! Charioteer, drive the chariot to that very place where my dear <s>Duḥśāsana</s> is!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
āyuṣmannakṣamāḥ saṃprati vāhāste rathamudvoḍhum* /apavārya**
manorathaṃ ca /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
Long-lived one, the horses are presently unable to draw the chariot.
*Aside*
Nor [to draw] the chariot of your desires.

[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
*Descending from the chariot, with pride and with pointed meaning*
Enough with this delay in chariot-travel!

[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
*With embarrassment and pity*
May the long-lived one forgive, may he forgive!

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
dhiksūta kiṃ rathena / kevalamarātivimardasaṃghaṭṭasaṃcārī duryodhanaḥ khalvaham / tadgadāmātrasahāyaḥ samarabhuvamavatarāmi /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
Curse you, charioteer — what need of a chariot? I am <s>Duryodhana</s>, who moves solely in the thick of battle against enemies! Therefore, with only my mace as companion, I descend onto the battlefield!

[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
Indeed so, long-lived one. What doubt is there?
[Verse 4.5]

children.text: bālasya me prakṛtidurlalitasya pāpaḥ $ pāpaṃ vyavasyati samakṣamudāyudho 'sau &
children.translated_text: That wicked one resolves upon a wicked deed against me, a mere boy, spoiled by nature, before my very eyes, weapon in hand —

children.text: asminnivārayasi kiṃ vyavasāyinaṃ māṃ ē̃ krodho na nāma karuṇā na ca te 'sti lajjā // 4.5 //
children.translated_text: and you restrain me who am determined to act? Have you no anger, no compassion, no shame? (4.5)

[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
If so, then why do you speak thus? Look!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
*sakaruṇaṃ pādayornipatya**
etadvijñāpayāmi / āyuṣmansaṃpūrṇapratijñena nivṛttena bhavitavyamidānīṃ durātmanā vṛkodarahatakena / ata evaṃ bravīmi /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
*With compassion, falling at his feet*
This is what I wish to convey: Long-lived one, that wicked wretch <s>Vṛkodara</s> must surely have retired now, his vows fulfilled. That is why I speak thus.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*sahasā bhūmau patan**
hā vatsa duḥśāsana hā madājñāvirodhitapāṇḍava hā vikramaikarasa hā madaṅkadurlalita hā arātikulagajaghaṭāmṛgendra hā yuvarāja kvāsi / prayaccha me prativacanam* /iti niḥśvasya mohamupagataḥ**
children.translated_text:
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
*Falling suddenly to the ground*
Ah, dear child <s>Duḥśāsana</s>! Ah, you who defied the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> at my command! Ah, you whose sole pleasure was valor! Ah, you who were fondly raised on my lap! Ah, you lion among the elephant-herds of the enemy clan! Ah, crown prince — where are you? Give me a reply!
*Sighing, he falls into a swoon*

[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
O King, be consoled, be consoled!

[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
*Regaining consciousness. Sighing.*
[Verse 4.6]

children.text: mukto yatheṣṭamupabhogasukheṣu naiva $ tvaṃ lālito 'pi hi mayā na vṛthāgrajena &
children.translated_text: You were never set free to enjoy pleasures at will; nor were you, though cherished, brought up properly by me, your eldest brother —

children.text: asyāstu vatsa tava heturahaṃ vipatte- ē̃ ryatkārito 'syavinayaṃ na ca rakṣito 'si // 4.6 //
children.translated_text: may I be the cause of this calamity of yours, dear child, since you were made to commit transgressions and were not protected! (4.6)
*He collapses.*

[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
Long-lived one, be consoled, be consoled!
[Verse 4.7]
By my younger brother <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, who was a boy, always obedient to my commands,
who should have been protected — I was instead protected, as by an offering. (4.7)

[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
Curse you, charioteer — what have you done?

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
mahārāja marmabhedibhiriṣutomaraśaktiprāsavarṣairmahārathānāmapahṛtacetanatvānniśceṣṭaḥ kṛto mahārāja ityapahṛto mayā rathaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
Great King, rendered unconscious and motionless by showers of arrows, javelins, spears, and lances that pierced his vital points from the great chariot-warriors, the great king [was in such a state that] I carried off the chariot.
[Verse 4.8]
I was not awakened by the blows of that very <s>Pāṇḍava</s> beast, my brother's enemy, [dealt] with the thunderbolt-strikes of his mace;

children.text: tāmeva nādhiśayito rudhirārdraśayyāṃ ē̃ dauḥśāsanīṃ yadahamāśu vṛkodaro vā // 4.8 //
children.translated_text: let me or <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) swiftly claim that same blood-soaked bed that belongs to <s>Duḥśāsana</s>! (4.8)

[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
Charioteer, you have done a disgraceful thing!

children.text:
*niśvasya nabho vilokya**
nanu bho hatavidhe kṛpāvirahita bharatakulavimukha
VERSE_4.9
api nāma bhavenmṛtyurna ca hantā vṛkodaraḥ /
children.translated_text:
*Sighing, looking at the sky*
Alas, O wretched Fate, devoid of mercy, turned against the <s>Bharata</s> clan!
[Verse 4.9]
Would that death might come, but not at the hands of <s>Vṛkodara</s> as the slayer!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
śāntaṃ pāpaṃ śāntaṃ pāpam / mahārāja kimidam /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer):]
Perish the evil thought, perish the evil thought! Great King, what is this?
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
[Verse 4.9]
With all my kinsmen slain, what use is kingdom or victory to me? (4.9)
*Then enters <s>Sundaraka</s>, his body adorned with bandages bound over wounds from arrow-strikes.*

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_102}ajjā abi ṇāma imassiṃ uddese sārahidudīo diṭṭho tumhehiṃ mahārāadujjohaṇo ṇa vetti *nirūpya**
kahaṃ ṇa ko bi mantedi / hodu / edāṇaṃ baddhapariarāṇaṃ purisāṇaṃ samūho dīsai / ettha gadua pucchissaṃ* /parikramya vilokya ca**
kahaṃ ede kkhu sassāmiṇo gāḍhappahārahadassa ghaṇasaṃṇāhajāladubbhejjamuhehiṃ kaṅkavadaṇehiṃ hiaādo sallāiṃ uddharanti / tā ṇa kkhu ede jāṇanti / hodu / aṇṇado viciṇaissaṃ* /agrato 'valokya kiṃcitparikramya**
ime kkhu abare pahūdadarā saṃgadā vīramaṇussā dīsanti / tā ettha gadua pucchissaṃ* /upagamya**
haṃho jāṇaha tumhe kassiṃ uddese kuruṇāho vaṭṭai tti* /dṛṣṭvā**
kahaṃ ede bi maṃ pekkhia ahiadaraṃ roanti / tā ṇa hu ede bi jāṇanti / hā adikaruṇaṃ kkhu ettha vaṭṭai / esā vīramādā samalaviṇihadaṃ puttaaṃ suṇia rattaṃsuaṇivasaṇāe samaggabhūsaṇāe vahūe saha aṇumaradi* /saślāgham**
sāhu vīramāde sāhu / aṇṇassiṃ bi jammantare aṇihadaputtaā huvissasi / hodu / aṇṇado viciṇaissaṃ* /anyato vilokya**
aaṃ abaro bahuppahāraṇihadakāo akidavvaṇappaḍīāro evva johasamūho imaṃ suṇṇāsaṇaṃ tulaṃgamaṃ ubālahia roidi / ṇūṇaṃ edāṇaṃ ettha evva sāmī vābādido / tā ṇa hu ede bi jāṇanti / hodu / aṇṇado gadua pucchissaṃ* /sarvato vilokya**
kahaṃ savvo evva avatthāṇurūbaṃ visaṇaṃ aṇuhavanto bhāadheavimuhadāe pajjāulo jaṇo / tā kaṃ ettha pucchissaṃ / kaṃ vā ubālahissaṃ / hodu / saaṃ evva ettha viciṇaissaṃ* /parikramya**
hodu / devvaṃ dāṇīṃ ubālahissaṃ / haṃho devva eādasāṇaṃ akkhohiṇīṇaṃ ṇāho jeṭṭho bhādusadassa bhattā gaṅgeaddoṇaṅgarāasallakibakidavammassatthāmappamuhassa rāacakkassa saalapahuvīmaṇḍalekkaṇāho mahārāadujjohaṇo bi aṇṇesīadi / aṇṇesīanto bi ṇa jāṇīadi kassiṃ uddese vaṭṭai tti* /vicintya niḥśvasya ca**
aha vā kiṃ ettha devvaṃ ubālahāmi / tassa kkhu edaṃ ṇibbhacchiaviuravaaṇavīassa avahīridapidāmahahidobadesaṅkurassa sauṇippocchāhaṇādivirūḍhamūlassa jadugehajūdavisasāhiṇo saṃbhūdaciraālasaṃbaddhaverālavālassa pañcālīkesaggahaṇakusumassa phalaṃ pariṇamadi* /anyato vilokya**
jahā ettha eso viviharaaṇappahāsaṃvalidasūrakiraṇappasūdasakkacābasahassasaṃpūridadasadisāmuho lūṇakeduvaṃso raho dīsai tā ahaṃ takkemi avassaṃ ediṇā mahārāadujjohaṇassa vissāmuddeseṇa hodavvaṃ / jāva ṇirūbemi* /upagamya dṛṣṭvā niśvasya ca**
kadhaṃ eādasāṇaṃ akkhohiṇīṇaṃ ṇāako bhavia mahārāo dujjohaṇo pāidapuriso via asalāhaṇīe bhūmie upaviṭṭho ciṭṭhadi / atha vā tassa kkhu edaṃ pañcālīkesaggahakusumassa phalaṃ pariṇamadi /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Sundaraka</s>:]
[Prakrit] Masters, has the chariot of great king <s>Duryodhana</s>, with a trustworthy guide, been spotted by you in this area? He doesn't know.
*Looking about*
What — no one answers? So be it. Now a group of men with bound armor can be seen. Let me go there and ask.
*Walking around and looking*
What — these men, servants of their master, are extracting arrows from the hearts [of warriors] with arrow-headed forceps, whose faces are impenetrable through dense layers of armor, [warriors] struck by heavy blows. So they do not know either. So be it — I shall search elsewhere.
*Looking ahead and walking a little*
These appear to be brave men, open-handed and valiant, gathered together. Let me go there and ask.
*Approaching*
Ho there! Do you know in which area the <s>Kuru</s> lord is to be found?
*Seeing*
What — even these, upon seeing me, weep all the more! So they too do not know. Ah, most pitiful is what is happening here. There is a heroic mother who, hearing that her son has been killed in battle, grieves together with his wife, who wears blood-stained garments and all her ornaments.
*With admiration*
Well done, O heroic mother, well done! In another birth too, you shall be a mother of unslain sons! So be it — I shall search elsewhere.
*Looking in another direction*
Ah, this army — their bodies slain by numerous blows, with no reciprocation of deeds possible — is weeping, lifting up this empty saddle-horse. Surely the master has been injured in this very place. But they too do not know. So be it — let me go elsewhere and ask.
*Looking in all directions*
How is it that all the people, experiencing grief appropriate to their circumstances, are in utter distress from the turn of fate's face against them? Whom shall I ask here? Whom shall I approach? So be it — I shall search here by myself.
*Walking around*
So be it — I shall now beseech the gods. Ho there, O gods! The lord of eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> (army divisions), the eldest of a hundred brothers, the husband of <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s... the king <s>Duryodhana</s>, foremost jewel of the entire assembly of great warriors — of <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), <s>Śalya</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Aśvatthāman</s> and others — is being searched for! And though being searched for, it is not known in which area he is to be found!
*Reflecting and sighing*
Or rather, why should I beseech the gods here? For this is indeed the fruit now ripening of that dice-game tree, poisonous to the family — whose hero's face of fearless valor was disregarded, whose sprout of counsel beneficial to the father's great purpose was pushed aside, whose root had grown from the urging of <s>Śakuni</s>, whose trench-bed was the long-accumulated enmity, and whose flower was the seizing of <s>Pāñcālī</s>'s (<s>Draupadī</s>'s) hair!
*Looking in another direction*
Since here this chariot is seen with its banner-staff cut down, the surrounding ten directions filled with the brilliance of thousands of bare swords gleaming in the spreading sunshine, playing about in the open battlefield — I surmise that this must be the resting place of great king <s>Duryodhana</s>. Let me look closely.
*Approaching, seeing, and sighing*
How is it that the great king <s>Duryodhana</s>, having been the lord of eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s>, sits upon inglorious ground like a common man? But then, this is indeed the fruit now ripening of that flower which was the seizing of <s>Pāñcālī</s>'s hair.

children.text:
SktCh_102: āryāḥ api nāmāsmindeśe sārathidvitīyo dṛṣṭo yuṣmābhirmahārājaduryodhano na veti / kathaṃ na ko 'pi mantrayate / bhavatu / eteṣāṃ baddhaparikarāṇāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ samūho dṛśyate / atra gatvā prakṣyāmi / kathamete khalu svasvāmino gāḍhaprahārahatasya ghanasaṃnāhajāladurbhedyamukhaiḥ kaṅkavadanairhṛdayācchalyānyuddharanti / tanna khalvete jānanti / bhavatu / anyato viceṣyāmi / ime khalvapare prabhūtatarāḥ saṃgatā vīramanuṣyā dṛśyante / tadatra gatvā prakṣyāmi / haṃho jānītha yūyaṃ kasminnuddeśe kurunātho vartata iti / kathamete 'pi māṃ prekṣyādhikataraṃ rudanti / tanna khalvete 'pi jānanti / hā atikaruṇaṃ khalvatra vartate / eṣā vīramātā samaravinihataṃ putrakaṃ śrutvā raktāṃśukanivasanayā samagrabhuṣaṇayā vadhvā sahānumriyate / sādhu vīramātaḥ sādhu / anyasminnapi janmāntare 'nihataputrakā bhaviṣyasi / bhavatu / anyato viceṣyāmi / ayamaparo bahuprahāranihatakāyo 'kṛtavraṇabandha eva yodhasamūha imaṃ śūnyāsanaṃ turaṃgamamupālabhya roditi / nūnameteṣāmatraiva svāmī vyāpāditaḥ / tanna khalvete 'pi jānanti / bhavatu / anyato gatvā prakṣyāmi / kathaṃ sarva evāvasthānurūpaṃ vyasanamanubhavanbhāgadheyavimukhatayā paryākulo janaḥ / tatkamatra prakṣyāmi / kaṃ vopālapsye / bhavatu / svayamevātra viceṣyāmi / bhavatu / daivamidānīmupālapsye / haṃho daiva ekādaśānāmakṣauhiṇīnāṃ nātho jyeṣṭho bhrātṛśatasya bhartā gāṅgeyadroṇāṅgarājaśalyakṛpakṛtavarmāśvatthāmapramukhasya rājacakrasya sakalapṛthvīmaṇḍalaikanātho mahārājaduryodhano 'pyanviṣyate / anviṣyamāṇo 'pi na jñāyate kasminnuddeśe vartata iti / atha vā kimatra daivamupālabhe / tasya khalvidaṃ
nirbhartsitaviduravacanabījasyāvadhīritapitāmahahitopadeśāṅkurasya śakuniprotsāhanādivirūḍhamūlasya jatugṛhadyūtaviṣaśākhinaḥ saṃbhūtacirakālasaṃbaddhavairālavālasya pāñcālīkeśagrahaṇakusumasya phalaṃ pariṇamati / yathātraiva vividharatnaprabhāsaṃvalitasūryakiraṇaprasūtaśakracāpasahasrasaṃpūritadaśadiśāmukho lūnaketavaṃśo ratho dṛśyate tathāhaṃ tarkayāmyavaśyametena mahārājaduryodhanasya viśrāmoddeśena bhavitavyamiti / yāvannirūpayāmi / kathamekādaśānāmakṣauhiṇīnāṃ nāyako bhūtvā mahārājo duryodhanaḥ prākṛtapuruṣa ivāślāghanīyāyāṃ bhūmāvupavaṣṭastiṣṭhati / atha vā tasya khalvidaṃ pāñcālīkeśagrahakusumasya phalaṃ pariṇamati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Noble ones, have any of you seen in this region the great king <s>Duryodhana</s> accompanied by his charioteer, or not? Why does no one answer? So be it. I see a crowd of men with their equipment fastened. I shall go there and ask. How is it that these men are extracting arrows from the hearts of their masters, who have been struck by fierce blows, through the openings of their thick, impenetrable armor-mesh, using heron-faced [forceps]? No, they do not know. So be it. I shall search elsewhere. Here I see another, larger group of heroic men assembled. I shall go there and ask. Ho! Do you know in which direction the lord of the <s>Kurus</s> abides? Why do even these weep all the more upon seeing me? No, they too do not know. Alas, how exceedingly pitiful is the scene here! Here a hero's mother, upon hearing that her son has been slain in battle, is preparing to die along with her daughter-in-law, who is clad in blood-red garments and wearing all her ornaments. Well done, O mother of a hero, well done! In another birth too, may you have a son who is never slain. So be it. I shall search elsewhere. Here is yet another troop of warriors, their bodies struck by many blows, still without bandages on their wounds, weeping upon finding this horse with an empty saddle. Surely their master was slain right here. No, they too do not know. So be it. I shall go elsewhere and ask. Alas, everyone is experiencing sorrow befitting their circumstances, bewildered by the cruelty of fate! Then whom shall I ask here? Whom shall I reproach? So be it. I shall search here by myself. Very well. Now I shall reproach Fate! Ho, Fate! He who was the lord of eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> (army divisions), the eldest of a hundred brothers, the master [of a court] headed by <s>Gāṅgeya</s> (Bhīṣma), <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (Karṇa), <s>Śalya</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Kṛtavarman</s>, and <s>Aśvatthāman</s> — the sole sovereign of the entire circle of the earth, the great king <s>Duryodhana</s> — is being searched for! And though searched for, it is not known in which region he abides! Or rather, why do I blame Fate here? For this indeed is the fruit of that tree [of enmity] — whose seed was the scorning of <s>Vidura</s>'s counsel, whose sprout was the disregard of the grandfather's (<s>Bhīṣma</s>'s) beneficial advice, whose root grew strong through <s>Śakuni</s>'s instigation, whose branches were the house of lac, the gambling match, and poison, whose basin was the long-accumulated and deep-seated enmity, and whose blossom was the seizing of <s>Pāñcālī</s>'s (Draupadī's) hair — that fruit is now ripening. Inasmuch as right here I see a chariot with its flagstaff cut down, its ten directions filled with thousands of rainbows produced by the sun's rays mingled with the radiance of diverse gems — I surmise that this must be the resting place of the great king <s>Duryodhana</s>. Let me look closely. What! Having been the commander of eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s>, the great king <s>Duryodhana</s> sits upon the bare ground like a common man, in a place unworthy of praise! Or rather, this indeed is the fruit ripening — of that tree whose blossom was the seizing of <s>Pāñcālī</s>'s hair.
*[He approaches and questions the charioteer by gestures.]*
<s>Sūta</s> (charioteer): *[Seeing him]* Oh! How has <s>Sundaraka</s> returned from the battle?
<s>Sundaraka</s>: *[Approaching]* [Prakrit] Victory, victory to the great king!
[Sanskrit rendering:] Victory, victory to the great king!
<s>Duryodhana</s>: *[Looking]* Oh, <s>Sundaraka</s>! <s>Sundaraka</s>, is all well with <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>)?
<s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Your Majesty, he is well — in body only.
[Sanskrit rendering:] Your Majesty, he is well — in body only.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*sasaṃbhramam**
sundaraka kiṃ kirīṭināsya nihatā dhaureyā hataḥ sārathirbhagno vā rathaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Duryodhana</s>: *[With alarm]* <s>Sundaraka</s>! What — have the chief warriors of <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) been slain? Has his charioteer been killed? Or has his chariot been shattered?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_105}deva ṇa bhaggo raho / se maṇoraho bi /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Your Majesty, the chariot is not shattered. Not even his desire!

children.text: SktCh_105: deva na bhagno rathaḥ / asya manoratho 'pi /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Your Majesty, the chariot is not shattered. Not even his desire!

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*saroṣam**
kimavispaṣṭakathitairākulamapi paryākulayasi me hṛdayam / tadaśeṣato vispaṣṭaṃ kathyatām /
children.translated_text: <s>Duryodhana</s>: *[Angrily]* Why do you confuse my already troubled heart with unclear speech? Tell everything plainly and completely!

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_106}jaṃ devo āṇabedi / ae devassa muuḍamaṇippahāveṇa abaṇīdā me raṇappahāraveaṇā* /iti sāṭopaṃ parikramya**
suṇādu devo / atthi dāṇiṃ kumāladussāsaṇavaha* /ityardhokte mukhamācchādya śaṅkāṃ nāṭayati**
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] As Your Majesty commands. Ah, by the power of Your Majesty's crest-jewel, my pain from battle-wounds has vanished! *[Strutting about proudly]* Hear, Your Majesty! There is now the matter of Prince <s>Duḥśāsana</s>'s slay— *[He covers his mouth mid-word and mimes apprehension.]*

children.text: SktCh_106: yaddeva ājñāpayati / aye devasya mukuṭamaṇiprabhāveṇāpanītā me raṇaprahāravedanā / śṛṇotu devaḥ / astīdānīṃ kumāraduḥśāsanavadha /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] As Your Majesty commands. Ah, by the power of Your Majesty's crest-jewel, my pain from battle-wounds has vanished! Hear, Your Majesty! There is now the matter of Prince <s>Duḥśāsana</s>'s slaying—
<s>Sūta</s> (charioteer): <s>Sundaraka</s>, speak! Fate has already spoken it.
<s>Duryodhana</s>: Speak! We have heard it.

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_107}saṇādu devo / ajja dāva kumāladussāsaṇavahāmarisideṇa sāmiṇā aṅgarāeṇa kuḍilabhiuḍībhaṅgabhīsaṇaṇiḍalabaṭṭeṇa aviṇṇādasaṃdhāṇamokkhasilīmuhasaṃghādavarisiṇā abhijutto so durāāro majjhamapaṇḍavo bhīmaseṇahadao /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Hear, Your Majesty! Today, the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), enraged by the slaying of Prince <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, with a terrifyingly furrowed brow upon his forehead, showering arrows whose stringing and release were imperceptible, attacked that wicked middle <s>Pāṇḍava</s> — that wretch <s>Bhīmasena</s> was struck down!

children.text: SktCh_107: śṛṇotu devaḥ / adya tāvatkumāraduḥśāsanavadhāmarṣitena svāmināṅgarājena kuṭilabhrukuṭībhaṅgabhīṣaṇaniṭalapaṭṭenāvijñātasaṃdhānamokṣaśilīmukhasaṃghātavarṣiṇābhiyuktaḥ sa durācāro madhyamapāṇḍavo bhīmasenahatakaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Hear, Your Majesty! Today, the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), enraged by the slaying of Prince <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, with a terrifyingly furrowed brow upon his forehead, showering arrows whose stringing and release were imperceptible, attacked that wicked middle <s>Pāṇḍava</s> — that wretch <s>Bhīmasena</s> was struck down!
Both: Then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_108}tado deva uhaabalamilantadippantakarituraapadādisamubbhūdadhūliṇiareṇa pallatthagaaghaḍāsaṃghādeṇa a vittharanteṇa andhaāreṇa andhīkidaṃ uhaabalaṃ / ṇa hu gagaṇatalaṃ lakkhīadi /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, Your Majesty, both armies were blinded by the darkness spreading from the dense dust raised by the elephants, horses, and infantry of both forces, combined with the massed elephant-columns collapsing. The sky itself could not be seen!

children.text: SktCh_108: tato deva ubhayabalamiladdīpyamānakarituragapadātisamudbhūtadhūlinikareṇa paryastagajaghaṭāsaṃghātena ca vistīrṇamānenāndhakāreṇāndhīkṛtamubhayabalam / na khalu gaganatalaṃ lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Then, Your Majesty, both armies were blinded by the darkness spreading from the dense dust raised by the blazing elephants, horses, and infantry of both forces, combined with the overturned elephant-column masses. Indeed, the sky itself could not be seen!
Both: Then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_109}tado deva dūrākaṭṭhiadhaṇugguṇācchoḍaṇaṭaṃkāreṇa gambhīrabhīsaṇeṇa jāṇīadi gajjidaṃ palaajalahareṇa tti /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, Your Majesty, from the terrifyingly deep twang of bowstrings drawn far back, one would think it was the rumbling of doomsday storm-clouds!

children.text: SktCh_109: tato deva dūrākṛṣṭadhanurguṇācchoṭanaṭaṃkāreṇa gambhīrabhīṣaṇena jñāyate garjitaṃ pralayajaladhareṇeti /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Then, Your Majesty, by the terrifyingly deep twang of bowstrings drawn far back, one would think it was the thunder of doomsday storm-clouds!
<s>Duryodhana</s>: Then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_110}tado deva doṇṇaṃ bi tāṇaṃ aṇṇoṇṇasiṃhaṇādagajjidapisuṇaṃ vivihaparimukkappaharaṇāhadakavaasaṃgalidajjalaṇavijjucchaḍābhāsuraṃ gambhīratthaṇiacāpajalaharaṃ ppasarantasaradhārāsahassavarisaṃ jādaṃ samaraduddiṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, Your Majesty, between those two arose a terrible storm of battle — heralded by the mutual lion-roars of each, blazing with lightning-flashes of fire sparked from weapons striking armor, with the deep thunder of their bows as storm-clouds, raining thousands of streaming arrow-showers!

children.text: SktCh_110: tato deva dvayorapi tayoranyo 'nyasiṃhanādagarjitapiśunaṃ vividhaparimuktapraharaṇāhatakavacasaṃgalitajvalanavidyucchaṭābhāsuraṃ gambhīrastanitacāpajaladharaṃ prasaraccharadhārāsahasravarṣi jātaṃ samaradurdinam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Then, Your Majesty, between those two arose a terrible storm of battle — heralded by the mutual lion-roars of each, blazing with lightning-flashes of fire sparked from the various weapons striking armor, with the deep thunder of their bows as storm-clouds, raining thousands of streaming arrow-showers!
<s>Duryodhana</s>: Then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_111}tado a deva edassiṃ antare jeṭṭhassa bhāduṇo parābhavasaṅkiṇā dhaṇaṃjaeṇa vajjaṇigghādaṇigghosavisamarasidadhaaaggaṭṭhidamahāvāṇaro turaṃgamasaṃvāhaṇavāpidavāsudevasaṅkhacakkāsigadālañchidacaubbāhudaṇḍaduddaṃsaṇo āpūriapañcajaṇṇadeadattatārarasidappaḍiravabharidadasadisāmuhakuharo dhāvido taṃ uddesaṃ rahavaro /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, Your Majesty, in the midst of this, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), fearing the defeat of his eldest brother, rushed his great chariot to that place — with the mighty monkey (<s>Hanumān</s>) seated atop the flag-staff roaring terribly with a sound rivaling thunder-claps, with <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) busy driving the horses, displaying the dread sight of his four arms marked with conch, discus, sword, and mace, filling all ten directions with the reverberating blasts of the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> and <s>Devadatta</s> conch-shells!

children.text: SktCh_111: tataśca deva etasminnantare jyeṣṭhasya bhrātuḥ parābhavaśaṅkinā dhanaṃjayena vajranirghātanirghoṣaviṣamarasitadhvajāgrasthitamahāvānarasturaṃgamasaṃvāhanavyāpṛtavāsudevaśaṅkhacakrāsigadālāñchitacaturbāhudaṇḍadurdarśana āpūritapāñcajanyadevadattatārarasitapratiravabharitadaśadiśāmukhakuharo dhāvitastamuddeśaṃ rathavaraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Then, Your Majesty, in the midst of this, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), fearing the defeat of his eldest brother, rushed his great chariot to that place — with the mighty monkey atop the flag-staff roaring terribly with a sound rivaling thunder-claps, with <s>Vāsudeva</s> busy driving the horses, displaying the dread sight of his four arms marked with conch, discus, sword, and mace, the ten directions resounding with the reverberating blasts of the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> and <s>Devadatta</s> conch-shells!
<s>Duryodhana</s>: Then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_112}tado bhīmaseṇadhanaṃjaehiṃ abhijuttaṃ pidaraṃ pekkhia sasaṃbhamaṃ vialiaṃ avadhūṇia raaṇasīsaaṃ ākaṇṇākaṭṭhidakaṭhiṇakodaṇḍajīo dāhiṇahatthukkhittasarapuṅkhavighaṭṭaṇatuvarāidasārahio taṃ desaṃ ubagado kumālavisaseṇo /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, seeing his father being assailed by <s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> (son of <s>Karṇa</s>) hastily shook off his alarm, cast aside his jeweled head-ornament, drew his stiff bow to his ear, and with the quickness of a charioteer urged by the flicking of arrow-notches tossed from his right hand, rushed to that place!

children.text: SktCh_112: tato bhīmasenadhanaṃjayābhyāmabhiyuktaṃ pitaraṃ prekṣya sasaṃbhramaṃ vigalitamavadhūya ratnaśīrṣakamākarṇākṛṣṭakaṭhinakodaṇḍajīvaḥ dakṣiṇahastotkṣiptaśarapuṅkhavighaṭṭanatvaritasārathistaṃ deśamupagataḥ kumāravṛṣasenaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Then, seeing his father being assailed by <s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, having shaken off his alarm, cast aside his jeweled head-ornament, drew his stiff bow to his ear, and with the charioteer hastened by the flicking of arrow-notches tossed from his right hand, arrived at that place!
<s>Duryodhana</s>: *[With pride]* Then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_113}tado a deva teṇa āacchanteṇa evva kumālavisaseṇeṇa vidalidāsiladāsāmalasiṇiddhapuṅkhehiṃ kaṭhiṇakaṅkabattehiṃ kisaṇavaṇṇehiṃ sāṇasilāṇisidasāmalasallabandhehiṃ kusumido via tarū muhuttaeṇa silīmuhehiṃ pacchādido dhaṇaṃjaassa rahavaro /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, Your Majesty, even as Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> was still approaching, within a moment, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>'s great chariot was covered with his arrows — hard-feathered, dark-hued, with smooth polished shafts dark as split stone, sharpened on whetstone, their iron points gleaming — as if a tree were in bloom with flowers!

children.text: SktCh_113: tataśca deva tenāgacchataiva kumāravṛṣasenena vidalitāsilatāśyāmalasnigdhapuṅkhaiḥ kaṭhinakaṅkapatraiḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaiḥ śāṇaśilāniśitaśyāmalaśalyabandhaiḥ kusumita iva tarurmuhūrtena śilīmukhaiḥ pracchādito dhanaṃjayasya rathavaraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Then, Your Majesty, even as Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> was still approaching, within a moment, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>'s great chariot was covered with his arrows — hard, heron-feathered, dark-hued, with smooth polished shafts gleaming like split dark stone, sharpened on whetstone — as if a tree were flowering with blossoms!
Both: *[With joy]* Then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_114}tado deva tikkhavikkhittaṇisidabhallabāṇavarisiṇā dhaṇaṃjaeṇa īsi vihasia bhaṇidaṃ / are re visaseṇa piduṇo bi dāva de ṇa juttaṃ maha kubidassa abhimuhaṃ ṭhāduṃ / kiṃ uṇa bhavado bālassa / tā gaccha / abarehiṃ kumārehiṃ saha āodhehi tti / evvaṃ vāaṃ ṇisamia guraaṇāhikkhebeṇa uddībiakobobarattamuhamaṇḍalaviambhiabhiuḍībhaṅgabhīsaṇeṇa cābadhāriṇā kumālavisaseṇeṇa bi mammabhedaehiṃ parusavisamehiṃ sudivahakidappaṇaehiṃ ṇibbhacchido gaṇḍīvī bāṇehiṃ ṇa uṇa duṭṭhavaaṇehiṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, Your Majesty, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, who was showering sharp, well-aimed, and deadly <s>bhalla</s>-arrows, said with a slight smile: 'Ho there, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>! It is not fitting even for your father to stand before me when I am angered — how much less for you, a mere boy! Go then! Fight with the other princes!' Upon hearing these words, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, the bow-wielder, his face reddened with fury kindled by the insult to his elders, his furrowed brow terrifying, rebuked the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> — not with harsh words, but with arrows that pierced the vital joints, that were cruel and dreadful, and that had long been prepared with loving care!

children.text: SktCh_114: tato deva tīkṣṇavikṣiptaniśitabhallabāṇavarṣiṇā dhanaṃjayeneṣadvihasya bhaṇitam / are re vṛṣasena piturapi tāvatte na yuktaṃ mama kupitasyābhimukhaṃ sthātum / kiṃ punarbhavato bālasya / tadgaccha / aparaiḥ kumāraiḥ sahāyudhyasveti / evaṃ vācaṃ niśamya gurujanādhikṣepeṇoddīpitakopoparaktamukhamaṇḍalavijṛmbhitabhrukuṭībhaṅgabhīṣaṇena cāpadhāriṇā kumāravṛṣasenenāpi marmabhedakaiḥ paruṣaviṣamaiḥ śrutipathakṛtapraṇayairnirbhartsito gāṇḍīvī bāṇairna punarduṣṭavacanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Then, Your Majesty, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, who was showering sharp, well-aimed, and deadly <s>bhalla</s>-arrows, said with a slight smile: 'Ho there, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>! It is not fitting even for your father to stand before me when I am angered — how much less for you, a mere boy! Go then! Fight with the other princes!' Upon hearing these words, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, the bow-wielder, his face reddened with fury kindled by the insult to his elders, his furrowed brow terrifying, rebuked the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> — not with harsh words, but with arrows that pierced the vital joints, that were cruel and terrible, and that had found their way to the ears [of the listener]!
<s>Duryodhana</s>: Well done, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, well done! <s>Sundaraka</s>, then what? Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_115}tado deva ṇisidasarābhighādaveaṇopajādamaṇṇuṇā kirīṭiṇā caṇḍagaṇḍīvajīāsaddaṇijjidavajjaṇigghādaghoseṇa bāṇaṇipadaṇapaḍisiddhadaṃsaṇappasareṇa patthudaṃ sikkhābalāṇurūbaṃ kiṃ bi accaliaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundaraka</s>: [Prakrit] Then, Your Majesty, <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), feeling the pain of being struck by sharp arrows, with the fierce sound of his <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow-string drowning out even thunderclaps, his vision obstructed by the dense fall of arrows, began something extraordinary, befitting his training and strength—

children.text: SktCh_115: tato deva niśitaśarābhighātavedanopajātamanyunā kirīṭinā caṇḍagāṇḍīvajīvāśabdanirjitavajranirghātaghoṣeṇa bāṇanipatanapratiṣiddhadarśanaprasareṇa prastutaṃ śikṣābalānurūpaṃ kimapyāścaryam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 115:] Then, O lord, by <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), enraged by the pain of sharp arrow-blows, whose fierce <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow-string sound defeated the crash of thunderbolts, and whose rain of arrows blocked the range of vision, there was begun some extraordinary feat befitting his martial training.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with deliberate intent) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_116}tado a deva taṃ tārisaṃ pekkhia sattuṇo samaravvābāracaurattaṇaṃ avibhāviatūṇīramuhadhaṇugguṇagamaṇāgamaṇasarasaṃdhāṇamokkhacaḍulakaraaleṇa kumālavisaseṇeṇa bi savisesaṃ patthudaṃ samalakamma /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 116) Then, O lord, seeing such battle-skill of the enemy, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> too, with hands so swift that the coming and going of arrows from quiver-mouth to bow-string could not be perceived — their stringing and release — began his combat with even greater distinction.

children.text: SktCh_116: tataśca deva tattādṛśaṃ prekṣya śatroḥ samaravyāpāracaturatvamavibhāvitatūṇīramukhadhanurguṇagamanāgamanaśarasaṃdhānamokṣacaṭulakaratalena kumāravṛṣasenenāpi saviśeṣaṃ prastutaṃ samarakarma /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 116:] Then, O lord, seeing such battle-craft of the enemy, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> too, with hands so swift that the coming and going of arrows from quiver-mouth to bow-string, their stringing and release, could not be perceived, began his combat with even greater distinction.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_117}tado deva etthantare vimukkasamaravvābāro muhuttavissamidaverāṇubandho doṇaṃ bi kururāapaṇḍavabalāṇaṃ sāhu kumālavisaseṇa sāhu tti kidakalaalo vīraloo avaloiduṃ pautto /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 117) Then, O lord, in this interval, having paused from the engagement of battle, with enmity rested for a moment, the warrior-assembly of both the <s>Kuru</s> king's and the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> forces, raising a clamor of 'Well done, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, well done!' began to watch.

children.text: SktCh_117: tato deva atrāntare vimuktasamaravyāpāro muhūrtaviśramitavairānubandho dvayorapi kururājapāṇḍavabalayoḥ sādhu kumāravṛṣasena sādhviti kṛtakalakalo vīraloko 'valokayituṃ pravṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 117:] Then, O lord, in this interval, having ceased from the engagement of battle, with enmity rested for a moment, the warrior-assembly of both the <s>Kuru</s> king's and the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> forces, raising a clamor of 'Well done, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, well done!' began to watch.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with astonishment) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_118}tado a deva avahīridasaaladhāṇukkacakkaparakkamasāliṇo sudassa tahāviheṇa samalakammālambheṇa harisarosakaruṇāsaṃkaḍe vaṭṭamāṇassa sāmiṇo aṅgarāassa ṇipaḍiā sarapaddhaī bhīmaseṇe bapphapajjāulā diṭṭhī kumālavisaseṇe /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 118) Then, O lord, upon his son, who shamed the valor of all bowmen, beginning such a battle-engagement — upon the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), caught between joy, anger, and compassion — there fell a rain of arrows upon <s>Bhīmasena</s>, and a tear-clouded gaze upon Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>.

children.text: SktCh_118: tataśca deva avadhīritasakaladhānuṣkacakraparākramaśālinaḥ sutasya tathāvidhena samarakarmārambheṇa harṣaroṣakaruṇāsaṃkaṭe vartamānasya svāmino 'ṅgarājasya nipatitā śarapaddhatirbhīmasene bāṣpaparyākulā dṛṣṭiḥ kumāravṛṣasene /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 118:] Then, O lord, upon his son, who shamed the valor of all bowmen, beginning such a battle-engagement — upon the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), caught between joy, anger, and compassion — there fell a rain of arrows upon <s>Bhīmasena</s>, and a tear-clouded gaze upon Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with fear) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_119}tado a deva uhaabalappauttasāhukārāmarisideṇa saravarisappajjalideṇa gaṇḍīviṇā turaesu sārahiṃ pi rahavare dhaṇuṃ pi jīāiṃ pi ṇalindalañchaṇe sidādabatte bi a vābārido samaṃ silīmuhāsāro /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 119) Then, O lord, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, angered by the cheers of both armies, blazing with a shower of arrows, directed a simultaneous rain of shafts upon the horses, the charioteer, the great chariot, the bow, the bowstring, and the royal parasol — the insignia of a king.

children.text: SktCh_119: tataśca deva ubhayabalapravṛttasādhukārāmarṣitena śaravarṣaprajvalitena gāṇḍīvinā turageṣu sārathāvapi rathavare dhanuṣyapi jīvāyāmapi narendralāñchane sitātapatre 'pi ca vyāpāritaḥ samaṃ śilīmukhāsāraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 119:] Then, O lord, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, angered by the cheers of both armies, blazing with a shower of arrows, directed a simultaneous rain of shafts upon the horses, the charioteer, the great chariot, the bow, the bowstring, and the white royal parasol — the insignia of a king.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with fear) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_120}tado deva viraho lūṇaguṇakodaṇḍo paribbhamaṇavvābāramettappaḍisiddhasarasaṃpādo maṇḍalehiṃ viariduṃ pautto kumālo /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 120) Then, O lord, the prince, deprived of his chariot, his bow-string cut, prevented from acquiring arrows only by the whirling evasive maneuvers, began to move in circles.

children.text: SktCh_120: tato deva viratho lūnaguṇakodaṇḍaḥ paribhramaṇavyāpāramātrapratiṣiddhaśarasaṃpāto maṇḍalairvicarituṃ pravṛttaḥ kamāraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 120:] Then, O lord, the prince, deprived of his chariot, his bow-string cut, prevented from acquiring arrows only by the whirling evasive maneuvers, began to move in circles.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with apprehension) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_121}tado deva sudarahaviddhaṃsaṇāmarisuddībideṇa sāmiṇā aṅgarāeṇa agaṇiabhīmaseṇābhijoeṇa parimukko dhaṇaṃjaassa ubari silīmuhāsāro / kumālo bi parijaṇobaṇīdaṃ aṇṇaṃ rahaṃ āruhia puṇo bi pautto dhaṇaṃjaeṇa saha āodheduṃ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 121) Then, O lord, the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), inflamed with anger at the destruction of his son's chariot, disregarding the attack of <s>Bhīmasena</s>, unleashed a rain of shafts upon <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>). And the prince, mounting another chariot brought by his attendants, began again to fight with <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.

children.text: SktCh_121: tato deva sutarathavidhvaṃsanāmarṣoddīpitena svāmināṅgarājenāgaṇitabhīmasenābhiyogena parimukto dhanaṃjayasyopari śilīmukhāsāraḥ / kumāro 'pi parijanopanītamanyaṃ rathamāruhya punarapi pravṛtto dhanaṃjayena sahāyoddhum /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 121:] Then, O lord, the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s>, inflamed with anger at the destruction of his son's chariot, disregarding the attack of <s>Bhīmasena</s>, unleashed a rain of shafts upon <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>. And the prince, mounting another chariot brought by his attendants, began again to fight with <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
[Both:] Well done, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, well done! Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_122}tado deva bhaṇidaṃ a kumāleṇa re re tādāhikkhebamuhala majjhamapaṇḍava maha sarā tuha sarīraṃ ujjhia aṇṇassiṃ ṇa ṇibaḍanti / tti bhaṇia sarasahassehiṃ paṇḍavasarīraṃ pacchādia siṃhaṇādeṇa gajjiduṃ pautto /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 122) Then, O lord, the prince said: 'Ho, ho, middle <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, loud with insults to my father! My arrows, having left your body, do not fall upon another!' Having said this, covering the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>'s body with thousands of arrows, he began to roar with a lion's roar.

children.text: SktCh_122: tato deva bhaṇitaṃ ca kumāreṇa re re tātādhikṣepamukhara madhyamapāṇḍava mama śarāstava śarīramujjhitvānyasminna nipatanti / iti bhaṇitvā śarasahasraiḥ pāṇḍavaśarīraṃ pracchādya siṃhanādena garjituṃ pravṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 122:] Then, O lord, the prince said: 'Ho, ho, middle <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, loud with insults to my father! My arrows, having left your body, do not fall upon another!' Having said this, covering the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>'s body with thousands of arrows, he began to roar with a lion's roar.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with astonishment) Oh, the valor of the boy, though of innocent nature! Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_123}tado a deva taṃ sarasaṃpādaṃ samavadhūṇia ṇisidasarābhighādajādamaṇṇuṇā kirīṭiṇā gahidā rahucchaṅgādo kaṇantakaṇaakiṅkiṇījālajhaṃkāravirāiṇī mehobarohavimukkaṇahatthalaṇimmalā ṇisidasāmalasiṇiddhamuhī viviharaaṇappahābhāsurabhīsaṇaramaṇīadaṃsaṇā sattī sobahāsaṃ vimukkā a kumālāhimuhī /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 123) Then, O lord, by <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), enraged by the blows of sharp arrows, shaking off that rain of arrows — a <s>śakti</s> (lance) was seized from the chariot-seat, jingling with its net of tinkling golden bells, bright as the sky freed from the obstruction of clouds, with a sharp, dark, smooth point, wondrous and terrible to behold with the splendor of various gems — and hurled with a laugh, aimed at the prince.

children.text: SktCh_123: tataśca deva taṃ śarasaṃpātaṃ samavadhūya niśitaśarābhighātajātamanyunā kirīṭinā gṛhītā rathotsaṅgātkvaṇatkanakakiṅkiṇījālajhaṃkāravirāviṇī meghoparodhavimuktanabhastalanirmalā niśitaśyāmalasnigdhamukhī vividharatnaprabhābhāsurabhīṣaṇaramaṇīyadarśanā śaktiḥ sopahāsaṃ vimuktā ca kumārābhimukhī /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 123:] Then, O lord, by <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), enraged by the blows of sharp arrows, shaking off that rain of arrows — a <s>śakti</s> (lance) was seized from the chariot-seat, jingling with its net of tinkling golden bells, bright as the sky freed from the obstruction of clouds, with a sharp, dark, smooth point, wondrous and terrible to behold with the splendor of various gems — and hurled with a laugh, aimed at the prince.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with sorrow) Alas! Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_124}tado a deva pajjalantiṃ sattiṃ pekkhia vialiaṃ aṅgarāassa hatthādo sasaraṃ dhaṇuṃ hiaādo vīrasulaho ucchāho ṇaaṇādo bāpphasalilaṃ vaaṇādo rasidaṃ / hasidaṃ a dhaṇaṃjaeṇa siṃhaṇādaṃ viṇādidaṃ viodaleṇa dukkalaṃ dukkalaṃ tti ākkandidaṃ kurubaleṇa /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 124) Then, O lord, upon seeing the blazing lance, from <s>Aṅgarāja</s>'s (<s>Karṇa</s>'s) hand the bow with its arrow slipped away, from his heart the heroic enthusiasm faded, from his eyes tears flowed, from his mouth a cry escaped. And <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) laughed, <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) roared a lion's roar, and the <s>Kuru</s> army cried out 'Alas, alas!'

children.text: SktCh_124: tataśca deva prajvalantīṃ śaktiṃ prekṣya vigalitamaṅgarājasya hastātsaśaraṃ dhanurhṛdayādvīrasulabha utsāho nayanādbāṣpasalilaṃ vadanādrasitam / hasitaṃ ca dhanaṃjayena siṃhanādaṃ vināditaṃ vṛkodareṇa duṣkaraṃ duṣkaramityākranditaṃ kurubalena /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 124:] Then, O lord, upon seeing the blazing lance, from <s>Aṅgarāja</s>'s hand the bow with its arrow slipped away, from his heart the heroic enthusiasm — natural to a warrior — faded, from his eyes tears flowed, from his mouth a cry escaped. And <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> laughed, <s>Vṛkodara</s> roared a lion's roar, and the <s>Kuru</s> army cried out 'Impossible! Impossible!'
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with sorrow) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_125}tado deva kumālavisaseṇeṇa ākaṇṇākiṭṭhaṇisidakhurappehiṃ ciraṃ ṇijjhāia addhapahe evva bhāīrahī via bhaavadā visamaloaṇeṇa tidhā kidā sattī /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 125) Then, O lord, by Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, with sharp razor-edged arrows drawn to the ear, having long contemplated it, the lance was cut in three, midway in its flight — just as the river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Gaṅgā) was by the blessed <s>Viṣamalocana</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, the Odd-Eyed one).

children.text: SktCh_125: tato deva kumāravṛṣasenenākarṇākṛṣṭaniśitakṣurapraiściraṃ nidhyāyārdhapatha eva bhāgīrathīva bhagavatā viṣamalocanena tridhā kṛtā śaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 125:] Then, O lord, by Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, with sharp razor-edged arrows drawn to the ear, having long contemplated it, the lance was cut in three, midway in its flight — just as the river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> was by the blessed <s>Viṣamalocana</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Well done, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, well done! Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_126}tado a deva edassiṃ antare kidakalakalamuhareṇa vīraloasāhuvādeṇa antarido samaratūraravo / siddhacālaṇagaṇavimukkakusumappakareṇa pacchādidaṃ samalaṅgaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 126) Then, O lord, in this interval, the uproar of the warrior-assembly's cries of 'Bravo!' drowned out the sound of the war drums. And the battlefield was covered with showers of flowers released by the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Cāraṇas</s> (celestial beings).

children.text: SktCh_126: tataśca deva etasminnantare kṛtakalakalamukhareṇa vīralokasādhuvādenāntaritaḥ samaratūryaravaḥ / siddhacāraṇagaṇavimuktakusumaprakareṇa pracchāditaṃ samarāṅgaṇam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 126:] Then, O lord, in this interval, the uproar of the warrior-assembly's cries of 'Bravo!' drowned out the sound of the war drums. And the battlefield was covered with showers of flowers released by the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Cāraṇas</s>.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Oh, the valor of the boy! Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_127}tado a deva bhaṇiaṃ sāmiṇā aṅgarāeṇa / bho viodala asamatto tuha maha bi samalavvābāro / tā aṇumaṇṇa maṃ muhuttaaṃ / pekkhāma dāva vacchassa tuha bhāduṇo a dhaṇuvvedasikkhāṇiuṇattaṇaṃ / tuha bi edaṃ pekkhaṇīaṃ tti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 127) Then, O lord, the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>) spoke: 'O <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>), the battle between you and me is not yet finished. So grant me a moment. Let us watch the skill in archery of the boy — your and my brother's son. This too is worth seeing.'

children.text: SktCh_127: tataśca deva bhaṇitaṃ svāmināṅgarājena / bho vṛkodara asamāptastava mamāpi samaravyāpāraḥ / tadanumanyasva māṃ muhūrtam / prekṣāvahe tāvadvatsasya tava bhrātuśca dhanurvedaśikṣānipuṇatvam / tavāpyetatprekṣaṇīyamiti /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 127:] Then, O lord, the lord <s>Aṅgarāja</s> spoke: 'O <s>Vṛkodara</s>, the battle between you and me is not yet finished. So grant me a moment. Let us watch the skill in archery of the boy and your brother. This too is worth seeing for you.'
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_128}tado deva viradā raṇavvābāraṇibbandhādo muhuttaaṃ pasamidaverā duve bi pekkhaā jādā bhīmaseṇaṅgarāā /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 128) Then, O lord, having ceased from the persistence of battle engagement, with enmity calmed for a moment, both <s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Aṅgarāja</s> became spectators.

children.text: SktCh_128: tato deva viratau raṇavyāpāranirbandhānmuhūrtaṃ praśamitavairau dvāvapi prekṣakau jātau bhīmasenāṅgarājau /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 128:] Then, O lord, having ceased from the persistence of battle engagement, with enmity calmed for a moment, both <s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Aṅgarāja</s> became spectators.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with a meaningful look) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_129}tado a deva edassiṃ antare sattikhaṇḍaṇāmarisideṇa gaṇḍīviṇā bhaṇiaṃ / are re dujjohaṇappamuhā* /ityardhokte lajjāṃ nāṭayati**
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 129) Then, O lord, in this interval, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, angered by the shattering of the lance, said: 'Ho, ho, led by <s>Duryo</s>-' (stopping mid-word, he acts out embarrassment)

children.text: SktCh_129: tataśca deva etasminnantare śaktikhaṇḍanāmarṣitena gāṇḍīvinā bhaṇitam / are re duryodhanapramukhāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 129:] Then, O lord, in this interval, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, angered by the shattering of the lance, said: 'Ho, ho, led by <s>Duryodhana</s>!'
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] <s>Sundaraka</s>, speak on! Those are another's words.

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_130}suṇādu devo / are dujjohaṇappamuhā kurubalaseṇāpahuṇaā are aviṇaaṇokaṇṇadhāra kaṇṇa tumhehiṃ maha parokkhaṃ bahuhiṃ mahorahehiṃ parivāria eāī maha puttao ahimaṇṇū vābādido / ahaṃ uṇa tumhāṇaṃ pekkhantāṇaṃ evva edaṃ kumālavisaseṇaṃ sumaridavvasesaṃ karomi / tti bhaṇia sagavvaṃ āpphālidaṃ ṇeṇa vajjaṇigghādaṇigghosabhīsaṇajīāravaṃ gaṇḍīvaṃ / sāmiṇā bi sajjīkidaṃ kālapuṭṭhaṃ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 130) Let the lord hear. 'Ho, you who are led by <s>Duryodhana</s>, you chiefs of the <s>Kuru</s> army — ho, <s>Karṇa</s>, helmsman of ill-discipline — in my absence, many great warriors surrounded my son <s>Abhimanyu</s> and slew him. Now, before your very eyes, I shall reduce this Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> to a mere memory!' Having said this, he proudly struck his <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, whose bowstring twang was terrifying as the crash of a thunderbolt. And the lord (<s>Karṇa</s>) too readied his bow <s>Kālapṛṣṭha</s>.

children.text: SktCh_130: śṛṇotu devaḥ / are duryodhanapramukhāḥ kurubalasenāprabhavaḥ are avinayanaukarṇadhāra karṇa yuṣmābhirmama parokṣaṃ bahubhirmahārathaiḥ parivṛtyaikākī mama putrako 'bhimanyurvyāpāditaḥ / ahaṃ punaryuṣmākaṃ prekṣamāṇānāmevaitaṃ kumāravṛṣasenaṃ smartavyaśeṣaṃ karomi / iti bhaṇitvā sagarvamāsphālitamanena vajranirghātanirghoṣabhīṣaṇajīvāravaṃ gāṇḍīvam / svāmināpi sajjīkṛtaṃ kālapṛṣṭham /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 130:] Let the lord hear. 'Ho, you who are led by <s>Duryodhana</s>, you chiefs of the <s>Kuru</s> army — ho, <s>Karṇa</s>, helmsman of ill-discipline — by you all, in my absence, many great warriors surrounding him, my son <s>Abhimanyu</s> was slain alone. Now, before your very eyes, I shall reduce this Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> to a mere memory!' Having said this, he proudly struck his <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, whose bowstring twang was terrifying as the crash of a thunderbolt. And the lord (<s>Karṇa</s>) too readied his <s>Kālapṛṣṭha</s>.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] (with concern) Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_131}tado a deva paḍisiddhabhīmaseṇasamalakammālambheṇa gaṇḍīviṇā viraidā aṅgarāavisaseṇarahakūlaṃkasāo duve bāṇaṇaīo / tehiṃ bi duvehiṃ aṇṇoṇṇasiṇehadaṃsidasikkhāvisesehiṃ ahijutto so durāāro majjhamapaṇḍao /
children.translated_text: [<s>Sundaraka</s>:] (Prakrit 131) Then, O lord, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, having repelled <s>Bhīmasena</s>'s battle-engagement, directed two rivers of arrows, scraping the sides of <s>Aṅgarāja</s>'s and <s>Vṛṣasena</s>'s chariots. And by those two rivers, displaying skill born of mutual affection, that ill-conducted middle <s>Pāṇḍava</s> was assailed.

children.text: SktCh_131: tataśca deva pratiṣiddhabhīmasenasamarakarmārambheṇa gāṇḍīvinā viracite aṅgarājavṛṣasenarathakūlaṃkaṣe dve bāṇanadyau / tābhyāmapi dvābhyāmanyo 'nyasnehadarśitaśikṣāviśeṣābhyāmabhiyuktaḥ sa durācāro madhyamapāṇḍavaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 131:] Then, O lord, the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, having repelled <s>Bhīmasena</s>'s battle-engagement, directed two rivers of arrows, scraping the sides of <s>Aṅgarāja</s>'s and <s>Vṛṣasena</s>'s chariots. And by those two rivers, displaying skill born of mutual affection, that ill-conducted middle <s>Pāṇḍava</s> was assailed.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Then what?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_132}tado a deva gaṇḍīviṇā tārarasidajīāṇigghosamettaviṇṇādabāṇavariseṇa taha āaridaṃ pattihiṃ jaha ṇa ṇahatthalaṃ ṇa sāmī ṇa raho ṇa dharaṇī ṇa kumālo ṇa keduvaṃso ṇa balāiṃ ṇa sārahī ṇa tulaṃgamā ṇa disāo ṇa vīraloo a lakkhīadi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sundaraka</s>:
Then, O lord, with the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow, by a shower of arrows known only by the mere sound of bowstrings humming, he acted upon the foot-soldiers such that neither the sky, nor the master, nor the chariot, nor the ground, nor the prince, nor the banner-staff, nor the forces, nor the charioteer, nor the horses, nor the directions, nor the heroic warriors could be seen.

children.text: SktCh_132: tataśca deva gāṇḍīvinā tārarasitajīvānirghoṣamātravijñātabāṇavarṣeṇa tathācaritaṃ patribhiryathā na nabhastalaṃ na svāmī na ratho na dharaṇī na kumāro na ketuvaṃśo na balāni na sārathirna turaṃgamā na diśo na vīralokaśca lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Then, O lord, with the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow, by a shower of arrows recognized only by the mere sound of humming bowstrings, he acted upon the infantry such that neither the sky, nor the lord, nor the chariot, nor the earth, nor the prince, nor the banner-staff, nor the forces, nor the charioteer, nor the horses, nor the directions, nor the host of heroes could be seen.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*With astonishment*
Then what happened?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_133}tado a deva adikkante saravarise khaṇamettaṃ evva saharisasiṃhaṇāde paṇḍavaseṇṇe savisādamukkakkande koravabale samutthido mahanto kalaalo hā hado kumālavisaseṇo tti /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sundaraka</s>:
Then, O lord, when the shower of arrows had passed, for just a moment, as a joyful lion-roar arose in the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army and a despairing cry was released from the <s>Kaurava</s> forces, a great tumult arose: "Alas! Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> has been slain!"

children.text: SktCh_133: tataśca deva atikrānte śaravarṣe kṣaṇamātrameva saharṣasiṃhanāde pāṇḍavasainye saviṣādamuktākrande kauravabale samutthito mahānkalakalo hā hataḥ kumāravṛṣasena iti /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Then, O lord, when the shower of arrows had passed, for just a moment, as a joyful lion-roar arose in the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army and a despairing cry was released from the <s>Kaurava</s> forces, a great tumult arose: "Alas! Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s> has been slain!"

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*Choking back tears*
Then what happened?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_134}tado deva pekkhāmi kumālaṃ hadasārahitulaṃgaṃ lūṇādabattacābacāmarakeduvaṃsaṃ saggabbhaṭṭhaṃ via sulakumālaṃ ekkeṇa evva hiaamammabhediṇā silīmuheṇa bhiṇṇadehaṃ rahamajjhe pallatthaṃ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sundaraka</s>:
Then, O lord, I beheld the prince — his charioteer and horses slain, his parasol, bow, fly-whisk, and banner-staff cut down — like a tender celestial youth fallen from heaven, his body pierced by a single arrow that split his heart and vital parts, collapsed in the middle of his chariot.

children.text: SktCh_134: tato deva prekṣe kumāraṃ hatasārathituraṃgaṃ lūnātapatracāpacāmaraketuvaṃśaṃ svargabhraṣṭamiva surakumāramekenaiva hṛdayamarmabhedinā śilīmukhena bhinnadehaṃ rathamadhye paryastam /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Then, O lord, I beheld the prince — his charioteer and horses slain, his parasol, bow, fly-whisk, and banner-staff cut down — like a beautiful celestial youth fallen from heaven, his body pierced by a single arrow that split his heart and vital parts, fallen in the middle of his chariot.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*sāsram**
ahaha kumāra vṛṣasena / alamataḥ paraṃ śrutvā / hā vatsa hā madaṅkadurlalita hā madājñākara hā gadāyudhapriyaśiṣya hā śauryasāgara hā rādheyakulapraroha hā priyadarśana hā duḥśāsananirviśeṣa hā sarvaguruvatsala prayaccha me prativacanam /

children.translated_text: Verse 4.10:
That lotus-face of yours, with eyes fully developed, of recently risen moonstone-like beauty, with the charm of newly blossoming youth,

children.text: prāṇāpahāraparivartitadṛṣṭi dṛṣṭaṃ ē̃ karṇena tatkathamivānanapaṅkajaṃ te // 4.10 //
children.translated_text: its gaze turned away at the moment of death — how did <s>Karṇa</s> behold it? (4.10)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*With tears*
Ah, ah, Prince <s>Vṛṣasena</s>! Enough, I cannot bear to hear more! Alas, my child! Alas, one fondly raised in my lap! Alas, one obedient to my commands! Alas, dear pupil of <s>Gadāyudha</s>! Alas, ocean of valor! Alas, scion of <s>Rādheya</s>'s lineage! Alas, beautiful one! Alas, one no different from <s>Duḥśāsana</s>! Alas, one devoted to all elders! Give me an answer!

<s>Sūta</s> (charioteer):
Long-lived one, enough of this excessive torrent of grief!

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
sūta puṇyavanto hi duḥkhabhājo bhavanti / asmākaṃ punaḥ

children.translated_text: Verse 4.11:
The hearts of those whose kinsmen have been slain before their very eyes are burned exceedingly by this fire of humiliation;

children.text: hṛdayaṃ dahyate 'tyarthaṃ kuto duḥkhaṃ kuto vyathā // 4.11 //
children.translated_text: what need is there to speak of grief, what need of anguish? (4.11)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Charioteer, those who are meritorious become bearers of suffering. As for us, however —
*Thus he falls into a swoon.*

<s>Sūta</s>:
May the great king compose himself, may he compose himself! *He fans him with the edge of a cloth.*

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*labdhasaṃjñaḥ**
bhadra sundaraka tato vayasyena kiṃ pratipannamaṅgarājena /
children.translated_text:
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*Having regained consciousness*
Good <s>Sundaraka</s>, then what course of action was undertaken by my friend, the king of <s>Aṅga</s>?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_135}tado a deva tahāvidhassa puttassa daṃsaṇeṇa saṃgalidaṃ assujalaṃ ujjhia aṇabekkhidaparappaharaṇābhioeṇa sāmiṇā aṅgarāeṇa abhijutto dhaṇaṃjao / taṃ a sudavahāmarisuddībidaparakkamaṃ vimukkajīvidāsaṃ taha parakkamantaṃ pekkhia bhīmaṇaulasahadevapañcālappamuhehiṃ antarido dhaṇaṃjaassa rahavaro /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sundaraka</s>:
Then, O lord, upon seeing his son in that state, wiping away his flowing tears, without regard for the enemy's blows, the lord, the king of <s>Aṅga</s>, assailed <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>. And seeing him fighting thus, his valor inflamed by grief at his son's death, having abandoned all attachment to life, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>'s great chariot was intercepted by <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Nakula</s>, <s>Sahadeva</s>, the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, and others.

children.text: SktCh_135: tataśca deva tathāvidhasya putrasya darśanena saṃgalitamaśrujalamujjhitvānavekṣitaparapraharaṇābhiyogena svāmināṅgarājenābhiyukto dhanaṃjayaḥ / taṃ ca sutavadhāmarṣoddīpitaparākramaṃ vimuktajīvitāśaṃ tathā parākramantaṃ prekṣya bhīmanakulasahadevapāñcālapramukhairantarito dhanaṃjayasya rathavaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Then, O lord, upon seeing his son in that state, casting aside his flowing tears, without regard for the enemy's assault, the lord, the king of <s>Aṅga</s>, attacked <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>. And seeing him fighting thus, his valor inflamed by the grief of his son's death, having abandoned all attachment to life, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>'s great chariot was intercepted by <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Nakula</s>, <s>Sahadeva</s>, the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, and others.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Then what happened?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_136}tado deva sallena bhaṇidaṃ / aṅgarāa kkhalidatulaṃgamo mathidacakkaṇemikūbaro de raho / tā ṇa juttaṃ bhīmajjuṇehiṃ saha ājujjiduṃ / tti bhaṇia ṇivattido raho odārido sāmī sandaṇādo bahuppaāraṃ a samassāsido /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sundaraka</s>:
Then, O lord, <s>Śalya</s> spoke: "King of <s>Aṅga</s>, your horses have stumbled, your chariot's wheel-rim and axle are shattered. It is not fitting to fight against <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>." Having said this, he turned the chariot back, brought the lord down from the chariot, and consoled him in many ways.

children.text: SktCh_136: tato deva śalyena bhaṇitam / aṅgarāja skhalitaturaṃgamo mathitacakranemikūbaraste rathaḥ / tanna yuktaṃ bhīmārjunābhyāṃ sahāyoddhum / iti bhaṇitvā nirvartito ratho 'vatāritaḥ svāmī syandanādbahuprakāraṃ ca samāśvāsitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Then, O lord, <s>Śalya</s> spoke: "King of <s>Aṅga</s>, your horses have stumbled, your chariot's wheel-rim and axle are shattered. It is not fitting to fight against <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>." Having said this, he turned the chariot back, brought the lord down from the chariot, and consoled him in many ways.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Then what happened?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_137}tado a sāmiṇā suiraṃ vilabia pariaṇobaṇīdaṃ aṇṇaṃ rahaṃ pekkhia dīhaṃ ṇissasia mai diṭṭhī viṇikkhittā / sundaraa ehi tti bhaṇidaṃ a / tado ahaṃ ubagado sāmisamībaṃ / tado abaṇīa sīsaṭṭhāṇādo paṭṭiaṃ sarīrasaṃgalidehiṃ soṇiabindūhiṃ littamuhaṃ bāṇaṃ kadua avalihia pesido devassa saṃdeso* /iti paṭṭakāmarpayati**
children.translated_text:
<s>Sundaraka</s>:
Then the lord, having lamented for a long time, seeing another chariot brought by the attendants, heaving a deep sigh, cast his gaze upon me. "<s>Sundaraka</s>, come here," he said. Then I approached my lord's presence. Then, removing the headband from his brow, making an arrow whose tip was smeared with drops of blood flowing from his body, having inscribed it, he sent a message to the lord. *He presents the tablet.*

children.text: SktCh_137: tataśca svāminā suciraṃ vilapya parijanopanītamanyaṃ rathaṃ prekṣya dīrghaṃ niḥśvasya mayi dṛṣṭirvinikṣiptā / sundaraka ehīti bhaṇitaṃ ca / tato 'hamupagataḥ svāmisamīpam / tato 'panīya śīrṣasthānātpaṭṭikāṃ śarīrasaṃgalitaiḥ śoṇitabindubhirliptamukhaṃ bāṇaṃ kṛtvābhilikhya preṣito devasya saṃdeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Then the lord, having lamented for a long time, seeing another chariot brought by the attendants, heaving a deep sigh, cast his gaze upon me. "<s>Sundaraka</s>, come here," he said. Then I approached my lord's presence. Then, removing the headband from his brow, making an arrow whose tip was smeared with drops of blood flowing from his body, having inscribed it, he sent a message to the lord.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*gṛhītvā vācayati**
svasti / mahārājaduryodhanaṃ samarāṅgaṇātkarṇa etadantaṃ kaṇṭhe gāḍhamāliṅgya vijñāpayati /

children.translated_text: Verse 4.12:

children.text: astragrāmavidhau kṛtī na samareṣvasyāsti tulyaḥ pumā- $ nbhrātṛbhyo 'pi mamādhiko 'yamamunā jeyāḥ pṛthāsūnavaḥ &
children.translated_text: He is skilled in all the branches of weaponry, there is no man his equal in battles, he is superior even to my brothers — by him the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s> should have been conquered.

children.text: tvatsaṃbhāvita ityahaṃ na ca hato duḥśāsanārirmayā ē̃ tvaṃ duḥkhapratikāramehi bhujayorvīryeṇa bāṣpeṇa vā // 4.12 //
children.translated_text: That "he is honored by you" — this thought has been my undoing. <s>Duḥśāsana</s>'s enemy was not slain by me. Seek the remedy for your grief through the valor of your arms — or through tears. (4.12)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*Taking it and reading*
Greetings! <s>Karṇa</s> addresses this from the battlefield to the great king <s>Duryodhana</s>, embracing him tightly around the neck with these final words:
