children.text: vayasya karṇa kimidaṃ bhrātṛśatavadhaduḥkhitaṃ māmapareṇa vākśalyena ghaṭṭayasi / bhadra sundaraka athedānīṃ kimārambho 'ṅgarājaḥ /
children.translated_text: Friend <s>Karṇa</s>, what is this? You torment me, already grief-stricken by the slaughter of a hundred brothers, with yet another verbal arrow? Good <s>Sundaraka</s>, and now — what course does the king of <s>Aṅga</s> pursue?

children.text:
&sundarakaḥ&:
{Pkt_138}deva abaṇīdasarīrāvaraṇo attavahakidaṇiccao puṇo bi pattheṇa saha samalaṃ maggedi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sundaraka</s>:
O lord, having removed his bodily armor, determined upon self-sacrifice, he again seeks battle with <s>Pārtha</s>.

children.text: SktCh_138: deva apanītaśarīrāvaraṇa ātmavadhakṛtaniścayaḥ punarapi pārthena saha samaraṃ mārgayate /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: O lord, having removed his bodily armor, resolved upon his own death, he again seeks battle with <s>Pārtha</s>.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
*āvegādāsanāduttiṣṭhan**
sūta rathamupanaya / sundaraka tvamapi madvacanāttvaritataraṃ gatvā vayasyamaṅgarājaṃ pratibodhaya / alamatisāhasena / abhinna evāyamāvayoḥ saṃkalpaḥ / na khalu bhavāneko jīvitaparityāgākāṅkṣī / kiṃ tu

children.translated_text: Verse 4.13:

children.text: hatvā pārthānsalilamaśivaṃ bandhuvargāya dattvā $ muktvā bāṣpaṃ saha katipayairmantribhiścāribhiśca &
children.translated_text: Having slain the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>, having offered inauspicious water-libations for our kinsmen, having shed tears with the few remaining ministers and enemies,

children.text: kṛtvānyo 'nyaṃ suciramapunarbhāvi gāḍhopagūḍhaṃ ē̃ saṃtyakṣyāvo hatatanumimāṃ duḥkhitau nirvṛtau ca // 4.13 //
children.translated_text: having embraced each other long in a final, tight embrace that shall never recur — the two of us shall abandon these wounded bodies, both grieving and at peace. (4.13)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*Rising from his seat in agitation*
Charioteer, bring the chariot! <s>Sundaraka</s>, you too — go swiftly at my command and rouse my friend the king of <s>Aṅga</s>! Enough of this excessive recklessness! Our resolve remains unbroken. It is not that you alone desire to abandon life. But —

children.text: atha ca śokaṃ prati mayā na kiṃcitsaṃdeṣṭavyam /

children.translated_text: Verse 4.14:

children.text: vṛṣaseno na te putro na me duḥśāsano 'nujaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣasena</s> is not your son, <s>Duḥśāsana</s> is not my brother;

children.text: tvāṃ bodhayāmi kimahaṃ tvaṃ māṃ saṃsthāpayiṣyasi // 4.14 //
children.translated_text: why do I console you? It is you who will steady me. (4.14)
And moreover, regarding grief, I have nothing to instruct him about —

<s>Sundaraka</s>:
As the lord commands. *He exits.*
Sanskrit chāyā: As the lord commands.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Bring the chariot at once!

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
*karṇaṃ dattvā**
deva hreṣāsaṃvalito nemidhvaniḥ śrūyate / tathā tarkayāmi nūnaṃ parijanopanīto rathaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sūta</s>:
*Listening attentively*
O lord, the sound of neighing mingled with the rumble of wheel-rims is heard. I conjecture that a chariot brought by the attendants must be approaching.

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Charioteer, go and make it ready!

<s>Sūta</s>:
As the lord commands. *He exits and re-enters.*

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
*Looking*
Why have you not mounted?

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
eṣa khalu tāto 'mbā ca saṃjayādhiṣṭhitaṃ rathamāruhya devasya samīpamupagatau /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sūta</s>:
Indeed, my lord, your father and mother have arrived, having mounted the chariot attended by <s>Saṃjaya</s>.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
kiṃ nāma tāto 'mbā ca saṃprāptau / kaṣṭamatibībhatsamācaritaṃ daivena / sūta gaccha tvaṃ syandanaṃ tūrṇamupahara / ahamapi tātadarśanaṃ pariharannekānte tiṣṭhāmi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
What — father and mother have arrived? Cruel indeed is the most repugnant conduct of fate! Charioteer, go and bring the chariot quickly! I too shall stand aside, avoiding the sight of my father.

<s>Sūta</s>:
O lord, these two are your sole remaining kinsmen — how can you not console them?
Verse 4.15:

children.text: adyaivāvāṃ raṇamupagatau tātamambāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā $ ghrātastābhyāṃ śirasi vinato 'haṃ ca duḥśāsanaśca &
children.translated_text: Just today, the two of us — I and <s>Duḥśāsana</s> — having approached the battle, bowed before father and mother, and were kissed by them upon our heads.

children.text: tasminbāle prasabhamariṇā prāpite tāmavasthāṃ ē̃ pārśvaṃ pitrorapagataghṛṇaḥ kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi gatvā // 4.15 //
children.translated_text: Now that the boy has been brought to that state by the merciless enemy, how shall I, devoid of shame, go before my parents and what shall I say? (4.15)

<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Charioteer, how can I, whose fortune has turned its face away, console them? Behold —
Nevertheless, the elders must be saluted.

children.text:
*iti niṣkrāntau**
iti caturtho 'ṅkaḥ /

ACT_5
pañcamo 'ṅkaḥ /
*tataḥ praviśati rathayānena gāndhārī saṃjayo dhṛtarāṣṭraśca**
children.translated_text:
*Both exit.*
Thus ends the Fourth Act.

ACT 5
The Fifth Act.
*Then enter, on a chariot, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Saṃjaya</s>, and <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>.*

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa saṃjaya kathaya kathaya kasminnuddeśe kurukulakānanaikapravālo vatso me duryodhanastiṣṭhati / kaccijjīvati vā na vā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:
Child <s>Saṃjaya</s>, tell me, tell me — in which part of the field does my son <s>Duryodhana</s>, the sole shoot of the <s>Kuru</s> family forest, stand? Does he still live or not?

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_140}jāda jai saccaṃ jīvadi me vaccho tā kadhehi kassiṃ dese vaṭṭadi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Gāndhārī</s>:
Child, if my son truly lives, then tell me — in which part of the field is he?

children.text: SktCh_140: jāta yadi satyaṃ jīvati me vatsastatkathaya kasmindeśe vartate /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Child, if my son truly lives, then tell me — in which region is he?

<s>Saṃjaya</s>:
Indeed, O great king, there he sits alone in the shade of a banyan tree.

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_141}*sakaruṇam**
jāda eāī tti bhaṇāsi / kiṃ ṇu kkhu saṃpadaṃ bhādusadaṃ se pāse bhavissadi /
children.translated_text:
<s>Gāndhārī</s>:
*With compassion*
Child, you say "alone"? Will there not be a hundred brothers at his side now?

children.text: SktCh_141: jāta ekākīti bhaṇasi / kiṃ nu khalu sāṃprataṃ bhrātṛśatamasya pārśve bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Child, you say "alone"? Will there indeed be a hundred brothers at his side now?

<s>Saṃjaya</s>:
Father, mother — please descend gently from the chariot.
*Both mime the act of descending.*
*Then enters <s>Duryodhana</s>, seated with shame.*

children.text:
&saṃjayaḥ&:
*upasṛtya**
vijayatāṃ mahārājaḥ / nanveṣa tāto 'mbayā saha prāptaḥ / kiṃ na paśyati mahārājaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Saṃjaya</s>:
*Approaching*
Victory to the great king! Indeed, here is your father, arrived with your mother. Does the great king not see?
*<s>Duryodhana</s> mimes embarrassment.*
Verse 5.1:

children.text: śalyāni vyapanīya kaṅkavadanairunmocite kaṅkaṭe $ baddheṣu vraṇapaṭṭakeṣu śanakaiḥ karṇe kṛtāpāśrayaḥ &
children.translated_text: Having removed the arrows with their barbed tips, having unfastened the armor, having slowly bandaged the wounds, taking support upon <s>Karṇa</s>,

children.text: dūrānnirjitasāntvitānnarapatīnālokayaṁllīlayā ē̃ sahyā putraka vedaneti na mayā pāpena pṛṣṭo bhavān // 5.1 //
children.translated_text: gazing playfully from afar at the defeated and consoled kings — "The pain is bearable, my child" — thus I, the sinful one, did not ask after you. (5.1)
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:
*<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and <s>Gāndhārī</s> approach by touch and embrace him.*

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_142}vaccha adigāḍhappahāraveaṇāpajjāulassa amhesu saṃṇihidesu bi ṇa pasaradi de vāṇī /
children.translated_text:
<s>Gāndhārī</s>:
Child, though overwhelmed with the agony of grievous blows, even in our presence your voice does not stir forth.

children.text: SktCh_142: vatsa atigāḍhaprahāravedanāparyākulasyāsmāsu saṃnihiteṣvapi na prasarati te vāṇī /
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā: Child, though overwhelmed with the agony of exceedingly severe blows, even in our presence your voice does not extend forth.

<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:
Child <s>Duryodhana</s>, why is there now this unprecedented silence even toward me?

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_143}vaccha jai tumaṃ bi amhe ṇālabasi tā kiṃ saṃpadaṃ vaccho dussāsaṇo ālabadu dummarisaṇo vā adha aṇṇo vā* /iti roditi**
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Child, if even you do not speak to us, then what now? Let son <s>Duḥśāsana</s> speak, or <s>Durmarṣaṇa</s>, or another! [She weeps.]

children.text: SktCh_143: vatsa yadi tvamapyasmānnālapasi tatkiṃ sāṃprataṃ vatso duḥśāsana ālapatu durmarṣaṇo vāthānyo vā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Child, if even you do not speak to us, then what now? Let son <s>Duḥśāsana</s> speak, or <s>Durmarṣaṇa</s>, or else another!
[Verse 5.2]

children.text: pāpo 'hamapratikṛtānujanāśadarśī $ tātasya bāṣpapayasāṃ tava cāmba hetuḥ &
children.translated_text: Wicked am I, who could not prevent the destruction of my younger brothers, the cause of these tears streaming from the eyes of my father and of you, O mother;

children.text: durjātamatra vimale bharatānvavāye ē̃ kiṃ māṃ sutakṣayakaraṃ suta ityavaiṣi // 5.2 //
children.translated_text: an ill-born one in this spotless lineage of the <s>Bharatas</s> — why do you call me 'son,' me who has caused the destruction of [your] sons? (5.2)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_144}jāda alaṃ paridevideṇa / tumaṃ bi dāva ekko imassa andhajualassa maggobadesao / tā ciraṃ jīva / kiṃ me rajjeṇa jaeṇa vā /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, enough of lamentation! You at least are the one guide for this blind couple. So live long! What use to me is the kingdom or victory?

children.text: SktCh_144: jāta alaṃ paridevitena / tvamapi tāvadeko 'syāndhayugalasya mārgopadeśakaḥ / tacciraṃ jīva / kiṃ me rājyena jayena vā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Son, enough of lamentation! You at least are the one guide for this blind couple. So live long! What use to me is the kingdom or victory?
[Verse 5.3]

children.text: mātaḥ kimapyasadṛśaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ vacaste $ sukṣatriyā kva bhavatī kva ca dīnataiṣā &
children.translated_text: Mother, you speak something pitiable and unbecoming of you — where is your noble <s>Kṣatriya</s> spirit and where is this wretchedness?

children.text: nirvatsale sutaśatasya vipattimetāṃ ē̃ tvaṃ nānucintayasi rakṣasi māmayogyam // 5.3 //
children.translated_text: Devoid of motherly feeling, you do not grieve the calamity of your hundred sons, but seek to protect me, who am unworthy! (5.3)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
Surely this is the doing of the grief for [her] sons.

children.text:
&saṃjayaḥ&:
mahārāja kiṃ vāyaṃ lokavādo vitatho na ghaṭasya kūpapāte rajjurapi tatra prakṣeptavyeti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] Great king, is not this popular saying true — that when a pot falls into a well, the rope too must be cast in after it?
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] This is inadequate. When there is no one to be helped, what use is the instrument of help? [He weeps.]

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
*duryodhanaṃ pariṣvajya**
vatsa samāśvasihi samāśvāsaya cāsmānimāmatidīnāṃ mātaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] [Embracing <s>Duryodhana</s>.] Child, take courage, and console us and this exceedingly wretched mother as well.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
tāta durlabhaḥ samāśvāsa idānīṃ yuṣmākam / kiṃ tu

children.translated_text: [Verse 5.4]
Together with <s>Kuntī</s>, you two — [grieving over me] whose sons have been slain —
though resplendent even in grief, do not mourn your sons! (5.4)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Father, consolation is difficult for you now. But —

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_145}jāda edaṃ evva saṃpadaṃ pabhūdaṃ jaṃ tumaṃ bi dāva ekko jīvasi / tā jāda akālo de samarassa / pasīda / eso de sīsañjalī / ṇivattīadu samaravvābārādo / apacchimaṃ karehi me vaaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, this alone is now a great thing — that you at least are alive. So, child, this is not the time for your battle. Have mercy! Here is my head-salutation to you. Turn back from the business of war. Fulfill my last wish.

children.text: SktCh_145: jāta etadeva sāṃprataṃ prabhūtaṃ yattvamapi tāvadeko jīvasi / tajjāta akālaste samarasya / prasīda / eṣa te śīrṣāñjaliḥ / nivartyatāṃ samaravyāpārāt / apaścimaṃ kuru me vacanam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Son, this alone is now a great thing — that you at least are alive. So, child, this is not the time for your battle. Have mercy! Here is my head-salutation to you. Turn back from the business of war. Fulfill my last wish.

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa śṛṇu vacanaṃ tavāmbāyā mama ca nihatāśeṣabandhuvargasya / paśya /

children.translated_text: [Verse 5.5]

children.text: dāyādā na yayorbalena gaṇitāstau droṇabhīṣmau hatau $ karṇasyātmajamagrataḥ śamayato bhītaṃ jagatphālgunāt &
children.translated_text: Those two — <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s> — whose might could not be matched by the rival princes, have been slain; of <s>Karṇa</s>, who stilled before him the son [<s>Abhimanyu</s>] whom the world feared from <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: vatsānāṃ nidhanena me tvayi ripuḥ śeṣapratijño 'dhunā ē̃ mānaṃ vairiṣu muñca tāta pitarāvandhāvimau pālaya // 5.5 //
children.translated_text: by the death of [my] sons, the enemy whose vow is to destroy the remainder now [targets] you — abandon your pride against the foes, O child, and protect these two blind parents! (5.5)
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, hear the words of your mother and of me, whose entire band of kinsmen has been slain. Behold —
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Having turned back from battle, what should I do?

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_146}jāda jaṃ pidā de viuro vā bhaṇādi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, whatever your father or <s>Vidura</s> tells you.

children.text: SktCh_146: jāta yatpitā te viduro vā bhaṇati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Son, whatever your father or <s>Vidura</s> tells you.
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] Sire, it is so.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] <s>Saṃjaya</s>, is there still something to be taught?
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] Sire, as long as one breathes, one who desires victory is a fit ground for instruction by the wise.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] [Angrily.] Let us hear, then, from you yourself, O wise one, counsel befitting us at this moment.

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa yuktavādini saṃjaye kimatra krodhena / yadi prakṛtimāpadyase tadahameva bhavantaṃ bravīmi / śrūyatām /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, <s>Saṃjaya</s> speaks rightly — why this anger? If you will return to your natural disposition, then I myself shall speak to you. Listen.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Let father speak.

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa kiṃ vistareṇa / saṃdhattāṃ bhavānidānīmapi yudhiṣṭhiramīpsitapaṇabandhena /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, why elaborate? Let your lordship even now make peace with <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, binding yourself to [concede] his desired stake.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
tāta tanayasnehavaiklavyādambā bāliśatvātsaṃjayaśca kāmamevaṃ bravītu / yuṣmākamapyevaṃ vyāmohaḥ / atha vā prabhavati putranāśajanmā hṛdayajvaraḥ / anyacca tāta askhalitabhrātṛśato 'haṃ yadā tadāvadhīritavāsudevasāmopanyāsaḥ / saṃprati hi dṛṣṭapitāmahācāryānujarājacakravipattiḥ svaśarīramātrasnehādudāttapuruṣavrīḍāvahamasukhāvasānaṃ ca kathamiva kariṣyati duryodhanaḥ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ saṃdhim / anyacca nayavedinsaṃjaya

children.translated_text: [Verse 5.6]
Kings who are being diminished, they say, make peace with the enemy;
with <s>Duḥśāsana</s> slain, how are the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> together with their brothers undiminished? (5.6)

[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Father, let mother speak thus out of the bewilderment of maternal affection, and <s>Saṃjaya</s> out of foolishness — but that you too should be thus deluded! Or rather, the heart-fever born from the loss of sons is indeed overpowering. And another thing, father — I, whose hundred brothers were unfaltering, when I was [at the height of power], rejected the peace overtures of <s>Vāsudeva</s>. Now indeed, having witnessed the calamity of the grandsire, the teacher, the younger brothers, and the circle of kings — how could <s>Duryodhana</s>, merely out of attachment to his own body, do that which brings shame to a noble man and ends in misery — make peace with the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>? And another thing, O <s>Saṃjaya</s>, knower of statecraft —

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa evaṃ gate 'pi matprārthanayā na kiṃcinna karoti yudhiṣṭhiraḥ / anyacca sarvadaivāprakṛṣṭamātmānaṃ manyate yudhiṣṭhiraḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, even so, at my entreaty <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> would not refuse anything. Moreover, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> always considers himself not superior to fate.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] How so?

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa śrūyatāṃ pratijñā yudhiṣṭhirasya / nāhamekasyāpi bhrāturvipattau prāṇāndhārayāmīti / bahucchalatvātsaṃgrāmasyānujanāśamāśaṅkamāno yadaiva bhavate rocate tadaivāsau sajjaḥ saṃdhātum /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, hear the vow of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>: 'I shall not sustain my life even at the loss of a single brother.' Apprehending the destruction of his brothers because of the many contingencies of battle, he is ready to make peace whenever it pleases your lordship.
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] It is so.
[<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, accept the words of your father, which are supported by reason.
[Sanskrit rendering:] Son, accept the words of your father, which are supported by reason.
[Verse 5.7]

children.text: ekenāpi vinānujena maraṇaṃ pārthaḥ pratijñātavā- $ nbhrātḥṇāṃ nihate śate 'bhilaṣate duryodhano jīvitum &
children.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) has vowed to die at the loss of even a single brother — yet <s>Duryodhana</s>, with a hundred brothers slain, desires to live?

children.text: taṃ duḥśāsanaśoṇitāśanamariṃ bhinnaṃ gadākoṭibhi- ē̃ rbhīmaṃ dikṣu na vikṣipāmi kṛpaṇaḥ saṃdhiṃ vidadhyāmaham // 5.7 //
children.translated_text: If I do not tear apart with blows of my mace that enemy <s>Bhīma</s>, who feasted on the blood of <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, and scatter him to the quarters — wretch that I would be — should I make peace? (5.7)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Father, mother, <s>Saṃjaya</s> —

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_148}hā jāda dussāsaṇa hā madaṅkadullalita hā juarāa assudapuvvā kkhu kassa bi loe īdisī vipattī / hā vīrasadappasaviṇi hadagandhāri dukkhasadaṃ pasūdāsi ṇa uṇa sudasadaṃ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Alas, son <s>Duḥśāsana</s>! Alas, my darling child! Alas, young prince! Truly, such a calamity is unheard of for anyone in the world! Alas, you who gave birth to a hundred heroes, O slain <s>Gāndhārī</s>, you have brought forth a hundred sorrows, not a hundred sons!

children.text: SktCh_148: hā jāta duḥśāsana hā madaṅkadurlalita hā yuvarāja aśrutapūrvā khalu kasyāpi loka īdṛśī vipattiḥ / hā vīraśataprasavini hatagāndhāri duḥkhaśataṃ prasūtāsi na punaḥ sutaśatam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Alas, son <s>Duḥśāsana</s>! Alas, my darling child! Alas, young prince! Truly, such a calamity is unheard of for anyone in the world! Alas, you who gave birth to a hundred heroes, O slain <s>Gāndhārī</s>, you have brought forth a hundred sorrows, not a hundred sons!
[All weep.]

children.text:
&saṃjayaḥ&:
*bāṣpamutsṛjya**
tāta amba pratibodhayituṃ mahārājamimāṃ bhūmiṃ yuvāmāgatau / tadātmāpi tāvatsaṃstabhyatām /
children.translated_text: [<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] [Shedding tears.] Father, mother — you two came to this battlefield to rouse the great king. So let you yourselves at least be steadied first.

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa duryodhana evaṃ vimukheṣu bhāgadheyeṣu tvayi cāmuñcati sahajaṃ mānamariṣu tvadekaśeṣajīvitālambaneyaṃ tapasvinī gāndhārī kamavalambatāṃ śaraṇamahaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child <s>Duryodhana</s>, when fortunes have thus turned against us, and you will not relinquish your inborn pride against your enemies — this wretched <s>Gāndhārī</s>, whose sole support of life is your remaining existence, whom shall she take as her refuge? And I too?
[Verse 5.8]
Those who had conquered the world, who enjoyed sovereignty, who had humbled their foes, who were worshipped by the crests of a thousand bowing kings,

children.text: abhimukhamarīnghnantaḥ saṃkhye hatāḥ śatātmajā ē̃ vahatu sagareṇoḍhāṃ tāto dhuraṃ sahito 'mbayā // 5.8 //
children.translated_text: those hundred sons, slaying enemies face-to-face in battle, have been killed — let father, together with mother, bear the burden borne with fortitude! (5.8)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Hear what is now timely to undertake.
Otherwise, the duty of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> would be violated by this lord.
[Behind the scenes: a great uproar.]

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_149}*ākarṇya sabhayam**
jāda kahiṃ edaṃ hāhākāramissaṃ tūrarasidaṃ suṇīadi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] [Listening, fearfully.] Son, from where is this sound of drums mixed with cries of "alas" being heard?
[Sanskrit rendering:] Son, from where is this sound of drums mixed with cries of "alas" being heard?
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] Mother, this ground is the place for such great outcries that terrify the timid.

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa saṃjaya jñāyatāmatibhairavaḥ khalu vistārī hāhāravaḥ / kāraṇenāsya mahatā bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child <s>Saṃjaya</s>, find out — this cry of "alas" is truly most terrible and spreading. There must be a great cause for it.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
tāta prasīda / parāṅmukhaṃ khalu daivamasmākam / yāvadaparamapi kiṃcidatyāhitaṃ na śrāvayati tāvadevājñāpaya māṃ saṃgrāmāvataraṇāya /
children.translated_text: [<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Father, have mercy! Our fate is indeed turned away from us. Before it makes us hear yet another calamity, command me to descend into battle!
[<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, for a moment at least console me, the unfortunate one.

children.text: SktCh_150: jāta muhūrtaṃ tāvanmāṃ mandabhāgyāṃ samāśvāsaya /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Son, for a moment at least console me, the unfortunate one.

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa yadyapi bhavānsamarāya kṛtaniścayastathāpi rahaḥ parapratīghātopāyaścintyatām /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, even though you are resolved upon battle, still let a secret means of defeating the enemy be considered.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
VERSE_5.9
pratyakṣaṃ hatabāndhavā mama pare hantuṃ na yogyā rahaḥ $ kiṃ vā tena kṛtena tairiva kṛtaṃ yanna prakāśaṃ raṇe &
children.translated_text: [<s>Duryodhana</s>:] [Verse 5.9] My kinsmen have been slain before my very eyes — the enemies are not fit to be killed in secret. And what would be accomplished by such a deed? Whatever has not been done by them openly in battle [cannot be matched by stealth] —

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_151}jāda eāī tumaṃ / ko de sahāattaṇaṃ karissadi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, you are alone! Who will come to your aid?

children.text: SktCh_151: jāta ekākī tvam / kaste sāhāyyaṃ kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Son, you are alone! Who will come to your aid?
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
[Verse 5.9 continued]

children.text: eko 'haṃ bhavatīsutakṣayakaro mātaḥ kiyanto 'rayaḥ ē̃ sāmyaṃ kevalametu daivamadhunā niṣpāṇḍavā medinī // 5.9 //
children.translated_text: Alone am I, the cause of the destruction of your sons, O mother — how many are the enemies? Let fate alone now be equal — may the earth be rid of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>! A wretch would I be if I were to make peace! (5.9)
[Behind the scenes: after the uproar.]

children.text: bho bho yodhāḥ nivedayantu bhavantaḥ kauraveśvarāya / idaṃ mahatkadanaṃ pravṛttam / alamapriyaśravaṇaparāṅmukhatayā / yataḥ kālānurūpaṃ pratividhātavyamidānīm / tathā hi

children.translated_text: [Verse 5.10]

children.text: tyaktaprājanaraśmiraṅkitatanuḥ pārthāṅkitairmārgaṇai- $ rvāhaiḥ syandanavartmanāṃ paricayādākṛṣyamāṇaḥ śanaiḥ &
children.translated_text: With reins and bridle cast aside, his body marked by the arrows of <s>Arjuna</s>, his horses, through habit of the chariot-tracks, slowly dragging [the chariot] along,

children.text: vārtāmaṅgapatervilocanajalairāvedayanpṛcchatāṃ ē̃ śūnyenaiva rathena yāti śibiraṃ śalyaḥ kurūñśalyayan // 5.10 //
children.translated_text: announcing the news of the lord of <s>Aṅga</s> [<s>Karṇa</s>] with tears in his eyes to those who inquire — <s>Śalya</s> proceeds to the camp with an empty chariot, piercing the <s>Kurus</s> [with grief]! (5.10)

Ho, warriors! Let your lordships announce to the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>: this great slaughter has taken place. Let there be no turning away from hearing unwelcome news, for now a remedy befitting the time must be devised. For indeed —
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] [Having heard, with apprehension.] Ah! By whom was this announced, indistinct yet terrible as a thunderbolt? Who is there? Who?
[Enter a charioteer, in agitation.]
[Charioteer:] Alas, we are ruined! [He throws himself down.]
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Speak, speak!
[Verse 5.11]

children.text: śalyena yathā śalyena mūrcchitaḥ praviśatā janaugho 'yam /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Śalya</s>, like a thorn [<s>śalya</s>], having caused the crowd to faint as he entered,
mounted upon the empty chariot of <s>Karṇa</s> as if upon a [shattered] desire! (5.11)
[Charioteer:] Long-lived one, what else [can I say]?
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Alas, my friend <s>Karṇa</s>! [He falls into a swoon.]
[<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, take heart, take heart!
[Sanskrit rendering:] Son, take heart, take heart!
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] Let His Majesty take heart, take heart!
[Verse 5.12]

children.text: bhīṣme droṇe ca nihate ya āsīdavalambanam /
children.translated_text: When <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s> had been slain, he who was the [last] support —

children.text: vatssaya me suhṛcchūro rādheyaḥ so 'pyayaṃ hataḥ // 5.12 //
children.translated_text: that heroic friend of my son, <s>Rādheya</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>) — he too has now been slain! (5.12)
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Alas, how terrible, how terrible!

children.text: vatsa samāśvasihi samāśvasihi / nanu bho hatavidhe

children.translated_text: [Verse 5.13]
Blind, having endured the grief of the calamity of a hundred sons, I, together with my wife, have come to this pitiable state;

children.text: asminnaśeṣitasuhṛdgurubandhuvarge ē̃ duryodhane 'pi hi kṛto bhavatā nirāśaḥ // 5.13 //
children.translated_text: in this [situation] where the entire circle of friends, preceptors, and kinsmen has been destroyed — even regarding <s>Duryodhana</s>, you have now made us despair! (5.13)
Child, take heart, take heart! O fate —

children.text: vatsa duryodhana samāśvasihi samāśvasihi / samāśvāsaya tapasvinīṃ mātaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Child <s>Duryodhana</s>, take heart, take heart! And console your wretched mother as well.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] [Having regained consciousness.]
[Verse 5.14]

children.text: ayi karṇa karṇasukhadāṃ prayaccha me $ giramudgiranniva mudaṃ mayi sthirām &
children.translated_text: O <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, give me words pleasing to the ear, as if pouring forth steady joy upon me;

children.text: satatāviyuktamakṛtāpriyaṃ priyaṃ ē̃ vṛṣasenavatsala vihāya yāsi mām // 5.14 //
children.translated_text: O you who were ever inseparable, who never did me displeasure, O dear one fond of <s>Vṛṣasena</s> — you depart, leaving me! (5.14)
[He swoons again.]
[All try to console him.]
[Verse 5.15]
When he who was dearer to me than life, the lord of the <s>Aṅgas</s>, has been slain,
I am ashamed even to breathe, father — what talk of consolation! (5.15)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
Verse 5.16

children.text: śocāmi śocyamapi śatruhataṃ na vatsaṃ $ duḥśāsanaṃ tamadhunā na ca bandhuvargam &
children.translated_text: I do not grieve for my son slain by the enemy, though he is pitiable, nor for <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, nor now for the circle of kinsmen;

children.text: yenātiduḥśravamasādhu kṛtaṃ tu karṇe ē̃ kartāsmi tasya nidhanaṃ samare kulasya // 5.16 //
children.translated_text: but the one by whom that most unbearable, wicked deed was done within earshot — I shall bring about the destruction of his clan in battle! (5.16)
Moreover —
[<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, loosen for a moment this outpouring of tears.
[Sanskrit rendering:] Son, restrain for a moment this release of tears.
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, wipe away your tears for just a moment.
Verse 5.17
He who gave up his life for my sake was not restrained by anyone;

children.text: tatkṛte tyajato bāṣpaṃ kiṃ me dīnasya vāryate // 5.17 //
children.translated_text: when I, wretched as I am, shed tears for his sake, why am I being restrained? (5.17)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
Charioteer, by whom was this inconceivable deed done that has brought about the destruction of our family?
Verse 5.18
With his chariot wheel sunk in the ground, by the arrows of the charioteer of the Discus-Wielder (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
the son of <s>Indra</s>'s [friend] (<s>Karṇa</s>), the destroyer of our army, was reportedly slain. (5.18)
[Charioteer:] Long-lived one, this is what people are saying —
Verse 5.19
The ocean of grief, agitated by the memory of <s>Karṇa</s>'s moon-like face,
is being drunk up by my wrath-born fire, as if by the submarine fire (<s>vāḍavāgni</s>). (5.19)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:]
Verse 5.20
This unbearable fire born of grief burns me;

children.text: samānāyāṃ vipattau me varaṃ saṃśayito raṇaḥ // 5.20 //
children.translated_text: in this equal calamity, better for me is a battle of uncertain outcome. (5.20)
Father, mother, be at peace.
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] [Embracing <s>Duryodhana</s> and weeping.]
Verse 5.21

children.text: bhavati tanaya satyaṃ saṃśayaḥ sāhaseṣu $ dravati hṛdayametadbhīmamutprekṣya bhīmam &
children.translated_text: It is true, my son, there is uncertainty in bold ventures; this heart trembles when I imagine <s>Bhīma</s>, the terrible one;

children.text: anikṛtinipuṇaṃ te ceṣṭitaṃ mānaśauṇḍa ē̃ cchalabahulamarīṇāṃ saṃgaraṃ hā hato 'smi // 5.21 //
children.translated_text: O proud one, your conduct is skilled in deception — alas, the battle of enemies is full of treachery — I am undone! (5.21)

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_154}jāda teṇa evva sudasadakadanteṇa viodaleṇa samaṃ samalaṃ maggesi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, you seek battle with that very <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>), the destroyer of a hundred sons!

children.text: SktCh_154: jāta tenaiva sutaśatakṛtāntena vṛkodareṇa samaṃ samaraṃ mārgayase /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Son, you seek battle with that very <s>Vṛkodara</s>, the slayer of a hundred sons!
Verse 5.22

children.text: pāpena yena hṛdayasthamanoratho me $ sarvāṅgacandanaraso nayanāmalenduḥ &
children.translated_text: By what sin was the desire of my heart fulfilled — he who was the sandal-paste for all my limbs, the spotless moon of my eyes,

children.text: putrastavāmba tava tāta nayaikaśiṣyo ē̃ karṇo hataḥ sapadi tatra śarāḥ patantu // 5.22 //
children.translated_text: your son, O mother, your pupil in statesmanship, O father — <s>Karṇa</s> has been slain! May arrows fall upon that [killer] at once! (5.22)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Let <s>Vṛkodara</s> wait for now.

children.text: sūta alamidānīṃ kālātipātena / sajjaṃ me rathamupāhara / bhayaṃ cetpāṇḍavebhyastiṣṭha / gadāmātrasahāya eva samarabhuvamavatarāmi /
children.translated_text: Charioteer, enough now with this delay! Bring my chariot ready. If there is fear of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, wait — I shall descend onto the battlefield with only my mace as companion.
[Charioteer:] Do not think otherwise. I have already arrived. [Exit.]

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa duryodhana yadi sthira evāsmāndagdhumayaṃ te vyavasāyastatsaṃnihiteṣu vīreṣu senāpatiḥ kaścidabhiṣicyatām /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child <s>Duryodhana</s>, if this resolve of yours to burn us is truly firm, then let some commander-in-chief be consecrated from among the heroes present.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Indeed, one has already been consecrated.

children.text:
&gāndhārī&:
{Pkt_155}jāda kadaro uṇa so jahiṃ edaṃ hadāsaṃ olambissaṃ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, who then is he upon whom I, bereft of hope, shall depend?

children.text: SktCh_155: jāta kataraḥ punaḥ sa yatremāṃ hatāśāmavalambiṣye /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Son, who then is he upon whom I, bereft of hope, shall depend?
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Is it <s>Śalya</s>, or <s>Aśvatthāman</s>?
Verse 5.23

children.text: gate bhīṣme hate droṇe karṇe ca vinipātite /
children.translated_text: With <s>Bhīṣma</s> gone, <s>Droṇa</s> slain, and <s>Karṇa</s> brought down,
is there strong hope, O king, that <s>Śalya</s> will conquer the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>? (5.23)
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] Alas, how terrible!
Verse 5.24
Whether the one who would bestow the embrace of <s>Karṇa</s>, or the one who would take <s>Pārtha</s>'s (<s>Arjuna</s>'s) life —
this self of mine, with a torrent of unstoppable tears... (5.24)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Is it then <s>Śalya</s> or <s>Aśvatthāman</s>?
[A commotion is made offstage.]

children.text: bho bhoḥ kauravabalapradhānayodhā alamasmānavalokya bhayāditastato gamanena / kathayantu bhavantaḥ kasminnuddeśe suyodhanastiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: Ho there, chief warriors of the <s>Kaurava</s> army! Stop looking at us and running here and there in fear! Tell us — in what quarter does <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) stand?
[All listen with alarm.]
[Enter, agitated:]
[Charioteer:] Long-lived one — Verse 5.25: Mounted on a single chariot, the two have arrived, asking for you here and there;
[All:] Who and who?
[Charioteer:]
Verse 5.25

children.text: sa karṇāriḥ sa ca krūro vṛkakarmā vṛkodaraḥ // 5.25 //
children.translated_text: That enemy of <s>Karṇa</s>, and that cruel <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>), doer of wolf-like deeds! (5.25)
[<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit, fearfully] Son, what is to be done here?
[Sanskrit rendering:] Son, what is to be done here?
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Is not this mace right here at hand?
[<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Alas, I am slain, ill-fated woman that I am!
[Sanskrit rendering:] Alas, I am slain, ill-fated woman that I am!

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
amba alamidānīṃ kārpaṇyena / saṃjaya rathamāropya pitarau śibiraṃ pratiṣṭhasva / prāpto 'smacchokāpanodapraṇayī janaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Mother, enough now with this wretchedness. <s>Saṃjaya</s>, mount my parents on a chariot and proceed to the camp. The people eager to remove our grief have arrived.
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Child, wait but a single moment while I ascertain the intent of these two.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Father, what use is ascertaining that?
[Then enter <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, mounted on a chariot.]

children.text:
&bhīmaḥ&:
bho bhoḥ suyodhanānujīvinaḥ kimiti saṃbhramādayathāyathaṃ caranti bhavantaḥ / alamāvayoḥ śaṅkayā /

children.translated_text: Verse 5.26

children.text: kartā dyūtacchalānāṃ jatumayaśaraṇoddīpanaḥ so 'timānī $ kṛṣṇākeśottarīyavyapanayanamarutpāṇḍavā yasya dāsāḥ &
children.translated_text: The contriver of the dice-fraud, the arsonist of the house of lac, that supremely arrogant one — [<s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s] (<s>Draupadī</s>'s) hair was the upper garment removed by the wind, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> were whose slaves,

children.text: rājā duḥśāsanādergururanujaśatasyāṅgarājasya mitraṃ ē̃ kvāste duryodhano 'sau kathayata na ruṣā draṣṭumāgatau svaḥ // 5.26 //
children.translated_text: the king, the elder of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and others, lord of a hundred younger brothers, friend of the King of <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>) — where is that <s>Duryodhana</s>? Tell us — we have come not in anger but to see him! (5.26)
[<s>Bhīma</s>:] Ho there, followers of <s>Suyodhana</s>! Why do you act in such disorder, running here and there in alarm? Have no fear of us two.
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] <s>Saṃjaya</s>, cruel indeed is the taunting of this wicked one!

children.text:
&saṃjayaḥ&:
tāta karmaṇā kṛtaniḥśeṣavipriyāḥ saṃprati vācā vyavasyanti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] Father, those who have been completely wronged by deeds now settle the score with words.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Charioteer, go and tell those two: 'He stands here.'

children.text:
&sūtaḥ&:
yadājñāpayati devaḥ* /tāvupasṛtya**
bho vṛkodarārjunau eṣa mahārājastātenāmbayā ca saha nyagrodhacchāyāyāmupaviṣṭastiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: [Charioteer:] As Your Majesty commands. [Approaching them.] O <s>Vṛkodara</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, the great king is seated under the shade of the banyan tree, together with his father and mother.

children.text:
&arjunaḥ&:
ārya prasīda / na yuktaṃ putraśokapīḍitau pitarau punarasmaddarśanenodvejayitum / tadgacchāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Arjuna</s>:] Noble brother, be appeased. It is not right to further agitate our parents, already tormented by the grief of losing their sons, with our appearance. Let us go.

children.text:
&bhīmaḥ&:
mūḍha anullaṅghanīyaḥ sadācāraḥ / na yuktamanabhivādya gurūngantum* /upasṛtya**
saṃjaya pitrornamaskṛtiṃ śrāvaya / atha vā tiṣṭha / svayaṃ viśrāvya nāmakarmaṇī vandanīyā guravaḥ* /iti rathādavatarataḥ**
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhīma</s>:] Fool, proper conduct must not be transgressed. It is not right to depart without saluting one's elders. [Approaching.] <s>Saṃjaya</s>, announce our salutation to our parents. Or rather, wait — having ourselves announced our names and deeds, our elders are to be saluted. [They descend from the chariot.]
Verse 5.27

children.text: sakalaripujayāśā yatra baddhā sutaiste $ tṛṇamiva paribhūto yasya garveṇa lokaḥ &
children.translated_text: He in whom all your hopes for the conquest of enemies were placed, by whose pride the world was treated as straw,

children.text: raṇaśirasi nihantā tasya rādhāsutasya ē̃ praṇamati pitarau vāṃ madhyamaḥ pāṇḍavo 'yam // 5.27 //
children.translated_text: the slayer of that son of <s>Rādhā</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>) on the battlefield — this middle <s>Pāṇḍava</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) bows to you both, his parents. (5.27)
[<s>Arjuna</s>:] [Approaching.] Father! Mother!
Verse 5.28
Having crushed all the <s>Kauravas</s>, intoxicated with the blood of <s>Duḥśāsana</s>,
the breaker of <s>Suyodhana</s>'s thighs — this <s>Bhīma</s> bows his head. (5.28)
[<s>Bhīma</s>:]

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
durātmanvṛkodara na khalvidaṃ bhavataiva kevalaṃ sapatnānāmapakṛtam / yāvatkṣatraṃ tāvatsamaravijayino jitā hatāśca vīrāḥ / tatkimevaṃ vikatthanābhirasmānudvejayasi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] Wicked <s>Vṛkodara</s>, it is not you alone who has injured your enemies. As far as the <s>Kṣatriya</s> race extends, heroes have been conquered and slain in battle for victory. So why do you distress us with such boasting?
Verse 5.29

children.text: kṛṣṭā keśeṣu kṛṣṇā tava sadasi puraḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ nṛpairyaiḥ $ sarve te krodhavahnau kṛtaśalabhakulāvajñayā yena dagdhāḥ &
children.translated_text: When <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>) was dragged by the hair in your assembly before the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> by those kings — all of them were burned in the fire of wrath with the contempt shown to a swarm of moths, by the one through whom [this happened];

children.text: etasmācchrāvaye 'haṃ na khalu bhujabalaślāghayā nāpi darpā- ē̃ tputraiḥ pautraiśca karmaṇyatiguruṇi kṛte tāta sākṣī tvameva // 5.29 //
children.translated_text: therefore I proclaim — not out of boasting of my arm's strength, nor out of arrogance — that when a deed of such extreme gravity has been committed by sons and grandsons, O father, you yourself are the witness! (5.29)
[<s>Bhīma</s>:] Father, enough with this anger.

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
are re maruttanaya kimevaṃ vṛddhasya rājñaḥ purato ninditavyamātmakarma ślāghase / api ca

children.translated_text: Verse 5.30

children.text: kṛṣṭā keśeṣu bhāryā tava tava ca paśostasya rājñaḥ tayorvā $ pratyakṣaṃ bhūpatīnāṃ mama bhuvanapaterājñayā dyūtadāsī &
children.translated_text: Whether the wife was dragged by the hair — yours, or of that beast, or of that king, or of both —

children.text: asminvairānubandhe vada kimapakṛtaṃ tairhatā ye narendrā ē̃ bāhvorvīryātirekadraviṇagurumadaṃ māmajitvaiva darpaḥ // 5.30 //
children.translated_text: in the presence of the rulers, she was a slave by the dice by the command of the lord of the earth. In this chain of enmity, tell me, what wrong was done by those kings who were slain? Without even having conquered me, whose pride is heavy with the wealth of the prowess of my arms, this arrogance! (5.30)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Wretch, son of <s>Marut</s> (<s>Vāyu</s>)! How dare you praise your own deeds as blameworthy before an aged king! And furthermore —

children.text: āḥ durātman / eṣa na bhavasi* /iti sakrodhamutthāya hantumicchati**
children.translated_text: Ha, wretch! You shall not survive this! [Rising angrily, he attempts to strike him.]
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> restrains him and makes him sit down. <s>Bhīma</s> acts out anger.]
Verse 5.31

children.text: apriyāṇi karotyeṣa vācā śakto na karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: He causes offense with words, being powerless in deed;
grieving with a hundred brothers slain, what harm can his lamentations do? (5.31)
[<s>Arjuna</s>:] Noble brother, be calm. What use is anger here?
Verse 5.32

children.text: atraiva kiṃ na viśaseyamahaṃ bhavantaṃ $ duḥśāsanānugamanāya kaṭupralāpin &
children.translated_text: Should I not slaughter you right here, you harsh-tongued one, to send you after <s>Duḥśāsana</s>,

children.text: vighnaṃ gurū na kuruto yadi madgadāgra- ē̃ nirbhidyamānaraṇitāsthani te śarīre // 5.32 //
children.translated_text: if my elders do not create an obstacle — while your body resounds with the cracking of bones split by the tip of my mace? (5.32)
[<s>Bhīma</s>:] You there, disgrace of the <s>Bharata</s> clan —
Verse 5.33

children.text: śokaiḥ strīvannayanasalilaṃ yatparityājito 'si $ bhrāturvakṣaḥsthalavighaṭane yacca sākṣīkṛto 'si &
children.translated_text: That you were abandoned, shedding tears like a woman in grief, and that you were made a witness to the splitting open of your brother's chest —

children.text: āsīdetattava kunṛpateḥ kāraṇaṃ jīvitasya ē̃ kruddhe yuṣmatkulakamalinīkuñjare bhīmasene // 5.33 //
children.translated_text: this was the reason for sparing your life, O wretched king — when <s>Bhīmasena</s>, the elephant among the lotus-pond of your clan, was enraged! (5.33)
And another thing, fool —

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
durātmanbharatakulāpasada dyūtadāsa pāṇḍavapaśo nāhaṃ bhavāniva vikatthanāpragalbhaḥ / kiṃ tu

children.translated_text: Verse 5.34
Before long, your kinsmen shall see you lying asleep on the battlefield,
adorned with the terrible ornament of the braid-like crack in your chest-bone split by my mace! (5.34)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Wretch, lowest of the <s>Bharata</s> clan, slave of the dice, chattel of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> — I am not, like you, bold only in boasting! But —

children.text:
&bhīmaḥ&:
*vihasya**
yadyevaṃ nāśraddheyo bhavān / tathāpi pratyāsannameva kathayāmi /

children.translated_text: Verse 5.35

children.text: pīnābhyāṃ madbhujābhyāṃ bhramitagurugadāghātasaṃcūrṇitoroḥ $ krūrasyādhāya pādaṃ tava śirasi nṛṇāṃ paśyatāṃ śvaḥ prabhāte &
children.translated_text: With the chest crushed by the blow of a heavy mace whirled by my stout arms, placing my foot on the head of your cruel self while men watch, tomorrow at dawn,

children.text: tvanmukhyabhrātṛcakroddalanagaladasṛkcandanenānakhāgraṃ ē̃ styānenārdreṇa cāktaḥ svayamanubhavitā bhūṣaṇaṃ bhīmamasmi // 5.35 //
children.translated_text: smeared with the still-wet sandal-paste of blood flowing from the throat at the crushing of the circle of your foremost brothers — I, <s>Bhīma</s>, shall myself experience that ornament! (5.35)
[<s>Bhīma</s>:] [Laughing.] If so, you are not to be disbelieved. Nevertheless, let me tell you what is near at hand.
[Offstage:]

children.text: bho bho bhīmasenārjunau eṣa khalu nihatāśeṣārāticakra ākrāntaparaśurāmābhirāmayaśāḥ pratāpatāpitadiṅmaṇḍalasthāpitasvajanaḥ śrīmānajātaśatrurdevo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ samājñāpayati /
children.translated_text: Ho, <s>Bhīmasena</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>! He who has destroyed the entire circle of enemies, whose fame rivals that of <s>Paraśurāma</s>'s glory, who has established his kinsmen in the quarters scorched by his valor — the glorious <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, Lord <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, commands thus —
[Both:] What does our noble brother command?
[Again offstage:]
Verse 5.36

children.text: kurvantvāptā hatānāṃ raṇaśirasi janā vahnisāddehabhārā- $ naśrūnmiśraṃ kathaṃciddadatu jalamamī bāndhavā bāndhavebhyaḥ &
children.translated_text: Let trusted men perform the fire-rites for the bodies of the slain on the battlefield; let these kinsmen somehow offer water mixed with tears to their kinsmen;

children.text: mārgantāṃ jñātidehānhatanaragahane khaṇḍitāngṛdhrakaṅkai- ē̃ rastaṃ bhāsvānprayātaḥ saha ripubhirayaṃ saṃhriyantāṃ balāni // 5.36 //
children.translated_text: let them search for the bodies of relatives in the jungle of slain men, with vultures and jackals tearing at the limbs — the sun has set together with the enemies; let the armies be withdrawn! (5.36)
[Both:] As the noble one commands. [Exeunt.]
[Offstage:]
Verse 5.37

children.text: karṇakrodhena yuṣmadvijayi dhanuridaṃ tyaktametānyahāni $ prauḍhaṃ vikrāntamāsīdvana iva bhavatāṃ śūraśūnye raṇe 'smin &
children.translated_text: This bow, victorious over you through <s>Karṇa</s>'s wrath, was set aside these recent days; bold was the valor displayed by you in this battle empty of heroes, as if in a forest;

children.text: sparśaṃ smṛtvottamāṅge pituranavajitanyastaheterupetaḥ ē̃ kalpāgniḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ drupadasutacamūghasmaro drauṇirasmi // 5.37 //
children.translated_text: remembering the touch of my father's hand on my head — he, the unconquered, who laid down his weapon — I have arrived: I am <s>Drauṇi</s> (<s>Aśvatthāman</s>), the fire of the end of the age for the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, the devourer of <s>Drupada</s>'s daughter's army! (5.37)
You there, <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, you whose arms are glorious from drawing the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow — where are you going now?

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
*ākarṇya saharṣam**
vatsa duryodhana droṇavadhaparibhavoddīpitakrodhapāvakaḥ piturapi samadhikabalaḥ śikṣāvānamaropamaścāyamaśvatthāmā prāptaḥ / tatpratyupagamanena tāvadayaṃ saṃbhāvyatāṃ vīraḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] [Hearing this, with joy.] Child <s>Duryodhana</s>, this <s>Aśvatthāman</s> — whose fire of wrath is kindled by the insult of <s>Droṇa</s>'s slaying, who possesses strength surpassing even his father's, who is skilled in arms and equal to the immortals — has arrived! So let this hero be honored by going forth to welcome him.
[<s>Gāndhārī</s>:] [Prakrit] Son, go forth to meet this great-souled one.
[Sanskrit rendering:] Son, go forth to meet this great-souled one.
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Father, mother, what use is this herald of the King of <s>Aṅga</s>'s death, burdened with the useless weight of youth, weapons, and strength?

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa na khalvasminkāle parākramavatāmevaṃvidhānāṃ vāṅmātreṇāpi virāgamutpādayitumarhasi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] My son, at this time you should not produce disaffection, even by words alone, in men of valor such as these.
[Enter]
[<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>:] Victory to the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>!
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] [Rising.] Son of the teacher, come sit here. [He seats him.]
[Verse 5.38]

children.text: karṇena karṇasubhagaṃ bahu yattaduktvā $ yatsaṃgareṣu vihitaṃ viditaṃ tvayā tat &
children.translated_text: Much has been said by <s>Karṇa</s>, pleasing to the ear, and what he accomplished in battles is known to you.

children.text: drauṇistvadhijyadhanurāpatito 'bhyamitra- ē̃ meṣo 'dhunā tyaja nṛpa pratikāracintām // 5.38 //
children.translated_text: But the son of <s>Droṇa</s>, having arrived with bow strung, ready to advance against the enemy — now, O king, abandon your anxiety about countermeasures! (5.38)
[<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>:] King <s>Duryodhana</s> —
[Verse 5.39]
You wish to fight only at the end of the King of <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>)?

children.text: mamāpyantaṃ pratīkṣasva kaḥ karṇaḥ kaḥ suyodhanaḥ // 5.39 //
children.translated_text: Wait for my end too! What is <s>Karṇa</s>? What is <s>Suyodhana</s>? (5.39)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] [With envy.] Son of the teacher —

children.text:
&aśvatthāmā&:
*svagatam**
kathamadyāpi sa eva karṇapakṣapāto 'smāsu ca paribhavaḥ* /prakāśam**
rājankauraveśvara evaṃ bhavatu* /iti niṣkrāntaḥ**
children.translated_text: [<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>:] [Aside.] What! Even now the same partiality toward <s>Karṇa</s> and contempt toward us! [Aloud.] King, lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>, let it be so. [Exit.]

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa ka eṣa te vyāmoho yadasminnapi kāle evaṃvidhasya mahābhāgasyāśvatthāmno vākpāruṣyeṇāparāgamutpādayasi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] My son, what is this delusion of yours that even at this time you provoke the displeasure of such a great and noble man as <s>Aśvatthāmā</s> with harsh words?

children.text:
&duryodhanaḥ&:
kimasyāpriyamanṛtaṃ ca mayoktam / kiṃ vā nedaṃ krodhasthānam / paśya /

children.translated_text: [Verse 5.40]
He disparages to my face my friend the King of <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), whose greatness was unrecognized by bow-bearing <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, who fell in battle through the fault of your destiny.

children.text: parivadati samakṣaṃ mitramaṅgādhirājaṃ ē̃ mama khalu kathayāsminko viśeṣo 'rjune vā // 5.40 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, indeed, what distinction is there between him and <s>Arjuna</s>? (5.40)
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Have I said anything untrue or displeasing to him? Is this not indeed a cause for anger? Look —

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
vatsa tavāpi ko 'tra doṣaḥ / avasānamidānīṃ bharatakulasya / saṃjaya kimidānīṃ karomi mandabhāgyaḥ* /vicintya**
bhavatvevaṃ tāvat / saṃjaya madvacanādbrūhi bhāradvājamaśvatthāmānam /

children.translated_text: [Verse 5.41]

children.text: smarati na bhavānpītaṃ stanyaṃ vibhajya sahāmunā $ mama ca mṛditaṃ kṣaumaṃ bālye tvadaṅgavivartanaiḥ &
children.translated_text: Does he not remember the breast-milk drunk together with this one, and my fine cloth crumpled in childhood by the rolling of your body?

children.text: anujanidhanasphītācchokādatipraṇayācca ya- ē̃ dvacanavikṛtiṣvasya krodho mudhā kriyate tvayā // 5.41 //
children.translated_text: Out of grief at the death of a younger brother and out of excessive affection, his anger at your distortions of speech is in vain. (5.41)

[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] My son, what fault is yours in this? This is the end of the <s>Bharata</s> dynasty. <s>Saṃjaya</s>, what shall I, unfortunate one, do now? [Reflecting.] Very well then, let it be so for now. <s>Saṃjaya</s>, convey my words to <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>, son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s> —
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] As the father commands. [He rises.]
[Verse 5.42]

children.text: yanmocitastava pitā vitathena śastraṃ $ yattādṛśaḥ paribhavaḥ sa tathāvidho 'bhūt &
children.translated_text: Your father was released by a false oath regarding weapons; that such a great insult occurred to one like him —

children.text: etadvicintya balamātmani pauruṣaṃ ca ē̃ duryodhanoktamapahāya vidhāsyasīti // 5.42 //
children.translated_text: reflecting upon this, and upon your own strength and valor, you will disregard what <s>Duryodhana</s> has said and act accordingly. (5.42)
[<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] And you must also say this to him —
[<s>Saṃjaya</s>:] As the father commands. [Exit.]
[<s>Duryodhana</s>:] Charioteer, prepare my war chariot.
[Charioteer:] As His Majesty commands. [Exit.]

children.text:
&dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ&:
gāndhāri ito vayaṃ madrādhipateḥ śalyasya śibirameva gacchāvaḥ / vatsa tvamapyevaṃ kuru /
children.translated_text: [<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:] <s>Gāndhārī</s>, let us go to the camp of <s>Śalya</s>, the king of <s>Madra</s>. My son, you too should do likewise.
[They all walk about and exit.]

children.text:
iti pañcamo 'ṅkaḥ /

ACT_6
ṣaṣṭho 'ṅkaḥ /
*tataḥ praviśatyāsanastho yudhiṣṭhiro draupadī ceṭī puruṣaśca**
children.translated_text:
End of the Fifth Act.

ACT SIX
The Sixth Act.
[Then enter <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, seated, <s>Draupadī</s>, a maidservant, and a man.]
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] [Reflecting and sighing.]
[Verse 6.1]

children.text: tīrṇe bhīṣmamahodadhau kathamapi droṇānale nirvṛte $ karṇāśīviṣabhogini praśamite śalye ca yāte divam &
children.translated_text: The great ocean that was <s>Bhīṣma</s> has somehow been crossed; the fire that was <s>Droṇa</s> has been extinguished; the serpent-hood that was <s>Karṇa</s> has been pacified; <s>Śalya</s> too has gone to heaven.

children.text: bhīmena priyasāhasena rabhasātsvalpāvaśeṣe jaye ē̃ sarve jīvitasaṃśayaṃ vayamamī vācā samāropitāḥ // 6.1 //
children.translated_text: Now, with <s>Bhīma</s>, fond of daring exploits, impetuously pursuing what little remains of victory, we are all thrown into doubt regarding our lives by mere words. (6.1)

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_159}*sabāṣpam**
mahārāa pañcālie tti kiṃ ṇa bhaṇidaṃ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit, with tears.] Great king, has the name <s>Pāñcālī</s> not been spoken?

children.text: SktCh_159: mahārāja pāñcālyeti kiṃ na bhaṇitam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Great king, has the name <s>Pāñcālī</s> not been spoken?
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, indeed by me — [Looking at the man.] Fellow!
[Man:] My lord, command me.

children.text:
&yadhiṣṭhiraḥ&:
ucyatāṃ sahadevaḥ / kruddhasya vṛkodarasyāparyuṣitadāruṇāṃ pratijñāmupalabhya pranaṣṭasya māninaḥ kauravarājasya padavīmanveṣṭumatinipuṇamatayasteṣu teṣu sthāneṣu paramārthābhijñāścarāḥ susacivāśca bhaktimantaḥ paṭupaṭaharavavyaktaghoṣaṇāḥ suyodhanasaṃcāravedinaḥ pratiśrutadhanapūjāpratyupakriyāścarantu samantātsamantapañcakam / api ca

children.translated_text: [Verse 6.2]

children.text: paṅke vā saikate vā sunibhṛtapadavīvedino yāntu dāśāḥ $ kuñjeṣu kṣuṇṇavīrunnicayaparicayā ballavāḥ saṃcarantu &
children.translated_text: Let fishermen, expert in tracking footprints on mud or sand, go forth; let cowherds, familiar with heaps of trampled undergrowth in thickets, range about;

children.text: vyādhā vyāghrāṭavīṣu svaparapadavido ye ca randhreṣvabhijñā ē̃ ye siddhavyañjanā vā pratimuninilayaṃ te ca cārāścarantu // 6.2 //
children.translated_text: let hunters who know their own and others' tracks in tiger-infested forests, and those skilled in detecting secret places, and those adept at reading signs — let them all range as spies around every hermitage. (6.2)

[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Tell <s>Sahadeva</s>: having learned the terrible, fresh vow of the enraged <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>), to track down the proud <s>Kaurava</s> king who has vanished — let scouts of exceedingly sharp intelligence, knowing the true state of affairs, well-advised, devoted, making themselves known by clear proclamation with the rapid beating of drums, and knowing the movements of <s>Suyodhana</s>, range throughout <s>Samantapañcaka</s> in all directions. Moreover —
[Man:] As the lord commands.
[Verse 6.3]

children.text: jñeyā rahaḥ śaṅkitamālapantaḥ $ suptā rugārtā madirāvidheyāḥ &
children.translated_text: He should be recognized where, in secret, there are people moving fearfully in rows; people sleeping, people afflicted with disease, people under the influence of wine;

children.text: trāso mṛgāṇāṃ vayasāṃ virāvo ē̃ nṛpāṅkapādapratimāśca yatra // 6.3 //
children.translated_text: alarm among deer, cries of birds, and impressions resembling the footprints and marks of a king. (6.3)
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Wait. And <s>Sahadeva</s> should also be told this —

children.text:
&puruṣaḥ&:
yadājñāpayati devaḥ* /iti niṣkramya punaḥ praviśya saharṣam**
deva pāñcālakaḥ prāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Man:] As the lord commands. [He goes out and enters again, joyfully.] My lord, the <s>Pāñcālaka</s> (a man from <s>Pāñcāla</s>) has arrived!
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Bring him in quickly.

children.text:
&puruṣaḥ&:
*niṣkramya pāñcālakena saha praviśya**
eṣa devaḥ / upasarpatu pāñcālakaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Man:] [Going out and entering with the <s>Pāñcālaka</s>.] Here is the lord. Let the <s>Pāñcālaka</s> approach.

children.text:
&pāñcālakaḥ&:
jayatu jayatu devaḥ / priyamāvedayāmi mahārājāya devyai ca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] Victory, victory to the lord! I bring good news to the great king and the queen!

children.text:
&yudhiṣṭhiraḥ&:
bhadra pāñcālaka kaccidāsāditā tasya durātmanaḥ kauravādhamasya padavī /
children.translated_text: [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Good <s>Pāñcālaka</s>, has the trail of that wicked wretch, the vilest of the <s>Kauravas</s>, been found?

children.text:
&pāñcālakaḥ&:
deva na kevalaṃ padavī / sa eva durātmā devīkeśāmbarākarṣaṇamahāpātakapradhānaheturupalabdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] My lord, not merely the trail! That very villain himself, the chief cause of the great sin of dragging the queen's hair and garment, has been found!

children.text:
&yudhiṣṭhiraḥ&:
sādhu / bhadra priyamāveditam / atha darśanagocaraṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Excellent! Good man, welcome news has been reported. And has he come within sight?
[<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] My lord, you should rather ask: has he come within range of battle?
[<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit, with fear.] How? He is within range of battle? My lord, that is —

children.text: SktCh_160: kathaṃ samaragocaro vartate me nāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] How? He is within range of battle? My lord, that is —
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] [With apprehension.] Indeed, my young brother is within range of battle.
[<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] Indeed. What else would be reported to the great king?
[Verse 6.4]

children.text: trastaṃ vināpi vaṣayāduruvikramasya $ ceto vivekaparimantharatāṃ prayāti &
children.translated_text: Even without cause, the heart trembles at the great valor of that one, and the mind reaches a state of anxious deliberation.

children.text: jānāmi codyatagadasya vṛkodarasya ē̃ sāraṃ raṇeṣu bhujayoḥ pariśaṅkitaśca // 6.4 //
children.translated_text: I know the power of the arms of <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) with his upraised mace in battles, and yet I am anxious. (6.4)
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:]
[Verse 6.5]

children.text: gurūṇāṃ bandhūnāṃ kṣitipatisahasrasya ca puraḥ $ purābhūdasmākaṃ nṛpasadasi yo 'yaṃ paribhavaḥ &
children.translated_text: That humiliation which was ours before, in the assembly of kings, in the presence of elders, kinsmen, and thousands of rulers —

children.text: priye prāyastasya dvitayamapi pāraṃ gamayati ē̃ kṣayaḥ prāṇānāṃ naḥ kurupatipaśorvādya nidhanam // 6.5 //
children.translated_text: O beloved, perhaps both ends of that affair will be brought to completion today: either the death of the <s>Kaurava</s> beast or the loss of our lives. (6.5)
[Looking at <s>Draupadī</s>.] O noble <s>Kṣatriya</s> lady —
[Verse 6.6]
Surely today, by that hero who fears the breaking of his vow,
your braid of hair is being bound — and he is capable of dragging it! (6.6)
Or rather, enough of doubt —

children.text: pāñcālaka kathaya kathaya kathamupalabdhaḥ sa durātmā kasminnuddeśe kiṃ vādhunā pravṛttamiti /
children.translated_text: <s>Pāñcālaka</s>, tell me, tell me! How was that villain found? In what place? And what is happening now?
[<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit.] Good man, tell, tell!
[Sanskrit rendering:] Good man, tell, tell!

children.text:
&pāñcālakaḥ&:
śṛṇotu devo devī ca / astīha devena hate madrādhipatau śalye gāndhārarājakulaśalabhe sahadevaśastrānalaṃ praviṣṭe senāpatinidhananirākrandaviralayodhojjhitāsu samarabhūmiṣu ripubalaparājayoddhatavalgitavicitraparākramāsāditavimukhārāticakrāsu dhṛṣṭadyumnādhiṣṭhitāsu ca yuṣmatsenāsu pranaṣṭeṣu kṛpakṛtavarmāśvatthāmasu tathā dāruṇāmaparyuṣitāṃ pratijñāmupalabhya kumāravṛkodarasya na jñāyate kvāpi pralīnaḥ sa durātmā kauravādhamaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] Let the lord and the queen hear! When <s>Śalya</s>, king of <s>Madra</s>, was slain here by the lord, and the king of <s>Gāndhāra</s>, that moth to the flame of the <s>Kaurava</s> dynasty, had entered the fire of <s>Sahadeva's</s> weapons, and on the battlefields abandoned by warriors now scattered after the lament over the commander's death, and with the enemy forces routed and their retreating army scattered by the splendid and varied valor of your victorious forces, and with your armies under <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna's</s> command, and with <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Kṛtavarman</s>, and <s>Aśvatthāmā</s> having vanished, and hearing the terrible, fresh vow of prince <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>), that wicked wretch, the vilest of the <s>Kauravas</s>, was not to be found anywhere — he had disappeared.
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] And then? And then?
[<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit.] Sir, go on, tell more!
[Sanskrit rendering:] Sir, go on, tell more!

children.text:
&pāñcālakaḥ&:
avadhattāṃ devo devī ca / tataśca bhagavatā vāsudevenādhiṣṭhitamekarathamārūḍhau kumārabhīmārjunau samantātsamantapañcakaṃ paryaṭitumārabdhau tamanāsāditavantau ca / anantaraṃ daivamanuśocati mādṛśe bhṛtyavarge dīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca niśvasati kumāre bībhatsau jaladharasamayaniśāsaṃcāritataḍitprakarapiṅgalaiḥ kaṭākṣairādīpayati gadāṃ vṛkodare yatkiṃcanakāritāmadhikṣipati vidherbhagavati nārāyaṇe kaścitsaṃviditaḥ kumārasya māruterujjhitamāṃsabhāraḥ pratyagraviśasitamṛgalohitacaraṇanivasanastvaramāṇo 'ntikamupetya puruṣaḥ paruṣaśvāsagrastārdhaśrutavarṇānumeyapadayā vācā kathitavān / kumāra asminmahato 'sya sarasastīre dve padapaddhatī samavatīrṇapratibimbe / tayorekā sthalamuttīrṇā na dvitīyā / paratra kumāraḥ pramāṇamiti / tataḥ sasaṃbhramaṃ prasthitāḥ sarve vayaṃ tameva puraskṛtya / gatvā ca sarastīraṃ parijñāyamānasuyodhanapadalāñchanāṃ padavīmāsādya bhagavatā vāsudevenoktam / bho vīra vṛkodara jānāti kila suyodhanaḥ salilastambhanīṃ vidyām / tannūnaṃ tena tvadbhayātsarasīmenāmadhiśayitena bhavitavyam / etacca vacanamupaśrutya rāmānujasya sakaladiṅnikuñjapūritātiriktamudbhrāntasalilacaraśakuntakulaṃ trāsoddhatanakragrāhamāloḍya saraḥsalilaṃ bhairavaṃ ca garjitvā kumāravṛkodareṇābhihitam / are re vṛthāprakhyāpitālīkapauruṣābhimāninpāñcālarājatanayākeśāmbarākarṣaṇamahāpātakindhārtarāṣṭrāpasada

children.translated_text: [Verse 6.7]

children.text: janmendoramale kule vyapadiśasyadyāpi dhatse gadāṃ $ māṃ duḥśāsanakoṣṇaśoṇitamadhukṣībaṃ ripuṃ manyase &
children.translated_text: You claim birth in the stainless lunar dynasty and still bear the mace — do you think me, your enemy, drunk on the warm blood of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> as on wine, to be an easy foe?

children.text: darpāndho madhukaiṭabhadviṣi harāvapyuddhataṃ ceṣṭase ē̃ trāsānme nṛpaśo vihāya samaraṃ paṅke 'dhunā līyase // 6.7 //
children.translated_text: Blinded by arrogance, you acted insolently even toward <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> — and now, O royal beast, abandoning the battle out of fear of me, you hide in the mud! (6.7)

[<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] Let the lord and queen attend! Then, the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) took command, and princes <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, mounting a single chariot, began to search <s>Samantapañcaka</s> on all sides, but did not find him. Then, as fate laments over servants such as myself, as he sighs long and hot, as he sets prince <s>Arjuna</s> ablaze with sidelong glances tawny like streaks of lightning moving through a monsoon night, as he incites the mace of <s>Vṛkodara</s>, as he reproaches fate, as the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) feels the moment — a certain man, informed about the prince <s>Māruti</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>), his body stripped of flesh, his feet and garments smeared with the fresh blood of recently slaughtered deer, came hurrying and, with words whose half-heard syllables were swallowed by his harsh breathing and whose meaning could only be inferred, said: 'Prince, on the shore of this great lake there are two lines of footprints descending into the reflected [surface]. One of them ascends to dry land — but not the second. Beyond that, the prince himself is the judge.' Thereupon, we all set forth in haste, following that very man. And arriving at the lakeshore, having found the trail bearing the recognizable footmarks of <s>Suyodhana</s>, the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> said: 'O brave <s>Vṛkodara</s>, <s>Suyodhana</s> knows the art of solidifying water (<s>salilastambhanī vidyā</s>). He must certainly have taken refuge in this lake out of fear of you.' And hearing these words of the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), which filled every corner of the sky beyond measure, startling the flocks of aquatic birds, churning the lake water with its crocodiles and sharks agitated by fear, and roaring fearfully, prince <s>Vṛkodara</s> declared: 'Ho, ho! You whose falsely proclaimed boast of valor is hollow! You sinner, who dragged the hair and garment of the daughter of the <s>Pāñcāla</s> king — you wretch, disgrace of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra's</s> line —
[Verse 6.8]

children.text: pāñcālyā manyuvahniḥ sphuṭamupaśamitaprāya eva prasahya $ vyāsaktaiḥ keśapāśairhatapatiṣu mayā kauravāntaḥpureṣu &
children.translated_text: The fire of <s>Pāñcālī's</s> wrath has been virtually extinguished by force — by means of hair-braids fastened by me in the slain inner chambers of the <s>Kauravas</s>;

children.text: bhrāturduḥśāsanasya sravadasṛgurasaḥ pīyamānaṃ nirīkṣya ē̃ krodhātkiṃ bhīmasene vihitamasamaye yattvayāsto 'bhimānaḥ // 6.8 //
children.translated_text: seeing the thick, flowing blood of your brother <s>Duḥśāsana</s> being drunk — what was that arrogance you placed in <s>Bhīmasena</s> at an inopportune time, out of anger? (6.8)'
Moreover, O you who are blind with pride —

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_163}ṇāha abaṇīdo me maṇṇū jai puṇo bi sulahaṃ daṃsaṇaṃ bhavissadi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] [Prakrit.] My lord, my anger has been removed, if seeing him will indeed be easily obtained again.

children.text: SktCh_163: nātha apanīto me manyuryadi punarapi sulabhaṃ darśanaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] My lord, my anger has been removed, if indeed seeing him will be easily obtained again.
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, you should not utter inauspicious words at this time. Good man, and then? And then?

children.text:
&pāñcālakaḥ&:
tataścaivaṃ bhāṣamāṇena vṛkodareṇāvatīrya krodhoddhatabhramitabhīṣaṇagadāpāṇinā sahasaivollaṅghitatīramutsannanalinīvanamapaviddhamūrcchitagrāhamudbhrāntamatsyaśakuntamatibhairavāravabhramitavārisaṃcayamāyatamapi tatsaraḥ samantādāloḍitam /
children.translated_text: [<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] Then, <s>Vṛkodara</s>, speaking thus, descended — and with mace fearfully whirled in his rage-upraised hand, at once leaping across the shore, uprooting the lotus groves, casting aside the stunned crocodiles, scattering the fish and birds in alarm, churning the water mass with a most terrifying roar — though the lake was vast, he churned it from all sides!
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Good man, even so, did he not rise up?
VERSE 6.9

children.text: tyaktvotthitaḥ sarabhasaṃ sarasaḥ sa mūla- $ mudbhūtakopadahanograviṣasphuliṅgaḥ &
children.translated_text: Having impetuously risen, abandoning the lake from its very depths, with sparks of fierce poison-fire born of surging rage,
with the slow swinging of his arms terrible as <s>Bhīma</s>'s — like <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (the deadly poison) from the thoroughly churned ocean of milk. // 6.9 //
[<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] My lord, why did he not rise?
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Well done, O noble warrior, well done!
[<s>Draupadī</s>:] (Prakrit 164) Has he accepted the challenge to battle or not?
[Sanskrit rendering 164:] Has he accepted the challenge to battle or not?

children.text:
&pāñcālakaḥ&:
utthāya ca tasmātsalilāśayātkarayugalottambhitatoraṇīkṛtabhīmagadaḥ kathayati sma / are re mārute kiṃ bhayena pralīnaṃ duryodhanaṃ manyate bhavān / mūḍha anihatapāṇḍuputraḥ prakāśaṃ lajjamāno viśramitumadhyavasitavānasmi pātālam / evaṃ cokte vāsudevakirīṭibhyāṃ dvāvapyantaḥsalilaṃ niṣiddhasamarasamārambhau sthalamuttāritau bhīmasuyodhanau / āsīnaśca kauravarājaḥ kṣititale gadāṃ nikṣipya viśīrṇarathasahasraṃ nihatakuruśatagajavājinarasahasrakalevarasaṃmardasaṃpatadgṛdhrakaṅkajambūkamutsannasuyodhamasmadvīramuktasiṃhanādamapamitrabāndhavamakauravaṃ raṇasthānamavalokyāyatamuṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasitavān / tataśca vṛkodareṇābhihitam / ayi bhoḥ kauravarāja kṛtaṃ bandhunāśadarśanamanyunā / maivaṃ viṣādaṃ kṛthāḥ paryāptāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ samarāyāhamasahāya iti /

children.translated_text: VERSE 6.10
'Whom among the five of us you consider the best fighter (<s>suyodha</s>), O <s>Suyodhana</s>,
with him, when he is armored and has taken up his weapon, let your battle-festival be!' // 6.10 //

[<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] And having risen from that lake, with the <s>Bhīma</s>'s mace held aloft in both hands forming an arch, he declared: 'Ho there, son of the Wind! Does my lord think that <s>Duryodhana</s> has hidden out of fear? Fool! With the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> unslain, I was ashamed to appear openly and had resolved to rest in the netherworld.' When this was said, <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) brought both <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Suyodhana</s> — who had been prevented from beginning combat within the water — out onto dry land. And the <s>Kaurava</s> king, seated on the ground, having set down his mace, surveying the battlefield — strewn with the wreckage of thousands of chariots, with the corpses of hundreds of slain <s>Kuru</s> elephants, horses, and men in their thousands, thronged with vultures, herons, and jackals descending upon the carnage, resounding with the lion-roars of our heroes, bereft of friends, bereft of <s>Kauravas</s> — he let out a long, hot sigh. Then <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) said: 'Ho, King of the <s>Kauravas</s>! Enough of this sight of kinsmen's destruction, enough of anger! The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are sufficient for battle — I alone, without allies, say this.'
VERSE 6.11
'After the slaying of <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, you two are equal to me;
though disliked [by me], you alone are the beloved one to fight with, O lover of daring deeds!' // 6.11 //
Having heard this, the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, casting a glance free of malice upon the two princes, said:

children.text: ityutthāya parasparakrodhādhikṣepaparuṣavākkalahaprastāvitaghorasaṃgrāmau vicitravibhramabhramitagadāparibhāsurabhujadaṇḍau maṇḍalairvicaritumārabdhau bhīmaduryodhanau / ahaṃ ca devena cakrapāṇinā devasakāśamanupreṣitaḥ / āha ca devo devakīnandanaḥ / aparyuṣitapratijñe ca mārutau pranaṣṭe kauravarāje mahānāsīnno viṣādaḥ / saṃprati punarbhīmasenenāsādite suyodhane niṣkaṇṭakībhūtaṃ bhuvanatalaṃ parikalayatu bhavān / abhyudayocitāścānavarataṃ pravartyantāṃ maṅgalasamārambhāḥ / kṛtaṃ saṃdehena /

children.translated_text: VERSE 6.12

children.text: pūryantāṃ salilena ratnakalaśā rājyābhiṣekāya te $ kṛṣṇātyantacirojjhite ca kabarībandhe karotu kṣaṇam &
children.translated_text: 'Let the jeweled pitchers be filled with water for your royal consecration; and upon the braid-knot of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>), so long abandoned, let [it] make a moment [of adornment];

children.text: rāme śātakuṭhārabhāsurakare kṣatradrumocchedini ē̃ krodhāndhe ca vṛkodare paripatatyājau kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ // 6.12 //
children.translated_text: when <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) with his axe-bright hand was the uprooter of the warrior-tree, and when <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>), blind with rage, falls upon [the enemy] in battle — where is there room for doubt?' // 6.12 //

Thus, having risen, <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s>, whose terrible battle was commenced through a quarrel of harsh words of mutual anger and reproach, whose arm-staffs were resplendent with maces whirled in various graceful rotations, began to move in circles. And I was sent by the lord <s>Cakrapāṇi</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Discus-Bearer) to the lord's [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s] presence. And the lord, son of <s>Devakī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), said: 'When the son of the Wind had not yet fulfilled his vow and the <s>Kaurava</s> king had vanished, our grief was great. Now that <s>Suyodhana</s> has been confronted by <s>Bhīmasena</s>, let your lordship consider the surface of the earth to be freed of thorns. And let auspicious ceremonies befitting prosperity be performed without interruption. Away with doubt!'

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_165}*sabāṣpam**
jaṃ devo tihuaṇaṇāho bhaṇādi taṃ kahaṃ aṇṇahā bhavissadi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] (Prakrit 165) (with tears) Whatever the lord, the master of the three worlds, says — how can it be otherwise?
[Sanskrit rendering 165:] Whatever the lord, the master of the three worlds, says — how can it be otherwise?
[<s>Pāñcālaka</s>:] This is not merely a blessing — it is also the command of the Slayer of Demons (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>).

children.text:
&yudhiṣṭhiraḥ&:
ko hi nāma bhagavatā saṃdiṣṭaṃ vikalpayati / kaḥ ko 'tra bhoḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Who indeed would question what the Blessed Lord has ordained? Who is there? Ho!
(enters)
[<s>Kañcukī</s> (Chamberlain):] Let the lord command!

children.text:
&yudhiṣṭhiraḥ&:
devasya devakīnandanasya bahumānādvatsasya me vijayamaṅgalāya pravartyantāṃ taducitāḥ samārambhāḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Out of reverence for the lord, son of <s>Devakī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), let the ceremonies befitting my dear [brother's] victory-celebration be commenced!

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
yadājñāpayati devaḥ* /sotsāhaṃ parikramya**
bho bhoḥ saṃvidhātḥṇāṃ puraḥsarā yathāpradhānamantarveśmikā dauvārikāśca eṣa khalu bhujabalaparikṣepottīrṇakauravaparibhavasāgarasya nirvyūḍhadurvahapratijñābhārasya suyodhanānujaśatonmūlanaprabhañjanasya duḥśāsanoraḥsthalavidalananārasiṃhasya duryodhanorustambhabhaṅgaviniścitavijayasya balinaḥ prābhañjanervṛkodarasya snehapakṣapātinā manasā maṅgalāni kartumājñāpayati devo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ* /ākāśe**
kiṃ brūtha / sarvato 'dhikataramapi pravṛttaṃ kiṃ nālokayasīti / sādhu putrakāḥ sādhu / anuktahitakāritā hi prakāśayati manogatāṃ svāmibhaktim /
children.translated_text: [<s>Kañcukī</s>:] As the lord commands! (walking about with enthusiasm) Ho there! You superintendents, chief attendants, inner-chamber servants, and doorkeepers, each according to rank — this indeed is the command of the lord <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, with affectionate partiality of heart, to perform auspicious rites for the mighty son of <s>Prābhañjana</s> (the Wind God), <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) — he who has crossed the ocean of <s>Kaurava</s> insult by the strength of his arms, who has borne the unbearable weight of his vows, who was a tempest uprooting hundreds of <s>Suyodhana</s>'s brothers, who was a Man-Lion (<s>Narasiṃha</s>) in splitting open the chest of <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, and who is resolved upon victory through breaking the thigh-pillar of <s>Duryodhana</s>! (looking up to the sky) What do you say? Is even more than usual already under way, and I have not noticed? Well done, my sons, well done! For acting rightly without being told reveals the devotion to one's master that dwells in the heart.
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Noble <s>Jayaṃdhara</s>!
[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] Let the lord command!
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Go, reward the <s>Pāñcālaka</s>, the bearer of glad tidings, with a gift of gratification.
[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] As the lord commands! (exits with <s>Pāñcālaka</s>)

children.text:
&draupadī&:
{Pkt_166}mahārāa kiṃṇimittaṃ uṇa ṇāhabhīmaseṇeṇa so durāāro bhaṇido / pañcāṇaṃ bi amhāṇaṃ majjhe jeṇa de roadi teṇa saha de saṃgāmo hodu tti / jai maddīsudāṇaṃ ekadareṇa saha saṃgāmo teṇa patthido bhave tado accāhidaṃ bhave /
children.translated_text: [<s>Draupadī</s>:] (Prakrit 166) Great King, for what reason did my lord <s>Bhīmasena</s> say to that wicked one: 'Among the five of us, with whomever you desire, let your battle be with him'? If the battle had been sought with one of <s>Mādrī</s>'s sons, then it would have been a great calamity.

children.text: SktCh_166: mahārāja kiṃnimittaṃ punarnāthabhīmasenena sa durācāro bhaṇitaḥ / pañcānāmapyasmākaṃ madhye yena te rocate tena saha te saṃgrāmo bhavatviti / yadi mādrīsutayorekatareṇa saha saṃgrāmastena prārthito bhavettato 'tyāhitaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering 166:] Great King, for what reason did my lord <s>Bhīmasena</s> say to that wicked one: 'Among the five of us, with whomever you desire, let your battle be with him'? If the battle had been sought with one of <s>Mādrī</s>'s two sons, then it would have been a great calamity.

children.text:
&yudhiṣṭhiraḥ&:
kṛṣṇe evaṃ manyate jarāsaṃdhaghātī / hatasakalasuhṛdbandhuvīrānujarājanyāsu kṛpakṛtavarmāśvatthāmaśeṣāsvekādaśasvakṣauhiṇīṣvabāndhavaḥ śarīramātravibhavaḥ kadācidutsṛṣṭanijābhimāno dhārtarāṣṭraḥ parityajedāyudhaṃ tapovanaṃ vā vrajetsaṃdhiṃ vā pitṛmukhena yāceta / evaṃ sati sudūramatikrāntaḥ pratijñābhāro bhavetsakalaripujayasyeti / samaraṃ pratipattuṃ pañcānāmapi pāṇḍavānāmekasyāpi naiva kṣamaḥ suyodhanaḥ / śaṅke cāhaṃ gadāyuddhaṃ vṛkodarasyaivānena / ayi sukṣatriye paśya /

children.translated_text: VERSE 6.13

children.text: krodhodgūrṇagadasya nāsti sadṛśaḥ satyaṃ raṇe māruteḥ $ kauravye kṛtahastatā punariyaṃ deve yathā sīriṇi &
children.translated_text: 'Truly, there is no equal in battle to the son of <s>Māruta</s> (the Wind God) when his mace whirls in fury; yet this skill of hand that the <s>Kaurava</s> has is as if the lord <s>Sīrin</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>, the Plough-wielder) [himself were present].

children.text: svastyastūddhatadhārtarāṣṭranalinīnāgāya vatsāya me ē̃ śaṅke tasya suyodhanena samaraṃ naivetareṣāmaham // 6.13 //
children.translated_text: May all be well for my dear one, the serpent in the lotus-pond of the haughty son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>! I suspect his battle is with <s>Suyodhana</s> alone, not with the others.' // 6.13 //

[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, thus thinks the slayer of <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>): 'With all his friends, kinsmen, heroes, brothers, and kings slain, with only <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Kṛtavarman</s>, and <s>Aśvatthāman</s> remaining from eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s>, bereft of allies, possessing nothing but his body, <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) might perhaps abandon his self-regard, lay down his weapons, retire to the forest of asceticism, or sue for peace through his father as intermediary. In that case, the burden of the vow regarding the conquest of all enemies would have passed far beyond [fulfillment].' <s>Suyodhana</s> is not capable of facing even one of the five <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> in battle. And I suspect it will be a mace-fight with <s>Vṛkodara</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) alone. O noble lady, behold!
(offstage)
'I am thirsty! I am thirsty! Let someone honor me with the gift of water and shade!'
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] (listening) Who is there? Ho!
(enters)
[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] Let the lord command!
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Find out what this is.

children.text:
&kañcukī&:
yadājñāpayati devaḥ* /iti niṣkramya punaḥ praviśya**
deva kṣunmānatithirupasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Kañcukī</s>:] As the lord commands! (exits, then re-enters) My lord, a guest suffering from hunger has arrived.
[<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:] Bring him in quickly.
[<s>Kañcukī</s>:] As the lord commands! (exits)
